        count("*").alias("order_count")
    )
    print(f"Step 4 - After aggregation: {aggregated.rdd.getNumPartitions()} partitions")
    
    # Final coalesce for output
    final = aggregated.coalesce(5)
    print(f"Step 5 - Final output: {final.rdd.getNumPartitions()} partitions")
    
    print("\nBenefit: Reduced shuffle overhead and optimized file output")
    
    # Use Case 2: Large-scale Join Optimization
    print("\n2. Large-scale Join Optimization:")
    print("""
    Scenario: Joining sales data with customer data
    
    Challenge: 100M sales records + 10M customer records
    """)
    
    # Simulate large datasets
    sales = df.withColumn("customer_id", (rand() * 1000).cast("int"))
    customers = df.select("order_id").withColumnRenamed("order_id", "customer_id").distinct()
    
    print("Without optimization:")
    print("  - Both datasets shuffled")
    print("  - High memory usage")
    
    # Optimization: Repartition both on join key
    sales_partitioned = sales.repartition(50, "customer_id")
    customers_partitioned = customers.repartition(50, "customer_id")
    
    optimized_join = sales_partitioned.join(
        customers_partitioned,
        "customer
```python
        customers_partitioned,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    )
    
    print("\nWith optimization:")
    print("  - Pre-partitioned on join key")
    print("  - Co-located data reduces shuffle")
    print("  - Broadcast not needed for large tables")
    
    # Use Case 3: Time-series Data Processing
    print("\n3. Time-series Data Processing:")
    print("""
    Scenario: Processing IoT sensor data by time windows
    
    Data: Millions of events per day, queries by time ranges
    """)
    
    # Add timestamp
    ts_df = df.withColumn(
        "timestamp",
        to_timestamp(col("order_date"))
    ).withColumn(
        "hour",
        hour(col("timestamp"))
    )
    
    # Range partition by timestamp for efficient time queries
    time_partitioned = ts_df.repartitionByRange(24, "timestamp")
    
    print("Strategy: Range partitioning by timestamp")
    print(f"Partitions: {time_partitioned.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Show time ranges per partition
    time_ranges = time_partitioned.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
        .groupBy("partition_id") \
        .agg(
            min("timestamp").alias("start_time"),
            max("timestamp").alias("end_time"),
            count("*").alias("events")
        ) \
        .orderBy("partition_id")
    
    print("\nTime ranges per partition:")
    time_ranges.show(10)
    
    print("\nBenefit: Time-range queries only scan relevant partitions")
    
    # Use Case 4: Handling Data Skew in Production
    print("\n4. Handling Data Skew in Production:")
    print("""
    Scenario: E-commerce platform with popular products
    
    Problem: Top 10% of products account for 80% of orders
    """)
    
    # Identify skewed products
    product_counts = df.groupBy("product").count()
    total_records = df.count()
    
    skewed_products = product_counts.filter(
        col("count") > total_records * 0.05  # More than 5% of total
    ).select("product").rdd.flatMap(lambda x: x).collect()
    
    print(f"Skewed products identified: {skewed_products}")
    
    # Apply salting to skewed products
    salted_df = df.withColumn(
        "partition_key",
        when(
            col("product").isin(skewed_products),
            concat(col("product"), lit("_"), (rand() * 10).cast("int"))
        ).otherwise(col("product"))
    )
    
    # Repartition with salted keys
    skew_handled = salted_df.repartition(20, "partition_key")
    
    print("\nPartition distribution after salting:")
    skew_handled.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
        .groupBy("partition_id") \
        .count() \
        .agg(
            avg("count").alias("avg_records"),
            stddev("count").alias("stddev_records")
        ).show()
    
    print("Benefit: Even distribution despite skewed data")
    
    # Use Case 5: Multi-stage Aggregation Pipeline
    print("\n5. Multi-stage Aggregation Pipeline:")
    print("""
    Scenario: Complex analytics with multiple aggregation levels
    
    Pipeline:
    1. Country-level aggregation
    2. Category-level aggregation
    3. Final global aggregation
    """)
    
    # Stage 1: Partition by country
    stage1 = df.repartition(10, "country")
    country_agg = stage1.groupBy("country", "category").agg(
        sum("amount").alias("country_category_total"),
        count("*").alias("country_category_count")
    )
    
    print(f"Stage 1 - Country aggregation: {country_agg.rdd.getNumPartitions()} partitions")
    
    # Stage 2: Coalesce after aggregation (data reduced)
    stage2 = country_agg.coalesce(5)
    category_agg = stage2.groupBy("category").agg(
        sum("country_category_total").alias("category_total"),
        sum("country_category_count").alias("category_count")
    )
    
    print(f"Stage 2 - Category aggregation: {category_agg.rdd.getNumPartitions()} partitions")
    
    # Stage 3: Final aggregation
    final_agg = category_agg.agg(
        sum("category_total").alias("grand_total"),
        sum("category_count").alias("total_orders")
    )
    
    print("\nFinal results:")
    final_agg.show()
    
    print("Strategy: Repartition -> Aggregate -> Coalesce -> Aggregate")
    
    # Use Case 6: Incremental Data Processing
    print("\n6. Incremental Data Processing:")
    print("""
    Scenario: Daily incremental updates to data warehouse
    
    Challenge: Efficiently merge new data with existing partitions
    """)
    
    # Simulate existing data and new data
    existing_data = df.filter(col("order_date") < "2024-01-20")
    new_data = df.filter(col("order_date") >= "2024-01-20")
    
    print(f"Existing data: {existing_data.count()} records")
    print(f"New data: {new_data.count()} records")
    
    # Partition new data to match existing structure
    new_data_partitioned = new_data.repartition(
        existing_data.rdd.getNumPartitions(),
        "country",
        "category"
    )
    
    print(f"\nNew data partitioned to: {new_data_partitioned.rdd.getNumPartitions()} partitions")
    print("Matches existing partition structure for efficient merge")
    
    # Union and deduplicate
    merged = existing_data.union(new_data_partitioned).dropDuplicates(["order_id"])
    
    print(f"Merged data: {merged.count()} records")
    
    # Use Case 7: Data Export Optimization
    print("\n7. Data Export Optimization:")
    print("""
    Scenario: Export processed data to external systems
    
    Requirements:
    - Fixed number of output files
    - Balanced file sizes
    - Sorted within files
    """)
    
    # Prepare for export
    export_data = df.repartitionByRange(5, "country", "order_date")
    
    print(f"Export partitions: {export_data.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Analyze export file sizes
    export_stats = export_data.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
        .groupBy("partition_id") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("records"),
            min("country").alias("first_country"),
            max("country").alias("last_country")
        ) \
        .orderBy("partition_id")
    
    print("\nExport file distribution:")
    export_stats.show()
    
    print("""
    Write strategy:
    
    export_data.write \\
        .mode("overwrite") \\
        .option("maxRecordsPerFile", 10000) \\
        .parquet("/export/path")
    
    Benefits:
    - Predictable file count
    - Sorted data for efficient reads
    - Balanced file sizes
    """)
    
    # Use Case 8: Machine Learning Feature Engineering
    print("\n8. Machine Learning Feature Engineering:")
    print("""
    Scenario: Prepare features for distributed ML training
    
    Requirements:
    - Balanced partitions for parallel training
    - Reproducible splits
    """)
    
    # Create features
    ml_data = df.select(
        "category",
        "country",
        "amount",
        (col("amount") > 100).cast("int").alias("high_value")
    )
    
    # Repartition for balanced training
    ml_partitioned = ml_data.repartition(16)
    
    print(f"ML data partitions: {ml_partitioned.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Split into train/test
    train_data = ml_partitioned.filter(col("order_id") % 10 < 8)
    test_data = ml_partitioned.filter(col("order_id") % 10 >= 8)
    
    print(f"Training records: {train_data.count()}")
    print(f"Test records: {test_data.count()}")
    
    print("\nBenefit: Balanced partitions ensure even workload across workers")

def performance_benchmarking(df):
    """
    Benchmark different repartitioning strategies
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PERFORMANCE BENCHMARKING")
    print("="*80)
    
    import time
    
    strategies = {
        "No Repartition": lambda d: d,
        "Hash Repartition (4)": lambda d: d.repartition(4, "category"),
        "Hash Repartition (8)": lambda d: d.repartition(8, "category"),
        "Range Repartition (8)": lambda d: d.repartitionByRange(8, "amount"),
        "Round-Robin (8)": lambda d: d.repartition(8),
        "Coalesce (4)": lambda d: d.repartition(16).coalesce(4),
    }
    
    print("\nBenchmarking aggregation performance with different strategies:")
    print("\nStrategy | Partitions | Execution Time (s) | Records/Partition")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    results = []
    
    for name, strategy_func in strategies.items():
        # Apply strategy
        strategy_df = strategy_func(df)
        num_partitions = strategy_df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        # Benchmark aggregation
        start_time = time.time()
        
        result = strategy_df.groupBy("country", "category").agg(
            sum("amount").alias("total"),
            count("*").alias("count")
        ).collect()
        
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        records_per_partition = df.count() / num_partitions
        
        print(f"{name:<25} | {num_partitions:>10} | {execution_time:>18.3f} | {records_per_partition:>18.1f}")
        
        results.append({
            "strategy": name,
            "partitions": num_partitions,
            "time": execution_time,
            "records_per_partition": records_per_partition
        })
    
    print("\nAnalysis:")
    print("  - Optimal partition count depends on data size and cluster resources")
    print("  - Too few partitions: underutilized cluster")
    print("  - Too many partitions: excessive overhead")
    print("  - Coalesce is fastest when reducing partitions")
    
    return results

def create_repartitioning_report(df, output_path=None):
    """
    Generate a comprehensive repartitioning analysis report
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        output_path: Optional path to save report
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary containing analysis results
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("REPARTITIONING ANALYSIS REPORT")
    print("="*80)
    
    report = {}
    
    # 1. Current State Analysis
    print("\n1. CURRENT STATE ANALYSIS")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    current_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    total_records = df.count()
    
    current_distribution = df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
        .groupBy("partition_id") \
        .count() \
        .agg(
            count("partition_id").alias("num_partitions"),
            avg("count").alias("avg_records"),
            stddev("count").alias("stddev_records"),
            min("count").alias("min_records"),
            max("count").alias("max_records")
        ).collect()[0]
    
    report['current_state'] = {
        'total_records': total_records,
        'num_partitions': current_partitions,
        'avg_records_per_partition': current_distribution.avg_records,
        'stddev': current_distribution.stddev_records,
        'min_records': current_distribution.min_records,
        'max_records': current_distribution.max_records,
        'skew_factor': current_distribution.max_records / current_distribution.avg_records
    }
    
    print(f"Total Records: {total_records:,}")
    print(f"Current Partitions: {current_partitions}")
    print(f"Avg Records/Partition: {current_distribution.avg_records:,.1f}")
    print(f"Std Deviation: {current_distribution.stddev_records:,.1f}")
    print(f"Min Records: {current_distribution.min_records:,}")
    print(f"Max Records: {current_distribution.max_records:,}")
    print(f"Skew Factor: {report['current_state']['skew_factor']:.2f}x")
    
    # 2. Column Cardinality Analysis
    print("\n2. COLUMN CARDINALITY ANALYSIS")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    cardinality = {}
    for col_name in df.columns:
        try:
            distinct_count = df.select(col_name).distinct().count()
            cardinality[col_name] = distinct_count
            print(f"{col_name:20} : {distinct_count:>10,} distinct values")
        except:
            print(f"{col_name:20} : Unable to calculate")
    
    report['cardinality'] = cardinality
    
    # 3. Recommended Strategies
    print("\n3. RECOMMENDED STRATEGIES")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    recommendations = []
    
    # Calculate optimal partition count
    target_partition_size_mb = 128
    estimated_record_size = 1000  # bytes
    total_size_mb = (total_records * estimated_record_size) / (1024 * 1024)
    optimal_partitions = max(1, int(total_size_mb / target_partition_size_mb))
    
    recommendations.append({
        'strategy': 'Optimal Partition Count',
        'recommendation': optimal_partitions,
        'reason': f'Based on target partition size of {target_partition_size_mb}MB'
    })
    
    # Check for skew
    if report['current_state']['skew_factor'] > 2.0:
        recommendations.append({
            'strategy': 'Handle Data Skew',
            'recommendation': 'Use adaptive partitioning or salting',
            'reason': f'High skew factor detected: {report["current_state"]["skew_factor"]:.2f}x'
        })
    
    # Check for high cardinality columns
    high_cardinality_cols = [col for col, count in cardinality.items() 
                             if count > 10 and count < total_records * 0.5]
    
    if high_cardinality_cols:
        recommendations.append({
            'strategy': 'Hash Partitioning',
            'recommendation': f'Partition by: {", ".join(high_cardinality_cols[:2])}',
            'reason': 'Good cardinality for hash distribution'
        })
    
    # Check for date/time columns
    date_columns = [col for col in df.columns if 'date' in col.lower() or 'time' in col.lower()]
    
    if date_columns:
        recommendations.append({
            'strategy': 'Range Partitioning',
            'recommendation': f'Consider range partitioning by: {", ".join(date_columns)}',
            'reason': 'Temporal columns detected - good for time-series queries'
        })
    
    # Display recommendations
    for i, rec in enumerate(recommendations, 1):
        print(f"\n{i}. {rec['strategy']}")
        print(f"   Recommendation: {rec['recommendation']}")
        print(f"   Reason: {rec['reason']}")
    
    report['recommendations'] = recommendations
    
    # 4. Estimated Performance Impact
    print("\n4. ESTIMATED PERFORMANCE IMPACT")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    performance_estimates = []
    
    # Current state
    current_overhead = current_partitions * 0.1  # Task overhead estimate
    current_score = 100
    
    # Optimal partitioning
    optimal_overhead = optimal_partitions * 0.1
    optimal_improvement = ((current_overhead - optimal_overhead) / current_overhead) * 100
    
    performance_estimates.append({
        'scenario': 'Current State',
        'partitions': current_partitions,
        'estimated_overhead': f'{current_overhead:.1f}s',
        'performance_score': current_score
    })
    
    performance_estimates.append({
        'scenario': 'Optimized',
        'partitions': optimal_partitions,
        'estimated_overhead': f'{optimal_overhead:.1f}s',
        'performance_score': current_score + optimal_improvement
    })
    
    print(f"{'Scenario':<20} | {'Partitions':>10} | {'Overhead':>12} | {'Score':>10}")
    print("-" * 60)
    for est in performance_estimates:
        print(f"{est['scenario']:<20} | {est['partitions']:>10} | {est['estimated_overhead']:>12} | {est['performance_score']:>10.1f}")
    
    report['performance_estimates'] = performance_estimates
    
    # 5. Action Plan
    print("\n5. SUGGESTED ACTION PLAN")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    action_plan = []
    
    if current_partitions > optimal_partitions * 2:
        action_plan.append({
            'step': 1,
            'action': f'Coalesce from {current_partitions} to {optimal_partitions} partitions',
            'code': f'df.coalesce({optimal_partitions})',
            'benefit': 'Reduce task overhead and improve performance'
        })
    elif current_partitions < optimal_partitions:
        action_plan.append({
            'step': 1,
            'action': f'Repartition from {current_partitions} to {optimal_partitions} partitions',
            'code': f'df.repartition({optimal_partitions})',
            'benefit': 'Better parallelism and resource utilization'
        })
    
    if report['current_state']['skew_factor'] > 2.0:
        action_plan.append({
            'step': len(action_plan) + 1,
            'action': 'Apply salting to handle data skew',
            'code': 'df.withColumn("salt", (rand() * 10).cast("int")).repartition(col + "_salt")',
            'benefit': 'Even distribution across partitions'
        })
    
    if high_cardinality_cols:
        action_plan.append({
            'step': len(action_plan) + 1,
            'action': f'Use hash partitioning on {high_cardinality_cols[0]}',
            'code': f'df.repartition({optimal_partitions}, "{high_cardinality_cols[0]}")',
            'benefit': 'Optimize for joins and aggregations'
        })
    
    for action in action_plan:
        print(f"\nStep {action['step']}: {action['action']}")
        print(f"   Code: {action['code']}")
        print(f"   Benefit: {action['benefit']}")
    
    report['action_plan'] = action_plan
    
    # Save report if path provided
    if output_path:
        import json
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(report, f, indent=2, default=str)
        print(f"\nReport saved to: {output_path}")
    
    return report


def partition_size_calculator(num_records, avg_record_size_bytes, 
                              target_partition_size_mb=128):
    """
    Calculate optimal number of partitions based on data size
    
    Args:
        num_records: Total number of records
        avg_record_size_bytes: Average size of each record in bytes
        target_partition_size_mb: Target size for each partition in MB
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary with partition recommendations
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PARTITION SIZE CALCULATOR")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Calculate total size
    total_size_bytes = num_records * avg_record_size_bytes
    total_size_mb = total_size_bytes / (1024 * 1024)
    total_size_gb = total_size_mb / 1024
    
    # Calculate optimal partitions
    optimal_partitions = max(1, int(total_size_mb / target_partition_size_mb))
    
    # Calculate actual partition size
    actual_partition_size_mb = total_size_mb / optimal_partitions
    records_per_partition = num_records // optimal_partitions
    
    print(f"\nInput Parameters:")
    print(f"  Total Records: {num_records:,}")
    print(f"  Avg Record Size: {avg_record_size_bytes:,} bytes")
    print(f"  Target Partition Size: {target_partition_size_mb} MB")
    
    print(f"\nCalculated Metrics:")
    print(f"  Total Data Size: {total_size_mb:,.2f} MB ({total_size_gb:.2f} GB)")
    print(f"  Optimal Partitions: {optimal_partitions}")
    print(f"  Actual Partition Size: {actual_partition_size_mb:.2f} MB")
    print(f"  Records per Partition: {records_per_partition:,}")
    
    # Provide recommendations for different scenarios
    print(f"\nRecommendations for Different Scenarios:")
    
    scenarios = [
        ("Small cluster (4 cores)", 4),
        ("Medium cluster (16 cores)", 16),
        ("Large cluster (64 cores)", 64),
        ("Very large cluster (256 cores)", 256)
    ]
    
    print(f"\n{'Scenario':<30} | {'Min Partitions':>15} | {'Recommended':>15} | {'Max Partitions':>15}")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for scenario_name, cores in scenarios:
        min_parts = cores
        recommended = max(cores * 2, optimal_partitions)
        max_parts = cores * 4
        
        print(f"{scenario_name:<30} | {min_parts:>15} | {recommended:>15} | {max_parts:>15}")
    
    return {
        'total_size_mb': total_size_mb,
        'optimal_partitions': optimal_partitions,
        'actual_partition_size_mb': actual_partition_size_mb,
        'records_per_partition': records_per_partition
    }

def compare_partitioning_strategies(df, strategies_dict):
    """
    Compare multiple partitioning strategies side-by-side
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        strategies_dict: Dictionary of strategy names and functions
    
    Returns:
        Comparison results
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PARTITIONING STRATEGY COMPARISON")
    print("="*80)
    
    results = []
    
    for strategy_name, strategy_func in strategies_dict.items():
        print(f"\nAnalyzing: {strategy_name}")
        
        # Apply strategy
        strategy_df = strategy_func(df)
        
        # Collect metrics
        partition_stats = strategy_df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
            .groupBy("partition_id") \
            .count() \
            .agg(
                count("partition_id").alias("num_partitions"),
                avg("count").alias("avg_records"),
                stddev("count").alias("stddev_records"),
                min("count").alias("min_records"),
                max("count").alias("max_records")
            ).collect()[0]
        
        skew_factor = partition_stats.max_records / partition_stats.avg_records
        cv = partition_stats.stddev_records / partition_stats.avg_records
        
        results.append({
            'strategy': strategy_name,
            'num_partitions': partition_stats.num_partitions,
            'avg_records': partition_stats.avg_records,
            'stddev': partition_stats.stddev_records,
            'min_records': partition_stats.min_records,
            'max_records': partition_stats.max_records,
            'skew_factor': skew_factor,
            'cv': cv
        })
    
    # Display comparison table
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COMPARISON RESULTS")
    print("="*80)
    
    print(f"\n{'Strategy':<25} | {'Partitions':>10} | {'Avg Records':>12} | {'Std Dev':>10} | {'Skew':>8} | {'Quality':>10}")
    print("-" * 100)
    
    for result in results:
        quality = "Excellent" if result['cv'] < 0.1 else "Good" if result['cv'] < 0.3 else "Fair" if result['cv'] < 0.5 else "Poor"
        print(f"{result['strategy']:<25} | {result['num_partitions']:>10} | {result['avg_records']:>12.1f} | "
              f"{result['stddev']:>10.1f} | {result['skew_factor']:>8.2f}x | {quality:>10}")
    
    # Recommendations
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("RECOMMENDATIONS")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Find best strategy by different criteria
    best_distribution = min(results, key=lambda x: x['cv'])
    most_partitions = max(results, key=lambda x: x['num_partitions'])
    least_skew = min(results, key=lambda x: x['skew_factor'])
    
    print(f"\nBest Distribution (lowest CV): {best_distribution['strategy']}")
    print(f"  Coefficient of Variation: {best_distribution['cv']:.3f}")
    
    print(f"\nMost Parallelism: {most_partitions['strategy']}")
    print(f"  Partitions: {most_partitions['num_partitions']}")
    
    print(f"\nLeast Skewed: {least_skew['strategy']}")
    print(f"  Skew Factor: {least_skew['skew_factor']:.2f}x")
    
    return results

def example_complete_workflow():
    """
    Complete workflow example showing all patterns in action
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COMPLETE WORKFLOW EXAMPLE")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Step 1: Load data
    print("\n1. LOADING DATA")
    print("-" * 80)
    df = create_sample_data()
    print(f"Loaded {df.count():,} records with {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()} partitions")
    
    # Step 2: Analyze current state
    print("\n2. ANALYZING CURRENT STATE")
    print("-" * 80)
    report = create_repartitioning_report(df)
    
    # Step 3: Apply recommended strategy
    print("\n3. APPLYING OPTIMIZATION")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    optimal_partitions = report['recommendations'][0]['recommendation']
    print(f"Applying recommended partition count: {optimal_partitions}")
    
    optimized_df = df.repartition(optimal_partitions, "country", "category")
    
    # Step 4: Verify improvement
    print("\n4. VERIFYING IMPROVEMENT")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    print("\nBefore optimization:")
    visualize_partition_distribution(df)
    
    print("\nAfter optimization:")
    visualize_partition_distribution(optimized_df, "country")
    
    # Step 5: Perform operations
    print("\n5. PERFORMING OPERATIONS")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Aggregation
    result = optimized_df.groupBy("country", "category").agg(
        sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
        count("*").alias("order_count"),
        avg("amount").alias("avg_amount")
    )
    
    print("\nAggregation results:")
    result.show(10)
    
    # Step 6: Prepare for output
    print("\n6. PREPARING FOR OUTPUT")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Coalesce for writing
    output_partitions = 5
    output_df = result.coalesce(output_partitions)
    
    print(f"Coalesced to {output_partitions} partitions for output")
    print(f"This will create {output_partitions} output files")
    
    # Step 7: Write (simulated)
    print("\n7. WRITING OUTPUT")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    print("""
    Writing optimized data:
    
    output_df.write \\
        .mode("overwrite") \\
        .partitionBy("country") \\
        .parquet("/output/path")
    
    Benefits achieved:
    ✓ Optimized partition count
    ✓ Even data distribution
    ✓ Efficient aggregation
    ✓ Controlled output file count
    ✓ Partitioned for efficient reads
    """)
    
    return optimized_df


def create_partitioning_cheat_sheet():
    """
    Create a quick reference cheat sheet
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("REPARTITIONING CHEAT SHEET")
    print("="*80)
    
    cheat_sheet = """

╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    PYSPARK REPARTITIONING CHEAT SHEET                      ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. HASH PARTITIONING                                                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ df.repartition(num_partitions, "column_name")                           │
│ df.repartition(num_partitions, "col1", "col2")                          │
│                                                                           │
│ ✓ Use for: JOINs, GROUP BY                                              │
│ ✓ Benefit: Co-locates related data                                      │
│ ✗ Avoid: When column has low cardinality                                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. RANGE PARTITIONING                                                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ df.repartitionByRange(num_partitions, "column_name")                    │
│ df.repartitionByRange(num_partitions, col("amount").desc())             │
│                                                                           │
│ ✓ Use for: Sorted data, time-series, range queries                     │
│ ✓ Benefit: Maintains sort order                                         │
│ ✗ Avoid: When data is highly skewed                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3. ROUND-ROBIN PARTITIONING                                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ df.repartition(num_partitions)                                          │
│                                                                           │
│ ✓ Use for: Load balancing, parallel processing                         │
│ ✓ Benefit: Guaranteed even distribution                                 │
│ ✗ Avoid: When you need data co-location                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 4. COALESCE (REDUCE PARTITIONS)                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ df.coalesce(num_partitions)                    # No shuffle             │
│ df.coalesce(num_partitions, shuffle=True)      # With shuffle           │
│                                                                           │
│ ✓ Use for: Reducing partitions after filtering                         │
│ ✓ Benefit: No shuffle overhead (by default)                             │
│ ✗ Avoid: When increasing partition count                                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 5. QUICK DECISION TREE                                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                           │
│ Need to change partitions?                                              │
│   ├─ Increase → Use repartition()                                       │
│   └─ Decrease                                                            │
│       ├─ Need even distribution? → Use repartition()                    │
│       └─ Want efficiency? → Use coalesce()                               │
│                                                                           │
│ Preparing for JOIN?                                                      │
│   └─ Use repartition(n, join_key)                                        │
│                                                                           │
│ Time-series data?                                                        │
│   └─ Use repartitionByRange(n, timestamp_col)                            │
│                                                                           │
│ Writing output?                                                          │
│   └─ Use coalesce(desired_file_count)                                    │
│                                                                           │
│ Data skewed?                                                             │
│   └─ Apply salting + repartition()                                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 6. COMMON PATTERNS                                                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                           │
│ # Pattern 1: Filter then reduce                                         │
│ df.filter(condition).coalesce(10)                                        │
│                                                                           │
│ # Pattern 2: Repartition for join                                       │
│ df1.repartition(100, "key").join(df2.repartition(100, "key"), "key")    │
│                                                                           │
│ # Pattern 3: Aggregate then reduce                                      │
│ df.groupBy("col").agg(...).coalesce(5)                                   │

def validate_partitioning_strategy(df, strategy_name, strategy_df, 
                                   expected_partitions=None, 
                                   max_skew_factor=3.0):
    """
    Validate that a partitioning strategy meets expectations
    
    Args:
        df: Original DataFrame
        strategy_name: Name of the strategy
        strategy_df: DataFrame after applying strategy
        expected_partitions: Expected number of partitions (optional)
        max_skew_factor: Maximum acceptable skew factor
    
    Returns:
        Boolean indicating if validation passed
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"VALIDATING STRATEGY: {strategy_name}")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    validation_passed = True
    issues = []
    
    # Check 1: Partition count
    actual_partitions = strategy_df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    print(f"\n✓ Check 1: Partition Count")
    print(f"  Actual: {actual_partitions}")
    
    if expected_partitions:
        print(f"  Expected: {expected_partitions}")
        if actual_partitions != expected_partitions:
            validation_passed = False
            issues.append(f"Partition count mismatch: expected {expected_partitions}, got {actual_partitions}")
            print(f"  ✗ FAILED")
        else:
            print(f"  ✓ PASSED")
    else:
        print(f"  ✓ PASSED (no expectation set)")
    
    # Check 2: Data integrity
    original_count = df.count()
    strategy_count = strategy_df.count()
    
    print(f"\n✓ Check 2: Data Integrity")
    print(f"  Original records: {original_count:,}")
    print(f"  Strategy records: {strategy_count:,}")
    
    if original_count != strategy_count:
        validation_passed = False
        issues.append(f"Data loss detected: {original_count - strategy_count} records")
        print(f"  ✗ FAILED - Data loss detected!")
    else:
        print(f"  ✓ PASSED")
    
    # Check 3: Distribution quality
    partition_stats = strategy_df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
        .groupBy("partition_id") \
        .count() \
        .agg(
            avg("count").alias("avg_records"),
            max("count").alias("max_records"),
            min("count").alias("min_records"),
            stddev("count").alias("stddev_records")
        ).collect()[0]
    
    skew_factor = partition_stats.max_records / partition_stats.avg_records
    cv = partition_stats.stddev_records / partition_stats.avg_records
    
    print(f"\n✓ Check 3: Distribution Quality")
    print(f"  Avg records/partition: {partition_stats.avg_records:,.1f}")
    print(f"  Min records: {partition_stats.min_records:,}")
    print(f"  Max records: {partition_stats.max_records:,}")
    print(f"  Skew factor: {skew_factor:.2f}x")
    print(f"  Coefficient of variation: {cv:.3f}")
    
    if skew_factor > max_skew_factor:
        validation_passed = False
        issues.append(f"High skew detected: {skew_factor:.2f}x (max allowed: {max_skew_factor}x)")
        print(f"  ✗ FAILED - Skew too high!")
    else:
        print(f"  ✓ PASSED")
    
    # Check 4: Empty partitions
    empty_partitions = strategy_df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
        .groupBy("partition_id") \
        .count() \
        .filter(col("count") == 0) \
        .count()
    
    print(f"\n✓ Check 4: Empty Partitions")
    print(f"  Empty partitions: {empty_partitions}")
    
    if empty_partitions > 0:
        issues.append(f"Found {empty_partitions} empty partitions")
        print(f"  ⚠ WARNING - Empty partitions detected")
    else:
        print(f"  ✓ PASSED")
    
    # Summary
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    if validation_passed:
        print(f"✓ VALIDATION PASSED for {strategy_name}")
    else:
        print(f"✗ VALIDATION FAILED for {strategy_name}")
        print(f"\nIssues found:")
        for i, issue in enumerate(issues, 1):
            print(f"  {i}. {issue}")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    return validation_passed


def run_all_validations(df):
    """
    Run validations on all partitioning strategies
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("RUNNING COMPREHENSIVE VALIDATIONS")
    print("="*80)
    
    strategies = {
        "Hash Partitioning": (df.repartition(8, "category"), 8),
        "Range Partitioning": (df.repartitionByRange(8, "amount"), 8),
        "Round-Robin": (df.repartition(8), 8),
        "Coalesce": (df.repartition(16).coalesce(8), 8),
    }
    
    results = {}
    
    for strategy_name, (strategy_df, expected_parts) in strategies.items():
        passed = validate_partitioning_strategy(
            df, 
            strategy_name, 
            strategy_df, 
            expected_partitions=expected_parts,
            max_skew_factor=3.0
        )
        results[strategy_name] = passed
    
    # Summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("VALIDATION SUMMARY")
    print("="*80)
    
    print(f"\n{'Strategy':<25} | {'Status':<10}")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    for strategy_name, passed in results.items():
        status = "✓ PASSED" if passed else "✗ FAILED"
        print(f"{strategy_name:<25} | {status:<10}")
    
    total_passed = sum(results.values())
    total_tests = len(results)
    
    print(f"\nOverall: {total_passed}/{total_tests} strategies passed validation")
    
    return results

        print("[2/7] Loading data...")

        print(f"  Loaded {record_count:,} records")

        # Step 3: Analyze
        print("[3/7] Analyzing data characteristics...")
        report = create_repartitioning_report(df)
        
        # Step 4: Calculate optimal strategy
        print("[4/7] Calculating optimal partitioning strategy...")
        
        # Use report recommendations
        if report['current_state']['skew_factor'] > 2.0:
            print("  High skew detected - using adaptive strategy")
            # Apply salting for skewed data
            optimized_df = df.withColumn(
                "salt", 
                (rand() * 4).cast("int")
            ).repartition(16, "category", "salt").drop("salt")
        else:
            print("  Normal distribution - using hash partitioning")
            optimal_parts = report['recommendations'][0]['recommendation']
            optimized_df = df.repartition(optimal_parts, "country", "category")
        
        # Step 5: Validate
        print("[5/7] Validating partitioning...")
        validation_passed = validate_partitioning_strategy(
            df,
            "Optimized Strategy",
            optimized_df,
            max_skew_factor=3.0
        )
        
        if not validation_passed:
            print("  ⚠ Validation failed - falling back to round-robin")
            optimized_df = df.repartition(8)
        
        # Step 6: Cache if beneficial
        print("[6/7] Caching optimized DataFrame...")
        if record_count > 10000:  # Only cache if dataset is large enough
            optimized_df.cache()
            print("  DataFrame cached for reuse")
        else:
            print("  Skipping cache - dataset too small")
        
        # Step 7: Execute operations
        print("[7/7] Executing operations...")
        
        # Perform aggregation
        result = optimized_df.groupBy("country", "category").agg(
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
            count("*").alias("order_count"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_amount"),
            min("amount").alias("min_amount"),
            max("amount").alias("max_amount")
        )
        
        # Coalesce for output
        output_df = result.coalesce(5)
        
        print("\n✓ Pipeline completed successfully!")
        print(f"\nFinal results ({result.count()} aggregated records):")
        result.show(10)
        
        # Cleanup
        if record_count > 10000:
            optimized_df.unpersist()
        
        return output_df
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n✗ Error in production pipeline: {str(e)}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        return None

class RepartitioningHelper:
    """
    Interactive helper class for repartitioning decisions
    """
    
    def __init__(self, dataframe):
        """
        Initialize helper with a DataFrame
        
        Args:
            dataframe: PySpark DataFrame to analyze
        """
        self.df = dataframe
        self.current_partitions = dataframe.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        self.record_count = None
        
    def analyze(self):
        """
        Perform comprehensive analysis
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("REPARTITIONING HELPER - ANALYSIS")
        print("="*80)
        
        # Basic info
        self.record_count = self.df.count()
        
        print(f"\nDataFrame Information:")
        print(f"  Records: {self.record_count:,}")
        print(f"  Current Partitions: {self.current_partitions}")
        print(f"  Records/Partition: {self.record_count / self.current_partitions:,.1f}")
        
        # Distribution analysis
        dist_stats = self.df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
            .groupBy("partition_id") \
            .count() \
            .agg(
                avg("count").alias("avg"),
                stddev("count").alias("stddev"),
                min("count").alias("min"),
                max("count").alias("max")
            ).collect()[0]
        
        skew = dist_stats['max'] / dist_stats['avg']
        
        print(f"\nDistribution Statistics:")
        print(f"  Average: {dist_stats['avg']:,.1f}")
        print(f"  Std Dev: {dist_stats['stddev']:,.1f}")
        print(f"  Min: {dist_stats['min']:,}")
        print(f"  Max: {dist_stats['max']:,}")
        print(f"  Skew Factor: {skew:.2f}x")
        
        # Column analysis
        print(f"\nColumn Cardinality:")
        for col_name in self.df.columns[:5]:  # First 5 columns
            try:
                distinct = self.df.select(col_name).distinct().count()
                print(f"  {col_name}: {distinct:,} distinct values")
            except:
                print(f"  {col_name}: Unable to calculate")
        
        return {
            'record_count': self.record_count,
            'current_partitions': self.current_partitions,
            'skew_factor': skew,
            'avg_records_per_partition': dist_stats['avg']
        }
    
    def recommend(self, target_partition_size_mb=128):
        """
        Get recommendations for optimal partitioning
        
        Args:
            target_partition_size_mb: Target size per partition in MB
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("REPARTITIONING HELPER - RECOMMENDATIONS")
        print("="*80)
        
        if self.record_count is None:
            self.record_count = self.df.count()
        
        # Calculate optimal partitions
        estimated_record_size = 1000  # bytes
        total_size_mb = (self.record_count * estimated_record_size) / (1024 * 1024)
        optimal_partitions = max(1, int(total_size_mb / target_partition_size_mb))
        
        print(f"\nRecommendations:")
        print(f"  Estimated Data Size: {total_size_mb:.2f} MB")
        print(f"  Target Partition Size: {target_partition_size_mb} MB")
        print(f"  Recommended Partitions: {optimal_partitions}")
        
        # Strategy recommendation
        if self.current_partitions > optimal_partitions * 2:
            strategy = f"Use coalesce({optimal_partitions})"
            reason = "Current partitions significantly higher than optimal"
        elif self.current_partitions < optimal_partitions:
            strategy = f"Use repartition({optimal_partitions})"
            reason = "Need more partitions for better parallelism"
        else:
            strategy = "No change needed"
            reason = "Current partitioning is already optimal"
        
        print(f"\n  Strategy: {strategy}")
        print(f"  Reason: {reason}")
        
        return {
            'optimal_partitions': optimal_partitions,
            'strategy': strategy,
            'reason': reason
        }
    
    def suggest_partition_column(self):
        """
        Suggest best columns for partitioning
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("REPARTITIONING HELPER - COLUMN SUGGESTIONS")
        print("="*80)
        
        suggestions = []
        
        for col_name in self.df.columns:
            try:
                distinct_count = self.df.select(col_name).distinct().count()
                
                # Good partitioning column criteria:
                # - Not too few distinct values (> 5)
                # - Not too many (< 50% of total records)
                # - Reasonable cardinality
                
                if distinct_count > 5 and distinct_count < self.record_count * 0.5:
                    score = min(distinct_count / 100, 1.0)  # Normalize score
                    suggestions.append({
                        'column': col_name,
                        'distinct_values': distinct_count,
                        'score': score
                    })
            except:
                continue
        
        # Sort by score
        suggestions.sort(key=lambda x: x['score'], reverse=True)
        
        print(f"\nSuggested Partitioning Columns (ranked):")
        print(f"{'Rank':<6} | {'Column':<20} | {'Distinct Values':>15} | {'Score':>10}")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        for i, sug in enumerate(suggestions[:5], 1):
            print(f"{i:<6} | {sug['column']:<20} | {sug['distinct_values']:>15,} | {sug['score']:>10.2f}")
        
        if suggestions:
            print(f"\nTop recommendation: Partition by '{suggestions[0]['column']}'")
            print(f"  Example: df.repartition(n, '{suggestions[0]['column']}')")
        
        return suggestions
    
    def preview_strategy(self, strategy_func, strategy_name="Custom"):
        """
        Preview the impact of a partitioning strategy
        
        Args:
            strategy_func: Function that takes df and returns repartitioned df
            strategy_name: Name of the strategy
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print(f"REPARTITIONING HELPER - PREVIEW: {strategy_name}")
        print("="*80)
        
        # Apply strategy
        preview_df = strategy_func(self.df)
        
        # Analyze result
        new_partitions = preview_df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        dist_stats = preview_df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
            .groupBy("partition_id") \
            .count() \
            .agg(
                avg("count").alias("avg"),
                stddev("count").alias("stddev"),
                min("count").alias("min"),
                max("count").alias("max")
            ).collect()[0]
        
        new_skew = dist_stats['max'] / dist_stats['avg']
        
        # Current stats for comparison
        current_dist = self.df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
            .groupBy("partition_id") \
            .count() \
            .agg(
                avg("count").alias("avg"),
                max("count").alias("max")
            ).collect()[0]
        
        current_skew = current_dist['max'] / current_dist['avg']
        
        print(f"\nComparison:")
        print(f"{'Metric':<30} | {'Current':>15} | {'After Strategy':>15} | {'Change':>10}")
        print("-" * 80)
        print(f"{'Partitions':<30} | {self.current_partitions:>15} | {new_partitions:>15} | "
              f"{((new_partitions - self.current_partitions) / self.current_partitions * 100):>9.1f}%")
        print(f"{'Avg Records/Partition':<30} | {current_dist['avg']:>15,.1f} | {dist_stats['avg']:>15,.1f} | "
              f"{((dist_stats['avg'] - current_dist['avg']) / current_dist['avg'] * 100):>9.1f}%")
        print(f"{'Skew Factor':<30} | {current_skew:>15.2f}x | {new_skew:>15.2f}x | "
              f"{((new_skew - current_skew) / current_skew * 100):>9.1f}%")
        
        # Recommendation
        print(f"\nAssessment:")
        if new_skew < current_skew:
            print("  ✓ Improved distribution (lower skew)")
        elif new_skew > current_skew:
            print("  ✗ Worse distribution (higher skew)")
        else:
            print("  = Similar distribution")
        
        if abs(new_partitions - self.current_partitions) / self.current_partitions > 0.5:
            print("  ⚠ Significant change in partition count")
        
        return {
            'new_partitions': new_partitions,
            'new_skew': new_skew,
            'improvement': current_skew - new_skew
        }


# Example usage of RepartitioningHelper
def demonstrate_helper():
    """
    Demonstrate the RepartitioningHelper class
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("REPARTITIONING HELPER - DEMONSTRATION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create sample data
    df = create_sample_data()
    
    # Initialize helper
    helper = RepartitioningHelper(df)

    analysis = helper.analyze()

    # Preview strategies

        best_column = column_suggestions[0]['column']

        )
        
        helper.preview_strategy(

        )
        
        helper.preview_strategy(
            lambda d: d.coalesce(4),

        )
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("Helper demonstration complete!")
    print("="*80)


# Run helper demonstration if this is the main module
if __name__ == "__main__":
    demonstrate_helper()

def export_repartitioning_metrics_to_csv(df, output_path="partition_metrics.csv"):
    """
    Export detailed partition metrics to CSV for external analysis
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        output_path: Path to save CSV file
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("EXPORTING PARTITION METRICS")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Collect detailed metrics
    metrics = df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
        .groupBy("partition_id") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("record_count"),
            *[countDistinct(col_name).alias(f"distinct_{col_name}") 
              for col_name in df.columns[:5]]  # First 5 columns
        ) \
        .orderBy("partition_id")
    
    # Convert to Pandas and export
    try:
        pandas_df = metrics.toPandas()
        pandas_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
        print(f"\n✓ Metrics exported to: {output_path}")
        print(f"  Rows: {len(pandas_df)}")
        print(f"  Columns: {len(pandas_df.columns)}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n✗ Export failed: {str(e)}")
    
    return metrics


def create_partition_heatmap_data(df, partition_col, value_col):
    """
    Create data for visualizing partition distribution as a heatmap
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        partition_col: Column to partition by
        value_col: Column to aggregate
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with heatmap data
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("CREATING PARTITION HEATMAP DATA")
    print("="*80)
    
    heatmap_data = df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
        .groupBy("partition_id", partition_col) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("record_count"),
            sum(value_col).alias("total_value"),
            avg(value_col).alias("avg_value")
        ) \
        .orderBy("partition_id", partition_col)
    
    print("\nHeatmap data preview:")
    heatmap_data.show(20)
    
    # Pivot for better visualization
    pivot_data = heatmap_data.groupBy("partition_id") \
        .pivot(partition_col) \
        .agg(sum("record_count"))
    
    print("\nPivoted data (partitions x categories):")
    pivot_data.show()
    
    return heatmap_data, pivot_data

        "Optimal (8)": 8,
        "Many (16)": 16,
        "Very Many (32)": 32,
        "Excessive (64)": 64
    }
    
    print("\nSimulating different partition counts...\n")
    print(f"{'Scenario':<20} | {'Partitions':>10} | {'Avg Records':>12} | {'Skew':>8} | "
          f"{'Task Overhead':>15} | {'Assessment':>15}")
    print("-" * 95)
    
    results = []
    
    for scenario_name, num_parts in scenarios.items():
        # Repartition
        scenario_df = df.repartition(num_parts)
        
        # Calculate metrics
        stats = scenario_df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
            .groupBy("partition_id") \
            .count() \
            .agg(
                avg("count").alias("avg_records"),
                max("count").alias("max_records")
            ).collect()[0]
        
        skew = stats.max_records / stats.avg_records
        task_overhead = num_parts * 0.1  # Simplified overhead estimate
        
        # Assessment
        if num_parts < 4:
            assessment = "Under-partitioned"
        elif num_parts > 32:
            assessment = "Over-partitioned"
        elif 6 <= num_parts <= 12:
            assessment = "Optimal"
        else:
            assessment = "Acceptable"
        
        print(f"{scenario_name:<20} | {num_parts:>10} | {stats.avg_records:>12,.1f} | "
              f"{skew:>8.2f}x | {task_overhead:>13.1f}s | {assessment:>15}")
        
        results.append({
            'scenario': scenario_name,
            'partitions': num_parts,
            'avg_records': stats.avg_records,
            'skew': skew,
            'overhead': task_overhead,
            'assessment': assessment
        })
    
    print("\nKey Insights:")
    print("  • Too few partitions: Underutilized cluster, poor parallelism")
    print("  • Too many partitions: Excessive overhead, scheduler bottleneck")
    print("  • Optimal range: 2-4x the number of CPU cores")
    
    return results


def analyze_join_optimization(df1, df2, join_key):
    """
    Analyze and optimize partitioning for join operations
    
    Args:
        df1: First DataFrame
        df2: Second DataFrame
        join_key: Column to join on
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("JOIN OPTIMIZATION ANALYSIS")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Analyze both DataFrames
    df1_count = df1.count()
    df2_count = df2.count()
    df1_parts = df1.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    df2_parts = df2.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    
    print(f"\nDataFrame 1:")
    print(f"  Records: {df1_count:,}")
    print(f"  Partitions: {df1_parts}")
    print(f"  Records/Partition: {df1_count / df1_parts:,.1f}")
    
    print(f"\nDataFrame 2:")
    print(f"  Records: {df2_count:,}")
    print(f"  Partitions: {df2_parts}")
    print(f"  Records/Partition: {df2_count / df2_parts:,.1f}")
    
    # Check join key cardinality
    df1_key_cardinality = df1.select(join_key).distinct().count()
    df2_key_cardinality = df2.select(join_key).distinct().count()
    
    print(f"\nJoin Key Analysis ('{join_key}'):")
    print(f"  DF1 distinct values: {df1_key_cardinality:,}")
    print(f"  DF2 distinct values: {df2_key_cardinality:,}")
    
    # Determine optimal strategy
    print("\n" + "-"*80)
    print("OPTIMIZATION RECOMMENDATIONS:")
    print("-"*80)
    
    # Calculate optimal partitions
    total_records = df1_count + df2_count
    optimal_partitions = max(8, min(200, int(total_records / 10000)))
    
    print(f"\n1. Optimal Partition Count: {optimal_partitions}")
    print(f"   Reason: Based on total data volume")
    
    # Check if broadcast join is suitable
    broadcast_threshold = 10 * 1024 * 1024  # 10MB
    df2_size_estimate = df2_count * 1000  # Rough estimate
    
    if df2_size_estimate < broadcast_threshold:
        print(f"\n2. Broadcast Join Recommended")
        print(f"   Reason: DF2 is small ({df2_size_estimate / 1024 / 1024:.2f} MB)")
        print(f"   Code: df1.join(broadcast(df2), '{join_key}')")
    else:
        print(f"\n2. Shuffle Join Required")
        print(f"   Reason: Both DataFrames are large")
        print(f"   Recommendation: Pre-partition both on join key")
        print(f"\n   Code:")
        print(f"   df1_part = df1.repartition({optimal_partitions}, '{join_key}')")
        print(f"   df2_part = df2.repartition({optimal_partitions}, '{join_key}')")
        print(f"   result = df1_part.join(df2_part, '{join_key}')")
    
    # Check for skew
    df1_skew = df1.groupBy(join_key).count().agg(
        max("count").alias("max"),
        avg("count").alias("avg")
    ).collect()[0]
    
    skew_factor = df1_skew['max'] / df1_skew['avg']
    
    if skew_factor > 3.0:
        print(f"\n3. ⚠ SKEW DETECTED (factor: {skew_factor:.2f}x)")
        print(f"   Recommendation: Apply salting technique")
        print(f"\n   Code:")
        print(f"   # Add salt to skewed keys")
        print(f"   df1_salted = df1.withColumn('salt', (rand() * 10).cast('int'))")
        print(f"   df2_replicated = df2.withColumn('salt', explode(array(*[lit(i) for i in range(10)])))")
        print(f"   result = df1_salted.join(df2_replicated, ['{join_key}', 'salt'])")
    else:
        print(f"\n3. No significant skew detected (factor: {skew_factor:.2f}x)")
    
    return {
        'optimal_partitions': optimal_partitions,
        'broadcast_suitable': df2_size_estimate < broadcast_threshold,
        'skew_factor': skew_factor
    }


def partition_health_check(df):
    """
    Comprehensive health check for DataFrame partitioning
    
    Returns health score and recommendations
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PARTITION HEALTH CHECK")
    print("="*80)
    
    health_score = 100
    issues = []
    warnings = []
    recommendations = []
    
    # Check 1: Partition count
    num_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    record_count = df.count()
    
    print(f"\n[1/6] Checking partition count...")
    print(f"      Partitions: {num_partitions}")
    
    if num_partitions < 2:
        health_score -= 30
        issues.append("Too few partitions (< 2)")
        recommendations.append("Increase partitions for better parallelism")
    elif num_partitions > 1000:
        health_score -= 20
        issues.append("Too many partitions (> 1000)")
        recommendations.append("Reduce partitions to decrease overhead")
    elif num_partitions > 500:
        health_score -= 10
        warnings.append("High partition count (> 500)")
    
    # Check 2: Partition size
    print(f"\n[2/6] Checking partition sizes...")
    avg_records_per_partition = record_count / num_partitions
    
    if avg_records_per_partition < 100:
        health_score -= 25
        issues.append(f"Partitions too small (avg {avg_records_per_partition:.0f} records)")
        recommendations.append("Coalesce to fewer partitions")
    elif avg_records_per_partition > 1000000:
        health_score -= 25
        issues.append(f"Partitions too large (avg {avg_records_per_partition:,.0f} records)")
        recommendations.append("Repartition to more partitions")
    
    # Check 3: Distribution skew
    print(f"\n[3/6] Checking distribution skew...")
    dist_stats = df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
        .groupBy("partition_id") \
        .count() \
        .agg(
            avg("count").alias("avg"),
            max("count").alias("max"),
            min("count").alias("min"),
            stddev("count").alias("stddev")
        ).collect()[0]
    
    skew_factor = dist_stats['max'] / dist_stats['avg']
    cv = dist_stats['stddev'] / dist_stats['avg']
    
    print(f"      Skew factor: {skew_factor:.2f}x")
    print(f"      CV: {cv:.3f}")
    
    if skew_factor > 5.0:
        health_score -= 30
        issues.append(f"Severe skew detected ({skew_factor:.2f}x)")
        recommendations.append("Apply adaptive partitioning or salting")
    elif skew_factor > 3.0:
        health_score -= 15
        warnings.append(f"Moderate skew detected ({skew_factor:.2f}x)")
        recommendations.append("Consider rebalancing partitions")
    
    # Check 4: Empty partitions
    print(f"\n[4/6] Checking for empty partitions...")
    empty_partitions = df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()) \
        .groupBy("partition_id") \
        .count() \
        .filter(col("count") == 0) \
        .count()
    
    if empty_partitions > 0:
        health_score -= 10
        warnings.append(f"{empty_partitions} empty partitions found")
        recommendations.append("Coalesce to remove empty partitions")
    
    # Check 5: Partition efficiency
    print(f"\n[5/6] Checking partition efficiency...")
    efficiency = (dist_stats['min'] / dist_stats['avg']) * 100
    
    print(f"      Efficiency: {efficiency:.1f}%")
    
    if efficiency < 50:
        health_score -= 15
        warnings.append(f"Low partition efficiency ({efficiency:.1f}%)")
    
    # Check 6: Overall assessment
    print(f"\n[6/6] Overall assessment...")
    
    # Health score summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("HEALTH CHECK RESULTS")
    print("="*80)
    
    print(f"\nHealth Score: {health_score}/100")
    
    if health_score >= 90:
        status = "✓ EXCELLENT"
        color = "GREEN"
    elif health_score >= 70:
        status = "✓ GOOD"
        color = "YELLOW"
    elif health_score >= 50:
        status = "⚠ FAIR"
        color = "ORANGE"
    else:
        status = "✗ POOR"
        color = "RED"
    
    print(f"Status: {status}")
    
    # Issues
    if issues:
        print(f"\n❌ CRITICAL ISSUES ({len(issues)}):")
        for i, issue in enumerate(issues, 1):
            print(f"   {i}. {issue}")
    
    # Warnings
    if warnings:
        print(f"\n
```python
    # Warnings
    if warnings:
        print(f"\n⚠ WARNINGS ({len(warnings)}):")
        for i, warning in enumerate(warnings, 1):

    if recommendations:

def generate_repartitioning_code(df, strategy, num_partitions, columns=None):
    """
    Generate executable code for different repartitioning strategies
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame (for context)
        strategy: Strategy name ('hash', 'range', 'round-robin', 'coalesce')
        num_partitions: Number of partitions
        columns: Column(s) for partitioning
    
    Returns:
        String containing executable code
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("CODE GENERATOR")
    print("="*80)
    
    code_templates = {
        'hash': """
# Hash Repartitioning Strategy
# Distributes data based on hash of specified column(s)

# Single column
df_repartitioned = df.repartition({num_partitions}, "{column}")

# Multiple columns
df_repartitioned = df.repartition({num_partitions}, {columns})

# Usage example
result = df_repartitioned.groupBy("{column}").agg(sum("amount"))
""",
        'range': """
# Range Repartitioning Strategy
# Distributes data based on value ranges

# Ascending order
df_repartitioned = df.repartitionByRange({num_partitions}, "{column}")

# Descending order
df_repartitioned = df.repartitionByRange({num_partitions}, col("{column}").desc())

# Multiple columns
df_repartitioned = df.repartitionByRange({num_partitions}, {columns})

# Usage example
result = df_repartitioned.filter(col("{column}").between(100, 500))
""",
        'round-robin': """
# Round-Robin Repartitioning Strategy
# Evenly distributes data across partitions

df_repartitioned = df.repartition({num_partitions})

# Usage example
# Good for balanced parallel processing
result = df_repartitioned.mapPartitions(process_partition)
""",
        'coalesce': """
# Coalesce Strategy
# Reduces partitions without shuffle (efficient)

# Without shuffle (default)
df_coalesced = df.coalesce({num_partitions})

# With shuffle (for better distribution)
df_coalesced = df.coalesce({num_partitions}, shuffle=True)

# Usage example
# Good before writing to reduce output files
df_coalesced.write.parquet("/output/path")
""",
        'adaptive': """
# Adaptive Repartitioning Strategy
# Handles skewed data with salting

# Detect skewed values
skewed_values = df.groupBy("{column}").count() \\
    .filter(col("count") > threshold) \\
    .select("{column}") \\
    .rdd.flatMap(lambda x: x).collect()

# Apply salting to skewed values
df_salted = df.withColumn(
    "partition_key",
    when(
        col("{column}").isin(skewed_values),
        concat(col("{column}"), lit("_"), (rand() * 10).cast("int"))
    ).otherwise(col("{column}"))
)

# Repartition on salted key
df_repartitioned = df_salted.repartition({num_partitions}, "partition_key")

# Usage example
result = df_repartitioned.groupBy("{column}").agg(sum("amount"))
"""
    }
    
    # Get template
    template = code_templates.get(strategy.lower(), "# Strategy not found")
    
    # Format template
    if columns:
        if isinstance(columns, list):
            columns_str = ', '.join([f'"{col}"' for col in columns])
            column = columns[0]
        else:
            columns_str = f'"{columns}"'
            column = columns
    else:
        columns_str = '""'
        column = "column_name"
    
    code = template.format(
        num_partitions=num_partitions,
        column=column,
        columns=columns_str
    )
    
    print(f"\nGenerated code for '{strategy}' strategy:")
    print("="*80)
    print(code)
    print("="*80)
    
    return code


def create_partition_migration_plan(current_df, target_partitions, target_strategy='hash', target_columns=None):
    """
    Create a migration plan from current partitioning to target partitioning
    
    Args:
        current_df: Current DataFrame
        target_partitions: Target number of partitions
        target_strategy: Target partitioning strategy
        target_columns: Columns for partitioning
    
    Returns:
        Migration plan with steps and estimated impact
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PARTITION MIGRATION PLAN")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Analyze current state
    current_partitions = current_df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    current_count = current_df.count()
    
    print(f"\nCurrent State:")
    print(f"  Partitions: {current_partitions}")
    print(f"  Records: {current_count:,}")
    print(f"  Avg Records/Partition: {current_count / current_partitions:,.1f}")
    
    print(f"\nTarget State:")
    print(f"  Partitions: {target_partitions}")
    print(f"  Strategy: {target_strategy}")
    if target_columns:
        print(f"  Partition Columns: {target_columns}")
    print(f"  Expected Avg Records/Partition: {current_count / target_partitions:,.1f}")
    
    # Create migration steps
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("MIGRATION STEPS")
    print("="*80)
    
    steps = []
    
    # Step 1: Analyze and prepare
    steps.append({
        'step': 1,
        'action': 'Analyze current distribution',
        'code': 'current_df.withColumn("pid", spark_partition_id()).groupBy("pid").count().show()',
        'description': 'Understand current partition distribution'
    })
    
    # Step 2: Cache if beneficial
    if current_count > 100000:
        steps.append({
            'step': 2,
            'action': 'Cache DataFrame',
            'code': 'current_df.cache()\ncurrent_df.count()  # Materialize cache',
            'description': 'Cache data to avoid recomputation during migration'
        })
    
    # Step 3: Apply repartitioning
    if target_strategy == 'hash' and target_columns:
        repartition_code = f'df_migrated = current_df.repartition({target_partitions}, "{target_columns}")'
    elif target_strategy == 'range' and target_columns:
        repartition_code = f'df_migrated = current_df.repartitionByRange({target_partitions}, "{target_columns}")'
    elif target_strategy == 'coalesce' and target_partitions < current_partitions:
        repartition_code = f'df_migrated = current_df.coalesce({target_partitions})'
    else:
        repartition_code = f'df_migrated = current_df.repartition({target_partitions})'
    
    steps.append({
        'step': len(steps) + 1,
        'action': f'Apply {target_strategy} repartitioning',
        'code': repartition_code,
        'description': f'Migrate to {target_partitions} partitions using {target_strategy} strategy'
    })
    
    # Step 4: Validate
    steps.append({
        'step': len(steps) + 1,
        'action': 'Validate migration',
        'code': '''# Check partition count
print(f"New partitions: {df_migrated.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")

# Verify record count
assert df_migrated.count() == current_df.count(), "Data loss detected!"

# Check distribution
df_migrated.withColumn("pid", spark_partition_id()).groupBy("pid").count().show()''',
        'description': 'Ensure data integrity and verify new distribution'
    })
    
    # Step 5: Persist if needed
    steps.append({
        'step': len(steps) + 1,
        'action': 'Persist migrated DataFrame',
        'code': 'df_migrated.cache()\ndf_migrated.count()  # Materialize',
        'description': 'Cache migrated DataFrame for subsequent operations'
    })
    
    # Step 6: Cleanup
    if current_count > 100000:
        steps.append({
            'step': len(steps) + 1,
            'action': 'Cleanup old cache',
            'code': 'current_df.unpersist()',
            'description': 'Release memory from old DataFrame'
        })
    
    # Print steps
    for step in steps:
        print(f"\nStep {step['step']}: {step['action']}")
        print(f"  Description: {step['description']}")
        print(f"  Code:")
        for line in step['code'].split('\n'):
            print(f"    {line}")
    
    # Estimate impact
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ESTIMATED IMPACT")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Calculate shuffle cost
    shuffle_required = not (target_strategy == 'coalesce' and target_partitions < current_partitions)
    
    print(f"\nShuffle Required: {'Yes' if shuffle_required else 'No'}")
    
    if shuffle_required:
        estimated_shuffle_time = (current_count / 100000) * 10  # Rough estimate
        print(f"Estimated Shuffle Time: ~{estimated_shuffle_time:.1f} seconds")
        print(f"Network I/O: High (all data shuffled)")
    else:
        print(f"Estimated Time: ~5 seconds")
        print(f"Network I/O: Low (no shuffle)")
    
    # Memory impact
    if target_partitions > current_partitions * 2:
        print(f"Memory Impact: Moderate (more task overhead)")
    elif target_partitions < current_partitions / 2:
        print(f"Memory Impact: Low (fewer tasks)")
    else:
        print(f"Memory Impact: Minimal")
    
    # Performance impact
    partition_change_pct = ((target_partitions - current_partitions) / current_partitions) * 100
    
    print(f"\nPartition Change: {partition_change_pct:+.1f}%")
    
    if abs(partition_change_pct) < 20:
        print(f"Performance Impact: Minimal")
    elif abs(partition_change_pct) < 50:
        print(f"Performance Impact: Moderate")
    else:
        print(f"Performance Impact: Significant")
    
    # Recommendations
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("RECOMMENDATIONS")
    print("="*80)
    
    print("\n✓ Before Migration:")
    print("  • Test on a sample dataset first")
    print("  • Monitor cluster resources during migration")
    print("  • Schedule during low-traffic periods if possible")
    
    print("\n✓ During Migration:")
    print("  • Monitor Spark UI for shuffle metrics")
    print("  • Watch for memory pressure or spills")
    print("  • Be prepared to roll back if issues occur")
    
    print("\n✓ After Migration:")
    print("  • Validate data integrity")
    print("  • Compare query performance")
    print("  • Monitor partition distribution over time")
    
    return {
        'steps': steps,
        'shuffle_required': shuffle_required,
        'partition_change_pct': partition_change_pct,
        'current_partitions': current_partitions,
        'target_partitions': target_partitions
    }
