def production_deployment_guide():
    """
    Provides comprehensive guide for production deployment
    """
    guide = """
    
    ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║              BLOOM FILTER PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT GUIDE                    ║
    ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    1. CHOOSING THE RIGHT PATTERN
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Pattern                  | Use Case                    | Pros              | Cons
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Single Bloom Filter      | Static membership testing   | Fast, Low memory  | No deletions
    Cascading Bloom Filter   | Tiered access control      | Multi-level       | Complex setup
    Counting Bloom Filter    | Dynamic membership         | Supports deletes  | High memory
    Scalable Bloom Filter    | Growing datasets           | Auto-scaling      | Slight overhead
    Partitioned Bloom Filter | Distributed processing     | Parallel queries  | Coordination cost
    
    
    2. SIZING RECOMMENDATIONS
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Dataset Size    | Recommended FPR | Memory Budget  | Pattern Choice
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    < 10K           | 0.01            | < 10 KB        | Single
    10K - 100K      | 0.01            | 10-100 KB      | Single/Scalable
    100K - 1M       | 0.001           | 100 KB - 1 MB  | Scalable
    1M - 10M        | 0.001           | 1-10 MB        | Partitioned
    > 10M           | 0.0001          | > 10 MB        | Partitioned/Distributed
    
    
    3. PERFORMANCE TUNING
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Optimization                    | Configuration
    ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Reduce false positives          | Lower FPR (0.001 instead of 0.01)
    Reduce memory usage             | Higher FPR (0.1 instead of 0.01)
    Faster insertions               | Fewer hash functions (reduce FPR target)
    Better distribution             | Use MurmurHash3 (already implemented)
    Parallel processing             | Use Partitioned pattern
    
    
    4. SPARK CONFIGURATION
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    # For large-scale bloom filter operations
    spark = SparkSession.builder \\
        .appName("BloomFilterProduction") \\
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \\
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \\
        .config("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10MB") \\
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200") \\
        .config("spark.driver.memory", "4g") \\
        .config("spark.executor.memory", "8g") \\
        .getOrCreate()
    
    
    5. MONITORING AND ALERTING
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Metric                          | Alert Threshold        | Action
    ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Actual FPR > Expected FPR       | > 2x expected          | Rebuild filter
    Memory usage                    | > 80% of allocated     | Increase FPR
    Query latency                   | > 100ms p99            | Add partitions
    Filter fill rate                | > 90%                  | Scale up
    False positive count            | > 5% of queries        | Reduce FPR
    
    
    6. ERROR HANDLING
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    try:
        # Build bloom filter
        bf = build_bloom_filter(data)
    except MemoryError:
        # Fall back to higher FPR
        bf = build_bloom_filter(data, fpr=0.1)
    except Exception as e:
        # Log and use fallback strategy
        logger.error(f"Bloom filter creation failed: {e}")
        # Use exact matching as fallback
        use_exact_matching(data)
    
    
    7. MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Task                            | Frequency              | Notes
    ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Rebuild filters                 | Daily/Weekly           | For static data
    Monitor FPR                     | Hourly                 | Alert on deviation
    Validate accuracy               | Daily                  | Sample-based testing
    Archive old filters             | Monthly                | For time-decaying
    Performance benchmarking        | Weekly                 | Track degradation
    
    
    8. SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    - Bloom filters can leak information about dataset size
    - False positives may expose sensitive data
    - Use encryption for serialized filters containing PII
    - Implement access controls on filter endpoints
    - Audit filter queries for compliance
    
    
    9. COST OPTIMIZATION
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Strategy                        | Savings                | Trade-off
    ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Increase FPR                    | 50% memory reduction   | More false positives
    Use partitioned filters         | Parallel processing    | Coordination overhead
    Cache filters in memory         | Faster queries         | Memory cost
    Periodic rebuild vs continuous  | Reduced compute        | Staleness
    
    
    10. COMMON PITFALLS AND SOLUTIONS
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Pitfall                         | Solution
    ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Underestimating dataset size    | Use Scalable Bloom Filter
    Not accounting for growth       | Build with 2x capacity
    Ignoring false positives        | Validate critical operations
    Using wrong hash function       | Use MurmurHash3 or similar
    Not testing serialization       | Include in CI/CD pipeline
    Forgetting to rebuild           | Automate rebuild process
    
    """
    
    print(guide)

            transactions.append((
                f"txn_{i}",

        txn_df = spark.createDataFrame(

            ["transaction_id", "user_id", "amount", "status"]
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Processing {txn_df.count()} transactions")
        
        # Step 4: Filter suspicious transactions using Bloom filter
        logger.info("Step 4: Filtering suspicious transactions...")
        
        suspicious_txn = txn_df.filter(

        )
        
        suspicious_count = suspicious_txn.count()
        logger.info(f"Identified {suspicious_count} suspicious transactions")
        
        # Step 5: Detailed verification for suspicious transactions
        logger.info("Step 5: Performing detailed verification...")
        
        # Join with fraud database for exact verification
        verified_fraud = suspicious_txn
```python
.join(
            fraud_df,
            suspicious_txn.user_id == fraud_df.user_id,
            "inner"
        ).select(
            suspicious_txn["*"],
            fraud_df["risk_score"]
        )
        
        verified_count = verified_fraud.count()
        false_positives = suspicious_count - verified_count
        
        logger.info(f"Verified fraud transactions: {verified_count}")
        logger.info(f"False positives: {false_positives}")
        
        # Step 6: Calculate metrics
        logger.info("Step 6: Calculating performance metrics...")
        
        total_transactions = txn_df.count()
        fraud_detection_rate = (verified_count / total_transactions) * 100
        false_positive_rate = (false_positives / suspicious_count) * 100 if suspicious_count > 0 else 0
        
        # Step 7: Generate report
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("FRAUD DETECTION PIPELINE REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"\nTransaction Processing:")
        print(f"  Total Transactions: {total_transactions:,}")
        print(f"  Suspicious Flagged: {suspicious_count:,}")
        print(f"  Verified Fraud: {verified_count:,}")
        print(f"  False Positives: {false_positives:,}")
        
        print(f"\nPerformance Metrics:")
        print(f"  Fraud Detection Rate: {fraud_detection_rate:.2f}%")
        print(f"  False Positive Rate: {false_positive_rate:.2f}%")
        print(f"  Transactions Requiring Full Verification: {suspicious_count:,}")
        print(f"  Transactions Skipped (Bloom Filter): {total_transactions - suspicious_count:,}")
        
        efficiency_gain = ((total_transactions - suspicious_count) / total_transactions) * 100
        print(f"  Efficiency Gain: {efficiency_gain:.2f}%")
        
        # Step 8: Action on verified fraud
        logger.info("Step 8: Taking action on verified fraud...")
        
        blocked_txn = verified_fraud.withColumn("status", lit("blocked"))
        
        print(f"\nActions Taken:")
        print(f"  Transactions Blocked: {blocked_txn.count():,}")
        
        # Show sample of blocked transactions
        print(f"\nSample Blocked Transactions:")
        blocked_txn.select("transaction_id", "user_id", "amount", "risk_score", "status").show(10)
        
        # Step 9: Update metrics for monitoring
        logger.info("Step 9: Updating monitoring metrics...")
        
        metrics = {
            'timestamp': spark.sql("SELECT current_timestamp()").first()[0],
            'total_transactions': total_transactions,
            'suspicious_count': suspicious_count,
            'verified_fraud': verified_count,
            'false_positives': false_positives,
            'fpr': false_positive_rate,
            'efficiency_gain': efficiency_gain
        }
        
        metrics_df = spark.createDataFrame([metrics])
        print(f"\nMetrics logged for monitoring:")
        metrics_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        logger.info("Pipeline completed successfully")
        
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Pipeline failed: {str(e)}")
        raise
    finally:
        spark.stop()

def real_world_use_cases():
    """
    Documentation of real-world use cases for Bloom filters
    """
    use_cases = """
    
    ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║                    REAL-WORLD BLOOM FILTER USE CASES                     ║
    ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    
    1. WEB CRAWLING - Duplicate URL Detection
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Challenge: Crawling billions of URLs without revisiting
    Solution: Scalable Bloom Filter
    
    Implementation:
        - Initial capacity: 1M URLs
        - Growth factor: 2x
        - FPR: 0.001
        - Memory: ~1.2 MB per million URLs
    
    Results:
        - 99.9% duplicate detection
        - 50% reduction in bandwidth
        - 10x faster crawling
    
    
    2. DATABASE QUERY OPTIMIZATION - Join Filtering
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Challenge: Joining large fact table with small dimension table
    Solution: Single Bloom Filter on dimension table
    
    Implementation:
        - Build BF on dimension table keys
        - Filter fact table before shuffle
        - Reduce data movement by 95%
    
    Results:
        - Query time: 45s → 8s
        - Shuffle data: 100GB → 5GB
        - Cost savings: 80%
    
    
    3. CACHE SYSTEMS - Preventing Cache Pollution
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Challenge: Avoid cache lookups for non-existent keys
    Solution: Bloom Filter Cache Pattern
    
    Implementation:
        - BF before cache lookup
        - Capacity: 1M keys
        - FPR: 0.01
    
    Results:
        - Cache misses reduced by 70%
        - Latency improved by 40%
        - Backend load reduced by 60%
    
    
    4. FRAUD DETECTION - Real-time Transaction Screening

MATHEMATICAL FORMULAS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. Optimal bit array size (m):
   m = -(n × ln(p)) / (ln(2))²
   
   where:
   - n = expected number of elements
   - p = desired false positive rate

2. Optimal number of hash functions (k):
   k = (m/n) × ln(2)

3. Actual false positive probability:
   p = (1 - e^(-kn/m))^k

4. Memory usage:
   Memory (bytes) = m / 8


PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Operation          | Time Complexity | Space Complexity
───────────────────┼─────────────────┼──────────────────
Insert             | O(k)            | O(1)
Query              | O(k)            | O(1)
Delete (Counting)  | O(k)            | O(1)
Merge              | O(m)            | O(m)

where:
- k = number of hash functions
- m = size of bit array


CONFIGURATION EXAMPLES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    expected_elements=10000,
    false_positive_rate=0.01
)

# Medium dataset (100K - 1M elements)

    initial_capacity=100000,
    false_positive_rate=0.001,
    growth_factor=2
)

# Large dataset (> 1M elements)
bf = PartitionedBloomFilter(
    num_partitions=10,
    elements_per_partition=100000,
    false_positive_rate=0.0001
)

# High-precision requirements
bf = CascadingBloomFilter(
    expected_elements=100000,
    stages=[0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001]
)


SPARK INTEGRATION EXAMPLES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Build Bloom filter from DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import bloom_filter_agg

bf = df.select(
    bloom_filter_agg("column_name", 
                     expectedNumItems=1000000, 
                     fpp=0.01).alias("bf")
).first()["bf"]

# Use Bloom filter for filtering
from pyspark.sql.functions import might_contain, lit

filtered_df = df.filter(
    might_contain(lit(bf), col("column_name"))
)

# Join optimization
small_df_bf = small_df.select(
    bloom_filter_agg("key", expectedNumItems=10000, fpp=0.01).alias("bf")
).first()["bf"]

optimized_join = large_df.filter(
    might_contain(lit(small_df_bf), col("key"))
).join(small_df, "key")


MONITORING QUERIES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- Track Bloom filter effectiveness
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) as total_queries,
    SUM(CASE WHEN bloom_hit THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as bloom_hits,
    SUM(CASE WHEN bloom_hit AND actual_hit THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as true_positives,
    SUM(CASE WHEN bloom_hit AND NOT actual_hit THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as false_positives,
    (SUM(CASE WHEN bloom_hit AND NOT actual_hit THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / 
     NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN bloom_hit THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0)) as actual_fpr
FROM query_log
WHERE timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR;


TROUBLESHOOTING
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Problem: High false positive rate
Solution: 
  - Decrease FPR parameter
  - Increase expected_elements
  - Rebuild filter with more accurate size estimate

Problem: Out of memory
Solution:
  - Increase FPR (reduces memory)
  - Use partitioned approach
  - Switch to scalable filter

Problem: Slow query performance
Solution:
  - Reduce number of hash functions
  - Use partitioned filter for parallelism
  - Cache filter in memory

Problem: Filter not detecting elements
Solution:
  - Verify hash function consistency
  - Check for serialization issues
  - Ensure filter is properly populated


API REFERENCE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

SingleBloomFilter(expected_elements, false_positive_rate)
  .add(item)                    # Add item to filter
  .contains(item)               # Check membership
  .size                         # Get filter size
  .num_hashes                   # Get hash function count

CountingBloomFilter(expected_elements, false_positive_rate, counter_size)
  .add(item)                    # Increment counters
  .remove(item)                 # Decrement counters
  .contains(item)               # Check membership
  .estimate_count(item)         # Estimate item count

ScalableBloomFilter(initial_capacity, false_positive_rate, growth_factor)
  .add(item)                    # Add to current filter
  .contains(item)               # Check all filters
  .get_stats()                  # Get filter statistics

PartitionedBloomFilter(num_partitions, elements_per_partition, fpr)
  .add(item)                    # Add to appropriate partition
  .contains(item)               # Check assigned partition
  .contains_any_partition(item) # Check all partitions
  .get_partition_stats()        # Get partition statistics

CascadingBloomFilter(expected_elements, stages)
  .add(item, stage)             # Add to specific stage(s)
  .contains(item)               # Check all stages
  .progressive_check(item)      # Check each stage


BEST PRACTICES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. Size Estimation
   - Overestimate by 20-30%
   - Monitor actual vs expected size
   - Rebuild if size exceeds 90% capacity

2. False Positive Rate
   - Start with 0.01 (1%)
   - Adjust based on use case criticality
   - Monitor actual FPR in production

3. Hash Functions
   - Use MurmurHash3 (included)
   - Ensure consistency across systems
   - Don't modify after deployment

4. Serialization
   - Test save/load in development

# ============================================================================
# ADVANCED OPTIMIZATION TECHNIQUES
# ============================================================================

def advanced_optimization_techniques():
    """
    Advanced optimization techniques for Bloom filters in production
    """
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("AdvancedBloomFilterOptimizations") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ADVANCED BLOOM FILTER OPTIMIZATION TECHNIQUES")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Technique 1: Compressed Bloom Filters
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Technique 1: Compressed Bloom Filters")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    class CompressedBloomFilter(SingleBloomFilter):
        """
        Bloom filter with compression for storage and transmission
        """
        
        def compress(self) -> bytes:
            """Compress the bit array using run-length encoding"""
            import zlib
            
            # Convert bit array to bytes
            byte_array = bytearray()
            for i in range(0, len(self.bit_array), 8):
                byte = 0
                for j in range(8):
                    if i + j < len(self.bit_array) and self.bit_array[i + j]:
                        byte |= (1 << j)
                byte_array.append(byte)
            
            # Compress using zlib
            compressed = zlib.compress(bytes(byte_array), level=9)
            
            return compressed
        
        def decompress(self, compressed_data: bytes):
            """Decompress and restore the bit array"""
            import zlib
            
            # Decompress
            decompressed = zlib.decompress(compressed_data)
            
            # Convert bytes back to bit array
            self.bit_array = []
            for byte in decompressed:
                for j in range(8):
                    self.bit_array.append(bool(byte & (1 << j)))
            
            # Trim to original size
            self.bit_array = self.bit_array[:self.size]
    
    # Demonstrate compression
    cbf = CompressedBloomFilter(10000, 0.01)
    
    # Add data
    for i in range(5000):
        cbf.add(f"item_{i}")
    
    # Compress
    compressed = cbf.compress()
    original_size = len(cbf.bit_array) / 8  # bytes
    compressed_size = len(compressed)
    compression_ratio = (1 - compressed_size / original_size) * 100
    
    print(f"Original size: {original_size:,.0f} bytes")
    print(f"Compressed size: {compressed_size:,.0f} bytes")
    print(f"Compression ratio: {compression_ratio:.2f}%")
    print(f"Space saved: {original_size - compressed_size:,.0f} bytes")
    
    # Technique 2: Adaptive False Positive Rate
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Technique 2: Adaptive False Positive Rate")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    class AdaptiveBloomFilter:
        """
        Bloom filter that adjusts FPR based on observed performance
        """
        
        def __init__(self, initial_capacity: int, initial_fpr: float = 0.01):
            self.capacity = initial_capacity
            self.current_fpr = initial_fpr
            self.filter = SingleBloomFilter(initial_capacity, initial_fpr)
            
            # Monitoring
            self.queries = 0
            self.false_positives = 0
            self.rebuild_threshold = 1000
            
        def add(self, item: str):
            """Add item to filter"""
            self.filter.add(item)
        
        def contains(self, item: str, actual_exists: bool = None) -> bool:
            """
            Check membership and optionally track accuracy
            
            Parameters:
            - item: Item to check
            - actual_exists: If provided, used to track false positives
            """
            result = self.filter.contains(item)
            
            if actual_exists is not None:
                self.queries += 1
                
                # Track false positives
                if result and not actual_exists:
                    self.false_positives += 1
                
                # Check if we need to adapt
                if self.queries >= self.rebuild_threshold:
                    self._adapt_fpr()
            
            return result
        
        def _adapt_fpr(self):
            """Adapt FPR based on observed performance"""
            if self.queries == 0:
                return
            
            observed_fpr = self.false_positives / self.queries
            expected_fpr = self.current_fpr
            
            print(f"\nAdaptive FPR Analysis:")
            print(f"  Expected FPR: {expected_fpr:.4f}")
            print(f"  Observed FPR: {observed_fpr:.4f}")
            
            # If observed FPR is too high, rebuild with lower FPR
            if observed_fpr > expected_fpr * 1.5:
                new_fpr = expected_fpr * 0.5
                print(f"  Adjusting FPR: {expected_fpr:.4f} → {new_fpr:.4f}")
                
                # Rebuild filter with new FPR
                # (In production, you'd preserve existing items)
                self.current_fpr = new_fpr
                self.filter = SingleBloomFilter(self.capacity, new_fpr)
            
            # Reset counters
            self.queries = 0
            self.false_positives = 0
    
    # Demonstrate adaptive FPR
    abf = AdaptiveBloomFilter(1000, 0.1)  # Start with high FPR
    
    # Add items
    for i in range(500):
        abf.add(f"item_{i}")
    
    # Simulate queries with ground truth
    for i in range(2000):
        item = f"item_{i}"
        actual_exists = i < 500
        abf.contains(item, actual_exists=actual_exists)
    
    # Technique 3: Bloom Filter Sharding
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Technique 3: Bloom Filter Sharding")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    class ShardedBloomFilter:
        """
        Bloom filter distributed across multiple shards for parallel processing
        """
        
        def __init__(self, num_shards: int, elements_per_shard: int, fpr: float = 0.01):
            self.num_shards = num_shards
            self.shards = [
                SingleBloomFilter(elements_per_shard, fpr)
                for _ in range(num_shards)
            ]
            self.shard_counts = [0] * num_shards
        
        def _get_shard_id(self, item: str) -> int:
            """Determine which shard an item belongs to"""
            return hash(item) % self.num_shards
        
        def add(self, item: str):
            """Add item to appropriate shard"""
            shard_id = self._get_shard_id(item)
            self.shards[shard_id].add(item)
            self.shard_counts[shard_id] += 1
        
        def contains(self, item: str) -> bool:
            """Check if item exists in its shard"""
            shard_id = self._get_shard_id(item)
            return self.shards[shard_id].contains(item)
        
        def parallel_batch_check(self, items: list) -> list:
            """
            Check multiple items in parallel across shards
            Returns list of (item, exists) tuples
            """
            from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
            
            # Group items by shard
            shard_items = {i: [] for i in range(self.num_shards)}
            for item in items:
                shard_id = self._get_shard_id(item)
                shard_items[shard_id].append(item)
            
            # Process shards in parallel
            results = []
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=self.num_shards) as executor:
                futures = []
                for shard_id, shard_item_list in shard_items.items():
                    future = executor.submit(
                        self._check_shard,
                        shard_id,
                        shard_item_list
                    )
                    futures.append(future)
                
                for future in futures:
                    results.extend(future.result())
            
            return results
        
        def _check_shard(self, shard_id: int, items: list) -> list:
            """Check items in a specific shard"""
            return [(item, self.shards[shard_id].contains(item)) for item in items]
        
        def get_shard_stats(self) -> dict:
            """Get statistics for all shards"""
            return {
                'num_shards': self.num_shards,
                'total_elements': sum(self.shard_counts),
                'avg_elements_per_shard': sum(self.shard_counts) / self.num_shards,
                'min_elements': min(self.shard_counts),
                'max_elements': max(self.shard_counts),
                'shard_distribution': self.shard_counts
            }
    
    # Demonstrate sharding
    sbf = ShardedBloomFilter(num_shards=4, elements_per_shard=2500)
    
    # Add items
    print("\nAdding 10,000 items to sharded filter...")
    for i in range(10000):
        sbf.add(f"item_{i}")
    
    # Show shard distribution
    stats = sbf.get_shard_stats()
    print(f"\nShard Statistics:")
    print(f"  Total shards: {stats['num_shards']}")
    print(f"  Total elements: {stats['total_elements']:,}")
    print(f"  Avg per shard: {stats['avg_elements_per_shard']:.0f}")
    print(f"  Min/Max: {stats['min_elements']}/{stats['max_elements']}")
    print(f"  Distribution: {stats['shard_distribution']}")
    
    # Parallel batch check
    test_items = [f"item_{i}" for i in range(0, 10000, 100)]
    
    import time
    start = time.time()
    results = sbf.parallel_batch_check(test_items)
    parallel_time = time.time() - start
    
    print(f"\nParallel batch check:")
    print(f"  Items checked: {len(test_items)}")
    print(f"  Time: {parallel_time*1000:.2f}ms")
    print(f"  Items found: {sum(1 for _, exists in results if exists)}")
    
    # Technique 4: Probabilistic Counting with Bloom Filters
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Technique 4: Probabilistic Cardinality Estimation")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    class CardinalityEstimatingBloomFilter(CountingBloomFilter):
        """
        Bloom filter that estimates cardinality (unique element count)
        """
        
        def estimate_cardinality(self) -> int:
            """
            Estimate number of unique elements using bit array fill rate
            Formula: n ≈ -(m/k) * ln(1 - X/m)
            where X is number of set bits
            """
            import math
            
            # Count set bits
            set_bits = sum(1 for count in self.counters if count > 0)
            
            if set_bits == 0:
                return 0
            
            # Calculate fill rate
            fill_rate = set_bits / self.size
            
            if fill_rate >= 1.0:
                # Filter is full, estimate is unreliable
                return self.size * self.num_hashes
            
            # Estimate cardinality
            estimated = -(self.size / self.num_hashes) * math.log(1 - fill_rate)
            
            return int(estimated)
        
        def get_fill_rate(self) -> float:
            """Get the fill rate of the filter"""
            set_bits = sum(1 for count in self.counters if count > 0)
            return set_bits / self.size
    
    # Demonstrate cardinality estimation
    cebf = CardinalityEstimatingBloomFilter(10000, 0.01)
    
    actual_unique = set()
    for i in range(5000):
        item = f"item_{i % 3000}"  # Some duplicates
        cebf.add(item)
        actual_unique.add(item)
    
    estimated = cebf.estimate_cardinality()
    actual = len(actual_unique)
    error = abs(estimated - actual) / actual * 100
    
    print(f"Cardinality Estimation:")
    print(f"  Actual unique elements: {actual:,}")
    print(f"  Estimated unique elements: {estimated:,}")
    print(f"  Error: {error:.2f}%")
    print(f"  Fill rate: {cebf.get_fill_rate()*100:.2f}%")
    
    # Technique 5: Hierarchical Bloom Filters
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Technique 5: Hierarchical Bloom Filters")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    class HierarchicalBloomFilter:
        """
        Multi-level hierarchical Bloom filter for range queries
        """
        
        def __init__(self, levels: int, capacity_per_level: int, fpr: float = 0.01):
            self.levels = levels
            self.filters = [
                SingleBloomFilter(capacity_per_level, fpr)
                for _ in range(levels)
            ]
            self.level_ranges = []
            
        def add_with_level(self, item: str, level: int):
            """Add item to specific level"""
            if 0 <= level < self.levels:
                self.filters[level].add(item)
        
        def contains_at_level(self, item: str, level: int) -> bool:
            """Check if item exists at specific level"""
            if 0 <= level < self.levels:
                return self.filters[level].contains(item)
            return False
        
        def contains_in_range(self, item: str, start_level: int, end_level: int) -> bool:
            """Check if item exists in any level within range"""
            for level in range(start_level, min(end_level + 1, self.levels)):
                if self.filters[level].contains(item):
                    return True
            return False
        
        def find_level(self, item: str) -> int:
            """Find the level where item exists (returns first match)"""
            for level in range(self.levels):
                if self.filters[level].contains(item):
                    return level
            return -1

    hbf = HierarchicalBloomFilter(levels=5, capacity_per_level=1000)

"""
PySpark Query Execution Priority Patterns
==========================================
This module demonstrates different patterns for managing query execution priorities
in PySpark applications.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import time
from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, List, Callable
import threading
from queue import PriorityQueue
import logging

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# ============================================================================
# 1. HIGH PRIORITY PATTERN
# ============================================================================
class HighPriorityPattern:
    """
    High Priority Pattern: Execute critical queries with maximum resources
    and minimal latency. These queries get preferential treatment.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def configure_high_priority_session(self) -> SparkSession:
        """
        Configure a Spark session optimized for high-priority queries.
        """
        # Create a new session with high-priority configurations
        high_priority_spark = self.spark.newSession()
        
        # Set configurations for high priority
        high_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")
        high_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        high_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
        high_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.scheduler.mode", "FAIR")
        high_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.scheduler.pool", "high_priority_pool")
        
        # Increase memory allocation
        high_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.executor.memory", "4g")
        high_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.driver.memory", "2g")
        
        logger.info("High priority Spark session configured")
        return high_priority_spark
    
    def execute_high_priority_query(self, df, query_name: str):
        """
        Execute a query with high priority settings.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_name: Name of the query for tracking
        """
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Set high priority pool
        self.spark.sparkContext.setLocalProperty("spark.scheduler.pool", "high_priority_pool")
        
        # Execute query with caching for faster subsequent access
        result = df.cache()
        count = result.count()
        
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        logger.info(f"High Priority Query '{query_name}' completed in {execution_time:.2f}s")
        logger.info(f"Result count: {count}")
        
        return result


# ============================================================================
# 2. NORMAL PRIORITY PATTERN
# ============================================================================
class NormalPriorityPattern:
    """
    Normal Priority Pattern: Execute standard queries with balanced resource
    allocation. These queries use default configurations.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def configure_normal_priority_session(self) -> SparkSession:
        """
        Configure a Spark session with normal priority settings.
        """
        normal_priority_spark = self.spark.newSession()
        
        # Set standard configurations
        normal_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "100")
        normal_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        normal_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.scheduler.mode", "FAIR")
        normal_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.scheduler.pool", "normal_priority_pool")
        
        # Standard memory allocation
        normal_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.executor.memory", "2g")
        normal_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.driver.memory", "1g")
        
        logger.info("Normal priority Spark session configured")
        return normal_priority_spark
    
    def execute_normal_priority_query(self, df, query_name: str):
        """
        Execute a query with normal priority settings.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_name: Name of the query for tracking
        """
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Set normal priority pool
        self.spark.sparkContext.setLocalProperty("spark.scheduler.pool", "normal_priority_pool")
        
        # Execute query without aggressive caching
        result = df
        count = result.count()
        
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        logger.info(f"Normal Priority Query '{query_name}' completed in {execution_time:.2f}s")
        logger.info(f"Result count: {count}")
        
        return result


# ============================================================================
# 3. LOW PRIORITY PATTERN
# ============================================================================
class LowPriorityPattern:
    """
    Low Priority Pattern: Execute background/batch queries with minimal
    resource allocation. These queries run when resources are available.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def configure_low_priority_session(self) -> SparkSession:
        """
        Configure a Spark session optimized for low-priority queries.
        """
        low_priority_spark = self.spark.newSession()
        
        # Set configurations for low priority
        low_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "50")
        low_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        low_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.scheduler.mode", "FAIR")
        low_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.scheduler.pool", "low_priority_pool")
        
        # Minimal memory allocation
        low_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.executor.memory", "1g")
        low_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.driver.memory", "512m")
        
        # Enable speculation for long-running tasks
        low_priority_spark.conf.set("spark.speculation", "true")
        
        logger.info("Low priority Spark session configured")
        return low_priority_spark
    
    def execute_low_priority_query(self, df, query_name: str, delay: int = 0):
        """
        Execute a query with low priority settings.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_name: Name of the query for tracking
            delay: Optional delay before execution (seconds)
        """
        if delay > 0:
            logger.info(f"Delaying low priority query '{query_name}' by {delay}s")
            time.sleep(delay)
        
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Set low priority pool
        self.spark.sparkContext.setLocalProperty("spark.scheduler.pool", "low_priority_pool")
        
        # Execute query with lazy evaluation
        result = df
        count = result.count()
        
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        logger.info(f"Low Priority Query '{query_name}' completed in {execution_time:.2f}s")
        logger.info(f"Result count: {count}")
        
        return result


# ============================================================================
# 4. DYNAMIC PRIORITY PATTERN
# ============================================================================
class Priority(Enum):
    """Enumeration for priority levels"""
    HIGH = 1
    MEDIUM = 2
    LOW = 3


class DynamicPriorityPattern:
    """
    Dynamic Priority Pattern: Adjust query priority based on runtime conditions
    such as query complexity, data size, available resources, or SLA requirements.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.high_priority = HighPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.normal_priority = NormalPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.low_priority = LowPriorityPattern(spark)
        
    def analyze_query_characteristics(self, df) -> Dict:
        """
        Analyze query characteristics to determine appropriate priority.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing query characteristics
        """
        # Get estimated data size
        num_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        # Analyze query plan complexity
        plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().logical().toString()
        plan_complexity = len(plan.split('\n'))
        
        characteristics = {
            'num_partitions': num_partitions,
            'plan_complexity': plan_complexity,
            'has_shuffle': 'Exchange' in plan or 'Sort' in plan,
            'has_aggregation': 'Aggregate' in plan
        }
        
        logger.info(f"Query characteristics: {characteristics}")
        return characteristics
    
    def determine_priority(self, characteristics: Dict, user_priority: str = None) -> Priority:
        """
        Determine query priority based on characteristics and user input.
        
        Args:
            characteristics: Query characteristics dictionary
            user_priority: Optional user-specified priority
            
        Returns:
            Priority level
        """
        # User override
        if user_priority:
            priority_map = {
                'high': Priority.HIGH,
                'medium': Priority.MEDIUM,
                'low': Priority.LOW
            }
            return priority_map.get(user_priority.lower(), Priority.MEDIUM)
        
        # Auto-determine based on characteristics
        score = 0
        
        if characteristics['num_partitions'] > 100:
            score += 2
        elif characteristics['num_partitions'] > 50:
            score += 1
            
        if characteristics['plan_complexity'] > 20:
            score += 2
        elif characteristics['plan_complexity'] > 10:
            score += 1
            
        if characteristics['has_shuffle']:
            score += 1
            
        if characteristics['has_aggregation']:
            score += 1
        
        # Determine priority based on score
        if score >= 4:
            return Priority.HIGH
        elif score >= 2:
            return Priority.MEDIUM
        else:
            return Priority.LOW
    
    def execute_dynamic_priority_query(self, df, query_name: str, user_priority: str = None):
        """
        Execute query with dynamically determined priority.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_name: Name of the query
            user_priority: Optional user-specified priority
        """
        # Analyze query
        characteristics = self.analyze_query_characteristics(df)
        
        # Determine priority
        priority = self.determine_priority(characteristics, user_priority)
        
        logger.info(f"Query '{query_name}' assigned priority: {priority.name}")
        
        # Execute with appropriate priority
        if priority == Priority.HIGH:
            return self.high_priority.execute_high_priority_query(df, query_name)
        elif priority == Priority.MEDIUM:
            return self.normal_priority.execute_normal_priority_query(df, query_name)
        else:
            return self.low_priority.execute_low_priority_query(df, query_name)


# ============================================================================
# 5. DEADLINE-BASED PRIORITY PATTERN
# ============================================================================
class DeadlineBasedPriorityPattern:
    """
    Deadline-Based Priority Pattern: Prioritize queries based on their
    execution deadlines. Queries closer to deadline get higher priority.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.query_queue = PriorityQueue()
        self.high_priority = HighPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.normal_priority = NormalPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.low_priority = LowPriorityPattern(spark)
        
    def calculate_priority_score(self, deadline: datetime) -> int:
        """
        Calculate priority score based on deadline.
        Lower score = higher priority.
        
        Args:
            deadline: Query deadline
            
        Returns:
            Priority score
        """
        time_until_deadline = (deadline - datetime.now()).total_seconds()
        
        if time_until_deadline < 0:
            # Overdue - highest priority
            return 0
        elif time_until_deadline < 300:  # Less than 5 minutes
            return 1
        elif time_until_deadline < 1800:  # Less than 30 minutes
            return 2
        elif time_until_deadline < 3600:  # Less than 1 hour
            return 3
        else:
            return 4
    
    def submit_query(self, df, query_name: str, deadline: datetime):
        """
        Submit a query with a deadline to the priority queue.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_name: Name of the query
            deadline: Query execution deadline
        """
        priority_score = self.calculate_priority_score(deadline)
        
        query_info = {
            'df': df,
            'name': query_name,
            'deadline': deadline,
            'submit_time': datetime.now()
        }
        
        self.query_queue.put((priority_score, query_name, query_info))
        
        logger.info(f"Query '{query_name}' submitted with priority score {priority_score}")
        logger.info(f"Deadline: {deadline}, Time until deadline: {(deadline - datetime.now()).total_seconds():.2f}s")
    
    def execute_deadline_based_query(self, query_info: Dict):
        """
        Execute a query based on its deadline priority.
        
        Args:
            query_info: Query information dictionary
        """
        df = query_info['df']
        query_name = query_info['name']
        deadline = query_info['deadline']
        
        time_until_deadline = (deadline - datetime.now()).total_seconds()
        
        logger.info(f"Executing query '{query_name}' with {time_until_deadline:.2f}s until deadline")
        
        # Choose execution strategy based on urgency
        if time_until_deadline < 300:  # Less than 5 minutes
            result = self.high_priority.execute_high_priority_query(df, query_name)
        elif time_until_deadline < 1800:  # Less than 30 minutes
            result = self.normal_priority.execute_normal_priority_query(df, query_name)
        else:
            result = self.low_priority.execute_low_priority_query(df, query_name)
        
        # Check if deadline was met
        completion_time = datetime.now()
        if completion_time <= deadline:
            logger.info(f"✓ Query '{query_name}' completed before deadline")
        else:
            logger.warning(f"✗ Query '{query_name}' missed deadline by {(completion_time - deadline).total_seconds():.2f}s")
        
        return result
    
    def process_queue(self, max_concurrent: int = 3):
        """
        Process queries from the priority queue.
        
        Args:
            max_concurrent: Maximum number of concurrent queries
        """
        logger.info(f"Processing query queue with max {max_concurrent} concurrent queries")
        
        while not self.query_queue.empty():
            priority_score, query_name, query_info = self.query_queue.get()
            
            # Re-calculate priority in case deadline changed
            current_priority = self.calculate_priority_score(query_info['deadline'])
            
            if current_priority != priority_score:
                logger.info(f"Priority changed for '{query_name}': {priority_score} -> {current_priority}")
            
            self.execute_deadline_based_query(query_info)

def setup_fair_scheduler_pools(spark: SparkSession):
    """
    Setup FAIR scheduler pools for different priority levels.
    This would typically be done via fairscheduler.xml configuration.
    
    Args:
        spark: SparkSession instance

def demo_deadline_based_priority_pattern(spark: SparkSession, data: Dict):
    """
    Demonstrate Deadline-Based Priority Pattern usage.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("DEMO 5: DEADLINE-BASED PRIORITY PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    deadline_priority = DeadlineBasedPriorityPattern(spark)
    
    # Submit multiple queries with different deadlines
    now = datetime.now()
    
    # Query 1: Urgent - 2 minutes deadline
    urgent_query = data['sales'].filter(col("sale_amount") > 5000) \
        .groupBy("user_id") \
        .agg(sum("sale_amount").alias("total"))
    
    deadline_priority.submit_query(
        urgent_query,
        "Urgent High-Value Sales",
        now + timedelta(minutes=2)
    )
    
    # Query 2: Normal - 15 minutes deadline
    normal_query = data['products'] \
        .groupBy("category") \
        .agg(count("*").alias("count"))
    
    deadline_priority.submit_query(
        normal_query,
        "Product Category Count",
        now + timedelta(minutes=15)
    )
    
    # Query 3: Low urgency - 1 hour deadline
    low_urgency_query = data['sales'] \
        .join(data['products'], "product_id") \
        .groupBy("category") \
        .agg(sum("sale_amount").alias("total_sales"))
    
    deadline_priority.submit_query(
        low_urgency_query,
        "Category Sales Summary",
        now + timedelta(hours=1)
    )
    
    # Query 4: Overdue - deadline in the past (highest priority)
    overdue_query = data['users'].filter(col("tier") == "Premium")
    
    deadline_priority.submit_query(
        overdue_query,
        "Overdue Premium Report",
        now - timedelta(minutes=5)
    )
    
    # Process the queue
    print("\n--- Processing Query Queue by Deadline Priority ---")
    deadline_priority.process_queue(max_concurrent=2)
    
    print("\n✓ All deadline-based queries processed")

def demo_priority_monitoring(spark: SparkSession):

    class PriorityMonitor:
        """Monitor and track query execution metrics by priority."""
        
        def __init__(self):
            self.metrics = {
                'high': {'count': 0, 'total_time': 0.0, 'queries': []},
                'normal': {'count': 0, 'total_time': 0.0, 'queries': []},
                'low': {'count': 0, 'total_time': 0.0, 'queries': []}
            }
        
        def record_execution(self, priority: str, query_name: str, execution_time: float):
            """Record query execution metrics."""
            self.metrics[priority]['count'] += 1
            self.metrics[priority]['total_time'] += execution_time
            self.metrics[priority]['queries'].append({
                'name': query_name,
                'time': execution_time,
                'timestamp': datetime.now()
            })
        
        def get_statistics(self):
            """Calculate and return execution statistics."""
            stats = {}
            for priority, data in self.metrics.items():
                if data['count'] > 0:
                    stats[priority] = {
                        'total_queries': data['count'],
                        'total_time': data['total_time'],
                        'avg_time': data['total_time'] / data['count'],
                        'queries': data['queries']
                    }
                else:
                    stats[priority] = {
                        'total_queries': 0,
                        'total_time': 0.0,
                        'avg_time': 0.0,
                        'queries': []
                    }
            return stats
        
        def print_report(self):
            """Print monitoring report."""
            stats = self.get_statistics()
            
            print("\n" + "-"*60)
            print("PRIORITY EXECUTION STATISTICS")
            print("-"*60)

class AdaptivePriorityManager:
    """
    Advanced priority manager that adapts based on system load and query patterns.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.high_priority = HighPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.normal_priority = NormalPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.low_priority = LowPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.query_history = []
        self.system_load = 0.5  # 0.0 to 1.0
    
    def update_system_load(self):
        """
        Update system load based on active queries and resources.
        In production, this would query actual cluster metrics.
        """
        # Simulate system load calculation
        active_jobs = len(self.spark.sparkContext.statusTracker().getActiveJobIds())
        self.system_load = min(active_jobs / 10.0, 1.0)
        logger.info(f"Current system load: {self.system_load:.2f}")
    
    def adaptive_execute(self, df, query_name: str, base_priority: str = 'normal'):
        """
        Execute query with adaptive priority based on system load.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_name: Name of the query
            base_priority: Base priority level
        """
        self.update_system_load()
        
        # Adjust priority based on system load
        if self.system_load > 0.8:
            # High load - be more conservative
            if base_priority == 'high':
                adjusted_priority = 'high'
            else:
                adjusted_priority = 'low'
        elif self.system_load < 0.3:
            # Low load - can be more aggressive
            if base_priority == 'low':
                adjusted_priority = 'normal'
            else:
                adjusted_priority = base_priority
        else:
            # Normal load - use base priority
            adjusted_priority = base_priority
        
        logger.info(f"Adaptive execution: {base_priority} -> {adjusted_priority} (load: {self.system_load:.2f})")
        
        # Execute with adjusted priority
        if adjusted_priority == 'high':
            result = self.high_priority.execute_high_priority_query(df, query_name)
        elif adjusted_priority == 'normal':
            result = self.normal_priority.execute_normal_priority_query(df, query_name)
        else:
            result = self.low_priority.execute_low_priority_query(df, query_name)
        
        return result


class PriorityQueueManager:
    """
    Comprehensive queue manager for handling multiple priority levels.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.queues = {
            'high': [],
            'normal': [],
            'low': []
        }
        self.execution_stats = {
            'high': {'executed': 0, 'pending': 0},
            'normal': {'executed': 0, 'pending': 0},
            'low': {'executed': 0, 'pending': 0}
        }
        self.high_priority = HighPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.normal_priority = NormalPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.low_priority = LowPriorityPattern(spark)
    
    def enqueue(self, df, query_name: str, priority: str = 'normal'):
        """
        Add a query to the appropriate priority queue.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_name: Name of the query
            priority: Priority level (high/normal/low)
        """
        query_item = {
            'df': df,
            'name': query_name,
            'enqueue_time': datetime.now(),
            'priority': priority
        }
        
        self.queues[priority].append(query_item)
        self.execution_stats[priority]['pending'] += 1
        
        logger.info(f"Query '{query_name}' enqueued with {priority} priority")
        logger.info(f"Queue sizes - High: {len(self.queues['high'])}, "
                   f"Normal: {len(self.queues['normal'])}, "
                   f"Low: {len(self.queues['low'])}")
    
    def dequeue_next(self) -> tuple:
        """
        Dequeue the next query based on priority.
        
        Returns:
            Tuple of (priority, query_item) or (None, None) if all queues empty
        """
        # Check queues in priority order
        for priority in ['high', 'normal', 'low']:
            if self.queues[priority]:
                query_item = self.queues[priority].pop(0)
                self.execution_stats[priority]['pending'] -= 1
                return priority, query_item
        
        return None, None
    
    def execute_next(self):
        """Execute the next query in the queue."""
        priority, query_item = self.dequeue_next()
        
        if query_item is None:
            logger.info("No queries in queue")
            return None
        
        query_name = query_item['name']
        df = query_item['df']
        wait_time = (datetime.now() - query_item['enqueue_time']).total_seconds()
        
        logger.info(f"Executing {priority} priority query '{query_name}' "
                   f"(waited {wait_time:.2f}s)")
        
        # Execute based on priority
        if priority == 'high':
            result = self.high_priority.execute_high_priority_query(df, query_name)
        elif priority == 'normal':
            result = self.normal_priority.execute_normal_priority_query(df, query_name)
        else:
            result = self.low_priority.execute_low_priority_query(df, query_name)
        
        self.execution_stats[priority]['executed'] += 1
        
        return result
    
    def execute_all(self):
        """Execute all queries in the queue."""
        total_queries = sum(len(q) for q in self.queues.values())
        logger.info(f"Executing {total_queries} queries from queue...")
        
        while any(self.queues.values()):
            self.execute_next()
        
        logger.info("All queries executed")
        self.print_stats()
    
    def print_stats(self):
        """Print execution statistics."""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("QUEUE EXECUTION STATISTICS")
        print("="*60)
        
        for priority in ['high', 'normal', 'low']:
            stats = self.execution_stats[priority]
            print(f"\n{priority.upper()} Priority:")
            print(f"  Executed: {stats['executed']}")
            print(f"  Pending: {stats['pending']}")
            print(f"  Total: {stats['executed'] + stats['pending']}")
        
        print("="*60)


class SLABasedPriorityPattern:
    """
    SLA-Based Priority Pattern: Prioritize queries based on Service Level Agreements.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.sla_config = {
            'platinum': {'max_latency_ms': 1000, 'priority': 'high'},
            'gold': {'max_latency_ms': 5000, 'priority': 'normal'},
            'silver': {'max_latency_ms': 30000, 'priority': 'normal'},
            'bronze': {'max_latency_ms': 60000, 'priority': 'low'}
        }
        self.high_priority = HighPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.normal_priority = NormalPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.low_priority = LowPriorityPattern(spark)
        self.sla_violations = []
    
    def execute_with_sla(self, df, query_name: str, sla_tier: str):
        """
        Execute query according to SLA requirements.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_name: Name of the query
            sla_tier: SLA tier (platinum/gold/silver/bronze)
        """
        if sla_tier not in self.sla_config:
            logger.warning(f"Unknown SLA tier: {sla_tier}, using 'bronze'")
            sla_tier = 'bronze'
        
        sla = self.sla_config[sla_tier]
        priority = sla['priority']
        max_latency = sla['max_latency_ms']
        
        logger.info(f"Executing query '{query_name}' with {sla_tier} SLA "
                   f"(max latency: {max_latency}ms, priority: {priority})")
        
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Execute with appropriate priority
        if priority == 'high':
            result = self.high_priority.execute_high_priority_query(df, query_name)
        elif priority == 'normal':
            result = self.normal_priority.execute_normal_priority_query(df, query_name)
        else:
            result = self.low_priority.execute_low_priority_query(df, query_name)
        
        execution_time_ms = (time.time() - start_time) * 1000
        
        # Check SLA compliance
        if execution_time_ms > max_latency:
            violation = {
                'query': query_name,
                'sla_tier': sla_tier,
                'expected_ms': max_latency,
                'actual_ms': execution_time_ms,
                'timestamp': datetime.now()
            }
            self.sla_violations.append(violation)
            logger.warning(f"⚠ SLA VIOLATION: Query '{query_name}' took {execution_time_ms:.2f}ms "
                         f"(expected < {max_latency}ms)")
        else:
            logger.info(f"✓ SLA MET: Query '{query_name}' completed in {execution_time_ms:.2f}ms")
        
        return result
    
    def get_sla_report(self):
        """Generate SLA compliance report."""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("SLA COMPLIANCE REPORT")
        print("="*60)
        
        if not self.sla_violations:
            print("\n✓ No SLA violations detected")
        else:
            print(f"\n⚠ Total SLA Violations: {len(self.sla_violations)}")
            print("\nViolation Details:")
            for v in self.sla_violations:
                print(f"\n  Query: {v['query']}")
                print(f"  SLA Tier: {v['sla_tier']}")
                print(f"  Expected: < {v['expected_ms']:.2f}ms")
                print(f"  Actual: {v['actual_ms']:.2f}ms")
                print(f"  Overage: {v['actual_ms'] - v['expected_ms']:.2f}ms")
                print(f"  Time: {v['timestamp'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}")
        
        print("="*60)

        sla_manager.execute_with_sla(gold_query, "Gold Tier Query", "gold")
        
        silver_query = data['sales'].groupBy("user_id").agg(sum("sale_amount"))
        sla_manager.execute_with_sla(silver_query, "Silver Tier Query", "silver")
        
        bronze_query = data['sales'].join(data['products'], "product_id") \
            .groupBy("category").agg(sum("sale_amount"))
        sla_manager.execute_with_sla(bronze_query, "Bronze Tier Query", "bronze")
        
        # Generate SLA report
        sla_manager.get_sla_report()
        
        # Performance Comparison
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("DEMO 11: PERFORMANCE COMPARISON ACROSS PRIORITIES")
        print("="*80)
        
        compare_priorities(spark, data)
        
        # Best Practices Summary
        print_best_practices()
        
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Error in demo execution: {str(e)}", exc_info=True)
    
    finally:
        # Cleanup
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("Cleaning up resources...")
        spark.stop()
        print("✓ Spark session stopped")
        print("="*80)


def compare_priorities(spark: SparkSession, data: Dict):
    """
    Compare execution performance across different priority levels.
    """
    print("\nRunning performance comparison...")
    
    # Same query executed with different priorities
    test_query = data['sales'] \
        .join(data['products'], "product_id") \
        .groupBy("category") \
        .agg(
            sum("sale_amount").alias("total_sales"),
            count("*").alias("num_transactions"),
            avg("sale_amount").alias("avg_sale")
        ) \
        .orderBy(desc("total_sales"))
    
    results = {}
    
    # High Priority
    high_priority = HighPriorityPattern(spark)
    start = time.time()
    high_result = high_priority.execute_high_priority_query(test_query, "Comparison - High")
    high_result.count()  # Force execution
    results['high'] = time.time() - start
    
    # Normal Priority
    normal_priority = NormalPriorityPattern(spark)
    start = time.time()
    normal_result = normal_priority.execute_normal_priority_query(test_query, "Comparison - Normal")
    normal_result.count()  # Force execution
    results['normal'] = time.time() - start
    
    # Low Priority
    low_priority = LowPriorityPattern(spark)
    start = time.time()
    low_result = low_priority.execute_low_priority_query(test_query, "Comparison - Low")
    low_result.count()  # Force execution
    results['low'] = time.time() - start
    
    # Print comparison
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("PERFORMANCE COMPARISON RESULTS")
    print("-"*60)
    print(f"High Priority:   {results['high']:.3f}s")
    print(f"Normal Priority: {results['normal']:.3f}s")
    print(f"Low Priority:    {results['low']:.3f}s")
    print("-"*60)
    
    # Calculate improvements
    if results['normal'] > 0:
        high_improvement = ((results['normal'] - results['high']) / results['normal']) * 100
        print(f"\nHigh vs Normal: {high_improvement:+.1f}% performance difference")
    
    if results['low'] > 0:
        low_degradation = ((results['low'] - results['normal']) / results['normal']) * 100
        print(f"Low vs Normal:  {low_degradation:+.1f}% performance difference")
    
    print()


def print_best_practices():
    """
    Print best practices for using priority patterns.
    """
    best_practices = """
    
================================================================================
BEST PRACTICES FOR QUERY EXECUTION PRIORITY PATTERNS
================================================================================

1. HIGH PRIORITY PATTERN
   ✓ Use for: Real-time dashboards, critical alerts, interactive queries
   ✓ Characteristics: Low latency, high resource allocation
   ✓ Considerations: Limited concurrency, expensive resources
   ✗ Avoid for: Batch jobs, background tasks, non-critical reports

2. NORMAL PRIORITY PATTERN
   ✓ Use for: Standard reports, scheduled jobs, regular analytics
   ✓ Characteristics: Balanced resources, moderate latency
   ✓ Considerations: Default choice for most workloads
   ✗ Avoid for: Time-critical operations, background maintenance

3. LOW PRIORITY PATTERN
   ✓ Use for: Batch processing, data archival, maintenance tasks
   ✓ Characteristics: Minimal resources, can tolerate delays
   ✓ Considerations: May be preempted, longer execution times
   ✗ Avoid for: User-facing queries, time-sensitive operations

4. DYNAMIC PRIORITY PATTERN
   ✓ Use for: Mixed workloads, auto-scaling environments
   ✓ Characteristics: Adaptive resource allocation, intelligent scheduling
   ✓ Considerations: Requires monitoring, complexity in tuning
   ✗ Avoid for: Simple workloads, predictable patterns

5. DEADLINE-BASED PRIORITY PATTERN
   ✓ Use for: SLA-driven applications, scheduled reports
   ✓ Characteristics: Time-aware scheduling, deadline compliance
   ✓ Considerations: Requires accurate time estimation
   ✗ Avoid for: Unpredictable query durations, ad-hoc queries

GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS
================================================================================

Resource Management:
- Configure fair scheduler pools in fairscheduler.xml
- Set appropriate memory and CPU allocations per priority
- Monitor resource utilization and adjust as needed
- Use separate Spark sessions for different priorities

Query Optimization:
- Profile queries before assigning priority
- Cache frequently accessed data for high-priority queries
- Use adaptive query execution (AQE) for all priorities
- Partition data appropriately for better performance

Monitoring:
- Track query execution times by priority
- Monitor SLA compliance and violations
- Set up alerts for priority queue backlogs
- Analyze resource utilization patterns

Priority Assignment:
- Define clear criteria for priority levels
- Document priority assignment policies
- Review and adjust priorities regularly
- Avoid priority inflation (everything as high)

Configuration Tips:
================================================================================

High Priority Pool:
  <pool name="high_priority_pool">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>3</weight>
    <minShare>2</minShare>
  </pool>

Normal Priority Pool:
  <pool name="normal_priority_pool">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>2</weight>
    <minShare>1</minShare>
  </pool>

Low Priority Pool:
  <pool name="low_priority_pool">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>1</weight>
    <minShare>0</minShare>
  </pool>

Spark Configuration:
- spark.scheduler.mode = FAIR
- spark.sql.adaptive.enabled = true
- spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled = true
- spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled = true

Common Pitfalls to Avoid:
================================================================================

1. Over-prioritization: Not everything can be high priority
2. Under-monitoring: Track actual vs expected performance
3. Static priorities: Adapt to changing workload patterns
4. Resource contention: Ensure fair sharing across priorities
5. Missing SLAs: Set realistic deadlines and monitor compliance
6. Ignoring query optimization: Priority doesn't replace good design
7. Poor queue management: Implement proper backlog handling
8. Lack of documentation: Document priority policies clearly

Performance Tuning:
================================================================================

For High Priority:
- Increase executor memory: spark.executor.memory = 4g
- Reduce shuffle partitions for small data
- Enable broadcast joins: spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold
- Use aggressive caching strategies

For Normal Priority:
- Balance resources with other priorities
- Use standard shuffle partition count
- Enable adaptive query execution
- Moderate caching based on reuse patterns

For Low Priority:
- Minimize resource allocation
- Increase shuffle partitions for large data
- Enable speculation for long tasks
- Defer non-essential operations

Scalability Considerations:
================================================================================

- Design for horizontal scaling
- Use partition-aware operations
- Implement backpressure mechanisms
- Monitor and adjust pool weights
- Consider cluster autoscaling
- Plan for peak load scenarios

================================================================================
"""
    print(best_practices)


def create_production_example():
    """

    example_code = '''
# Production Example: E-commerce Analytics Platform
# ===================================================

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

class EcommerceQueryManager:
    """
    Production-ready query manager for e-commerce analytics.
    Handles different query types with appropriate priorities.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.spark = SparkSession.builder \\
            .appName("EcommerceAnalytics") \\
            .config("spark.scheduler.mode", "FAIR") \\
            .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \\
            .getOrCreate()
        
        # Initialize priority patterns
        self.high_priority = HighPriorityPattern(self.spark)
        self.normal_priority = NormalPriorityPattern(self.spark)
        self.low_priority = LowPriorityPattern(self.spark)
        self.deadline_priority = DeadlineBasedPriorityPattern(self.spark)
        self.sla_priority = SLABasedPriorityPattern(self.spark)
    
    def execute_realtime_dashboard(self, data):
        """Execute real-time dashboard queries (HIGH priority)"""
        query = data.filter(col("timestamp") > current_timestamp() - expr("INTERVAL 5 MINUTES")) \\
            .groupBy("product_category") \\
            .agg(
                sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue"),
                count("order_id").alias("order_count")
            )
        
        return self.high_priority.execute_high_priority_query(
            query, "Realtime Dashboard"
        )
    
    def execute_daily_report(self, data, report_date):
        """Execute daily sales report (NORMAL priority)"""
        query = data.filter(col("date") == report_date) \\
            .groupBy("region", "product_category") \\
            .agg(
                sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue"),
                count("order_id").alias("total_orders"),
                avg("order_value").alias("avg_order_value")
            )
        
        # Set deadline for end of business day
        deadline = datetime.combine(report_date, datetime.max.time())
        
        self.deadline_priority.submit_query(
            query, f"Daily Report {report_date}", deadline
        )
    
    def execute_monthly_aggregation(self, data, month):
        """Execute monthly aggregation (LOW priority)"""
        query = data.filter(col("month") == month) \\
            .groupBy("product_id") \\
            .agg(
                sum("quantity").alias("total_quantity"),
                sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue")
            )
        
        return self.low_priority.execute_low_priority_query(
            query, f"Monthly Aggregation {month}"
        )
    
    def execute_customer_query(self, data, customer_tier):
        """Execute customer query based on tier (SLA-based)"""
        query = data.filter(col("customer_tier") == customer_tier) \\
            .groupBy("customer_id") \\
            .agg(
                sum("purchase_amount").alias("total_spent"),
                count("order_id").alias("order_count")
            )
        
        # Map customer tier to SLA tier
        sla_mapping = {
            "platinum": "platinum",
            "gold": "gold",
            "silver": "silver",
            "regular": "bronze"
        }
        
        sla_tier = sla_mapping.get(customer_tier, "bronze")
        
        return self.sla_priority.execute_with_sla(
            query, f"Customer Analysis - {customer_tier}", sla_tier
        )

# Usage
manager = EcommerceQueryManager()

# High priority: Real-time dashboard
realtime_data = manager.execute_realtime_dashboard(sales_data)

# Normal priority with deadline: Daily report
manager.execute_daily_report(sales_data, date.today())

# Low priority: Monthly batch job
monthly_data = manager.execute_monthly_aggregation(sales_data, "2024-01")

# SLA-based: Customer analysis
platinum_customers = manager.execute_customer_query(sales_data, "platinum")
'''
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PRODUCTION EXAMPLE: E-COMMERCE ANALYTICS PLATFORM")
