─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

spark = SparkSession.builder \\
    .appName("DataQualityValidation") \\
    .getOrCreate()

def validate_and_write(df, output_path, quality_path):
    # Data quality checks
    total_records = df.count()
    
    quality_metrics = {
        'total_records': total_records,
        'null_checks': {},
        'duplicate_checks': {},
        'range_checks': {}
    }
    
    # Check for nulls in critical columns
    critical_columns = ['id', 'amount', 'date']
    for col_name in critical_columns:
        null_count = df.filter(col(col_name).isNull()).count()
        quality_metrics['null_checks'][col_name] = null_count
        if null_count > 0:
            print(f"⚠ Warning: {null_count} null values in {col_name}")
    
    # Check for duplicates
    duplicate_count = total_records - df.dropDuplicates(['id']).count()
    quality_metrics['duplicate_checks']['id'] = duplicate_count
    if duplicate_count > 0:
        print(f"⚠ Warning: {duplicate_count} duplicate IDs found")
    
    # Range validation
    if 'amount' in df.columns:
        negative_amounts = df.filter(col('amount') < 0).count()
        quality_metrics['range_checks']['negative_amounts'] = negative_amounts
        if negative_amounts > 0:
            print(f"⚠ Warning: {negative_amounts} negative amounts found")
    
    # Separate good and bad records
    valid_df = df.filter(
        col('id').isNotNull() &
        col('amount').isNotNull() &
        (col('amount') >= 0)
    )
    
    invalid_df = df.subtract(valid_df)
    
    # Write valid records
    valid_df.write \\
        .format("parquet") \\
        .mode("overwrite") \\
        .save(output_path)
    
    # Write invalid records for review
    if invalid_df.count() > 0:
        invalid_df.write \\
            .format("parquet") \\
            .mode("overwrite") \\
            .save(f"{output_path}_invalid")
    
    # Write quality metrics
    quality_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        [(str(quality_metrics), current_timestamp())],
        ["metrics", "check_timestamp"]
    )
    quality_df.write \\
        .format("parquet") \\
        .mode("append") \\
        .save(quality_path)
    
    print(f"✓ Validated {valid_df.count()} valid records")
    print(f"✓ Found {invalid_df.count()} invalid records")
    
    return valid_df, invalid_df

# Example usage
df = spark.read.parquet("/input/data")
valid_df, invalid_df = validate_and_write(
    df,
    "/output/valid_data",
    "/output/quality_metrics"
)

## Common Commands Reference:

```python
# ============= READING =============
# Parquet
df = spark.read.parquet("/path/to/data")
df = spark.read.format("parquet").load("/path")

# Avro
df = spark.read.format("avro").load("/path")

# ORC
df = spark.read.orc("/path")

# JSON
df = spark.read.json("/path")

# ============= WRITING =============
# Basic write
df.write.format("parquet").save("/path")

# With options
df.write \
    .format("parquet") \
    .option("compression", "snappy") \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .save("/path")

# With partitioning
df.write \
    .partitionBy("year", "month") \
    .parquet("/path")

# ============= OPTIMIZATION =============
# Column pruning
df.select("col1", "col2").show()

# Predicate pushdown
df.filter(col("amount") > 1000).count()

# Coalesce files
df.coalesce(10).write.parquet("/path")

# Repartition
df.repartition(100, "key_column") \
    .write.parquet("/path")

# ============= CONFIGURATION =============
# Enable vectorized reader
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.parquet.enableVectorizedReader", "true")

# Set compression
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec", "snappy")

# Ignore corrupt files
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.files.ignoreCorruptFiles", "true")

# Schema merging
df = spark.read \
    .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
    .parquet("/path")
```

## Troubleshooting Quick Reference:

```python
# Issue: Schema mismatch
# Solution:
df = spark.read.option("mergeSchema", "true").parquet("/path")

# Issue: Too many small files
# Solution:
df.coalesce(10).write.parquet("/path")

# Issue: Out of memory
# Solution:
df.select("needed_cols_only").filter(...).show()

# Issue: Slow writes
# Solution:
df.repartition(200).write \
    .option("compression", "snappy") \
    .parquet("/path")

# Issue: Partition pruning not working
# Solution:
df.filter(col("partition_col") == "value")  # Use exact match
```

```python
# ============================================================================
# SCENARIO 1: REAL-TIME ANALYTICS PLATFORM
# ============================================================================

class RealTimeAnalyticsPlatform:
    """
    Complete implementation for real-time analytics using hybrid storage
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.base_path = "/analytics_platform"
    
    def setup_streaming_pipeline(self):
        """Setup complete streaming to batch pipeline"""
        
        # Speed Layer: Real-time ingestion (Avro)
        streaming_query = self.spark.readStream \
            .format("kafka") \
            .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \
            .option("subscribe", "user_events") \
            .load() \
            .selectExpr("CAST(value AS STRING) as json_data") \
            .select(from_json(col("json_data"), self.get_event_schema()).alias("data")) \
            .select("data.*") \
            .writeStream \
            .format("avro") \
            .option("path", f"{self.base_path}/speed_layer") \
            .option("checkpointLocation", f"{self.base_path}/checkpoints/speed") \
            .trigger(processingTime='10 seconds') \
            .start()
        
        return streaming_query
    
    def run_batch_aggregation(self):
        """Batch layer: Hourly aggregation to Parquet"""
        
        from datetime import datetime, timedelta
        
        # Read last hour of data from speed layer
        current_hour = datetime.now().replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
        last_hour = current_hour - timedelta(hours=1)
        
        speed_data = self.spark.read \
            .format("avro") \
            .load(f"{self.base_path}/speed_layer") \
            .filter(
                (col("timestamp") >= last_hour) & 
                (col("timestamp") < current_hour)
            )
        
        # Aggregate
        aggregated = speed_data.groupBy(
            "user_id",
            "event_type",
            window("timestamp", "1 hour").alias("time_window")
        ).agg(
            count("*").alias("event_count"),
            countDistinct("session_id").alias("unique_sessions"),
            avg("duration").alias("avg_duration"),
            sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue")
        )
        
        # Write to batch layer (Parquet)
        aggregated.write \
            .format("parquet") \
            .option("compression", "snappy") \
            .partitionBy("event_type") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(f"{self.base_path}/batch_layer/hourly_aggregates")
        
        print(f"✓ Aggregated data for hour: {current_hour}")
        
        return aggregated
    
    def create_serving_layer(self):
        """Serving layer: Optimized for queries"""
        
        # Read from batch layer
        batch_data = self.spark.read.parquet(
            f"{self.base_path}/batch_layer/hourly_aggregates"
        )
        
        # Create materialized views for common queries
        
        # View 1: Daily user metrics
        daily_metrics = batch_data.groupBy(
            "user_id",
            to_date("time_window.start").alias("date")
        ).agg(
            sum("event_count").alias("daily_events"),
            sum("unique_sessions").alias("daily_sessions"),
            sum("total_revenue").alias("daily_revenue")
        )
        
        daily_metrics.write \
            .format("parquet") \
            .option("compression", "zstd") \
            .partitionBy("date") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .save(f"{self.base_path}/serving_layer/daily_metrics")
        
        # View 2: Event type trends
        event_trends = batch_data.groupBy(
            "event_type",
            to_date("time_window.start").alias("date")
        ).agg(
            sum("event_count").alias("total_events"),
            avg("avg_duration").alias("avg_duration")
        )
        
        event_trends.write \
            .format("parquet") \
            .option("compression", "zstd") \
            .partitionBy("event_type") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .save(f"{self.base_path}/serving_layer/event_trends")
        
        print("✓ Serving layer updated")
    
    def query_unified_view(self, user_id, start_date, end_date):
        """Query across all layers for complete view"""
        
        # Real-time data (last few hours)
        realtime_df = self.spark.read \
            .format("avro") \
            .load(f"{self.base_path}/speed_layer") \
            .filter(col("user_id") == user_id) \
            .filter(col("timestamp") >= start_date)
        
        # Historical data
        historical_df = self.spark.read \
            .parquet(f"{self.base_path}/serving_layer/daily_metrics") \
            .filter(col("user_id") == user_id) \
            .filter(
                (col("date") >= start_date) & 
                (col("date") < end_date)
            )
        
        return realtime_df, historical_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def get_event_schema():
        """Define event schema"""
        return StructType([
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("session_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("event_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("duration", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("revenue", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("properties", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
        ])


# ============================================================================
# SCENARIO 2: MULTI-TENANT DATA LAKE
# ============================================================================

class MultiTenantDataLake:
    """
    Data lake implementation with tenant isolation and format optimization
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.base_path = "/data_lake"
    
    def ingest_tenant_data(self, tenant_id, source_df, data_classification):
        """
        Ingest data with appropriate format based on classification
        
        Classifications:
        - hot: Frequently accessed, use Parquet + Snappy
        - warm: Occasionally accessed, use Parquet + ZSTD
        - cold: Rarely accessed, use Parquet + GZIP
        - streaming: Real-time data, use Avro
        """
        
        tenant_path = f"{self.base_path}/tenants/{tenant_id}"
        
        # Add metadata
        enriched_df = source_df \
            .withColumn("tenant_id", lit(tenant_id)) \
            .withColumn("ingestion_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("data_classification", lit(data_classification))
        
        # Choose format and compression based on classification
        format_config = {
            'hot': {'format': 'parquet', 'compression': 'snappy'},
            'warm': {'format': 'parquet', 'compression': 'zstd'},
            'cold': {'format': 'parquet', 'compression': 'gzip'},
            'streaming': {'format': 'avro', 'compression': 'snappy'}
        }
        
        config = format_config.get(data_classification, format_config['warm'])
        
        # Write with appropriate settings
        enriched_df.write \
            .format(config['format']) \
            .option("compression", config['compression']) \
            .partitionBy("data_classification", "ingestion_date") \
            .mode("append") \
            .save(f"{tenant_path}/raw_data")
        
        print(f"✓ Ingested data for tenant {tenant_id} as {data_classification}")
        
        # Update catalog
        self._update_catalog(tenant_id, data_classification, enriched_df.count())
    
    def implement_data_lifecycle(self, tenant_id):
        """Implement automated data lifecycle management"""
        
        from datetime import datetime, timedelta
        
        tenant_path = f"{self.base_path}/tenants/{tenant_id}/raw_data"
        
        # Read all data
        all_data = self.spark.read.parquet(tenant_path)
        
        # Define age thresholds
        now = datetime.now()
        hot_threshold = now - timedelta(days=30)
        warm_threshold = now - timedelta(days=90)
        
        # Reclassify data based on age
        
        # Hot data (< 30 days)
        hot_data = all_data.filter(col("ingestion_timestamp") >= hot_threshold)
        if hot_data.count() > 0:
            hot_data.write \
                .format("parquet") \
                .option("compression", "snappy") \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .save(f"{tenant_path}_hot")
        
        # Warm data (30-90 days)
        warm_data = all_data.filter(
            (col("ingestion_timestamp") < hot_threshold) &
            (col("ingestion_timestamp") >= warm_threshold)
        )
        if warm_data.count() > 0:
            warm_data.write \
                .format("parquet") \
                .option("compression", "zstd") \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .save(f"{tenant_path}_warm")
        
        # Cold data (> 90 days)
        cold_data = all_data.filter(col("ingestion_timestamp") < warm_threshold)
        if cold_data.count() > 0:
            cold_data.write \
                .format("parquet") \
                .option("compression", "gzip") \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .save(f"{tenant_path}_cold")
        
        print(f"✓ Lifecycle management completed for tenant {tenant_id}")
        print(f"  Hot: {hot_data.count()} records")
        print(f"  Warm: {warm_data.count()} records")
        print(f"  Cold: {cold_data.count()} records")
    
    def query_with_performance_tier(self, tenant_id, query_date, performance_tier='auto'):
        """
        Query data with automatic tier selection for optimal performance
        """
        
        tenant_path = f"{self.base_path}/tenants/{tenant_id}"
        
        if performance_tier == 'auto':
            # Automatically select tier based on query date
            from datetime import datetime, timedelta
            age_days = (datetime.now() - query_date).days
            
            if age_days <= 30:
                tier = 'hot'
            elif age_days <= 90:
                tier = 'warm'
            else:
                tier = 'cold'
        else:
            tier = performance_tier
        
        # Read from appropriate tier
        data_path = f"{tenant_path}_raw_data_{tier}"
        
        try:
            df = self.spark.read.parquet(data_path) \

class MLFeatureStore:

    def create_feature_group(self, feature_group_name, features_df, 
                            primary_key, event_time_col):
        """
        Create a feature group with optimized storage
        
        Uses Parquet with:
        - Partitioning by date for time-travel queries
        - Z-ordering simulation for efficient point lookups
        - Snappy compression for balance
        """
        
        feature_path = f"{self.base_path}/features/{feature_group_name}"
        
        # Add metadata
        features_with_meta = features_df \
            .withColumn("feature_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("feature_group", lit(feature_group_name)) \
            .withColumn("partition_date", to_date(col(event_time_col)))
        
        # Optimize for both point lookups and range scans
        optimized_df = features_with_meta \
            .repartition(50, primary_key) \
            .sortWithinPartitions(primary_key, event_time_col)
        
        # Write features
        optimized_df.write \
            .format("parquet") \
            .option("compression", "snappy") \
            .partitionBy("partition_date") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .save(feature_path)

            features_df.schema,

            .filter(col("rank") == 1) \

        return latest_features

"""
Purpose: Verify data integrity using checksums (CRC32, simple sum)
Use Case: File transfer validation, data transmission verification
"""

class ChecksumVerificationPattern:
    """
    Implements checksum-based data integrity verification
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_sample_data():
        """Create sample transaction data"""
        data = [
            (1, "TXN001", 100.50, "2024-01-01", "COMPLETED"),
            (2, "TXN002", 250.75, "2024-01-01", "COMPLETED"),
            (3, "TXN003", 175.25, "2024-01-02", "COMPLETED"),
            (4, "TXN004", 300.00, "2024-01-02", "COMPLETED"),
            (5, "TXN005", 450.80, "2024-01-03", "COMPLETED"),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("transaction_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("amount", StringType(), False),
            StructField("date", StringType(), False),
            StructField("status", StringType(), False)
        ])
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    @staticmethod
    def calculate_row_checksum(df):
        """
        Calculate CRC32 checksum for each row
        """
        # Concatenate all columns into a single string
        df_with_checksum = df.withColumn(
            "row_data",
            concat_ws("|", *[col(c).cast("string") for c in df.columns])
        ).withColumn(
            "crc32_checksum",
            crc32(col("row_data"))
        ).withColumn(
            "xxhash_checksum",
            xxhash64(col("row_data"))
        )
        
        return df_with_checksum
    
    @staticmethod
    def calculate_column_checksum(df, column_name):
        """
        Calculate checksum for a specific column
        """
        return df.withColumn(
            f"{column_name}_checksum",
            crc32(col(column_name).cast("string"))
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def verify_data_integrity(original_df, received_df):
        """
        Verify data integrity by comparing checksums
        """
        # Calculate checksums for both datasets
        original_with_checksum = ChecksumVerificationPattern.calculate_row_checksum(original_df)
        received_with_checksum = ChecksumVerificationPattern.calculate_row_checksum(received_df)
        
        # Join and compare
        comparison = original_with_checksum.alias("orig").join(
            received_with_checksum.alias("recv"),
            col("orig.id") == col("recv.id"),
            "full_outer"
        ).select(
            coalesce(col("orig.id"), col("recv.id")).alias("id"),
            col("orig.crc32_checksum").alias("original_checksum"),
            col("recv.crc32_checksum").alias("received_checksum"),
            when(
                col("orig.crc32_checksum") == col("recv.crc32_checksum"), 
                lit("VALID")
            ).when(
                col("orig.crc32_checksum").isNull(), 
                lit("MISSING_IN_ORIGINAL")
            ).when(
                col("recv.crc32_checksum").isNull(), 
                lit("MISSING_IN_RECEIVED")
            ).otherwise(
                lit("CORRUPTED")
            ).alias("integrity_status")
        )
        
        return comparison
    
    @staticmethod
    def calculate_batch_checksum(df):
        """
        Calculate overall batch checksum for the entire dataset
        """
        # Calculate checksum for entire dataset
        batch_checksum = df.agg(
            _sum(crc32(concat_ws("|", *[col(c).cast("string") for c in df.columns]))).alias("batch_checksum"),
            count("*").alias("record_count")
        )
        
        return batch_checksum

"""
Purpose: Use cryptographic hash functions (MD5, SHA-256) for data integrity
Use Case: Secure data verification, tamper detection, data deduplication
"""

class HashVerificationPattern:
    """
    Implements cryptographic hash-based data integrity verification
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_sample_data():
        """Create sample user data"""
        data = [
            (1, "john.doe@email.com", "John Doe", "123 Main St", "555-1234"),
            (2, "jane.smith@email.com", "Jane Smith", "456 Oak Ave", "555-5678"),
            (3, "bob.jones@email.com", "Bob Jones", "789 Pine Rd", "555-9012"),
            (4, "alice.wilson@email.com", "Alice Wilson", "321 Elm St", "555-3456"),
            (5, "charlie.brown@email.com", "Charlie Brown", "654 Maple Dr", "555-7890"),
        ]
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "email", "name", "address", "phone"])
    
    @staticmethod
    def calculate_hash(df, hash_type="sha256", columns=None):
        """
        Calculate cryptographic hash for specified columns
        hash_type: md5, sha1, sha256, sha512
        """
        if columns is None:
            columns = df.columns
        
        # Concatenate columns
        row_data = concat_ws("|", *[col(c).cast("string") for c in columns])
        
        if hash_type.lower() == "md5":
            return df.withColumn("hash_value", md5(row_data))
        elif hash_type.lower() in ["sha256", "sha2"]:
            return df.withColumn("hash_value", sha2(row_data, 256))
        elif hash_type.lower() == "sha512":
            return df.withColumn("hash_value", sha2(row_data, 512))
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported hash type: {hash_type}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def calculate_column_hashes(df, sensitive_columns):
        """
        Calculate individual hashes for sensitive columns
        """
        result_df = df
        for column in sensitive_columns:
            result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                f"{column}_hash_md5",
                md5(col(column))
            ).withColumn(
                f"{column}_hash_sha256",
                sha2(col(column), 256)
            )
        
        return result_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def detect_duplicates_by_hash(df, columns_to_check):
        """
        Detect duplicate records using hash comparison
        """
        # Calculate hash for specified columns
        df_with_hash = HashVerificationPattern.calculate_hash(
            df, 
            hash_type="sha256", 
            columns=columns_to_check
        )
        
        # Find duplicates
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("hash_value")
        
        duplicates = df_with_hash.withColumn(
            "duplicate_count",
            count("*").over(window_spec)
        ).withColumn(
            "is_duplicate",
            when(col("duplicate_count") > 1, lit(True)).otherwise(lit(False))
        )
        
        return duplicates
    
    @staticmethod
    def verify_hash_integrity(df, expected_hash_column, columns_to_verify):
        """
        Verify data integrity by comparing calculated hash with expected hash
        """
        # Calculate current hash
        df_with_current_hash = HashVerificationPattern.calculate_hash(
            df,
            hash_type="sha256",
            columns=columns_to_verify
        )
        
        # Compare with expected hash
        verification = df_with_current_hash.withColumn(
            "hash_match",
            col("hash_value") == col(expected_hash_column)
        ).withColumn(
            "verification_status",
            when(col("hash_match"), lit("VERIFIED"))
            .otherwise(lit("TAMPERED"))
        )
        
        return verification
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_hmac_signature(df, secret_key, columns):
        """
        Create HMAC signature for enhanced security
        """
        def calculate_hmac(data):
            if data is None:
                return None
            signature = hmac.new(
                secret_key.encode(),
                data.encode(),
                hashlib.sha256
            )
            return signature.hexdigest()
        
        hmac_udf = udf(calculate_hmac, StringType())
        
        row_data = concat_ws("|", *[col(c).cast("string") for c in columns])
        
        return df.withColumn("hmac_signature", hmac_udf(row_data))

"""

Use Case: Non-repudiation, data authenticity, audit trails

class SignatureVerificationPattern:
    """
    Implements digital signature verification for data integrity
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_sample_data():
        """Create sample transaction data with signatures"""
        data = [
            (1, "TXN001", "USER001", 1000.00, "2024-01-01 10:00:00", None),
            (2, "TXN002", "USER002", 2500.50, "2024-01-01 11:30:00", None),
            (3, "TXN003", "USER001", 750.25, "2024-01-02 09:15:00", None),
            (4, "TXN004", "USER003", 3200.00, "2024-01-02 14:45:00", None),
            (5, "TXN005", "USER002", 1800.75, "2024-01-03 16:20:00", None),
        ]
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(
            data, 
            ["id", "transaction_id", "user_id", "amount", "timestamp", "signature"]
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_signature(df, key_column, data_columns, secret_key="default_secret"):
        """
        Generate digital signature for each record
        """
        def create_signature(key, *values):
            # Combine key and values
            data_str = f"{key}|" + "|".join([str(v) if v is not None else "" for v in values])
            
            # Create HMAC signature
            signature = hmac.new(
                secret_key.encode(),
                data_str.encode(),
                hashlib.sha256
            )
            return signature.hexdigest()
        
        signature_udf = udf(create_signature, StringType())
        
        return df.withColumn(
            "signature",
            signature_udf(col(key_column), *[col(c) for c in data_columns])
        )

    def verify_signature(df, key_column, data_columns, signature_column, secret_key="default_secret"):
        """

        """

            data_str = f"{key}|" +

            return signature == expected_signature
        
        verify_udf = udf(verify_sig, BooleanType())
        
        return df.withColumn(
            "signature_valid",
            verify_udf(col(key_column), col(signature_column), *[col(c) for c in data_columns])
        ).withColumn(
            "verification_status",
            when(col("signature_valid"), lit("AUTHENTIC"))

    @staticmethod
    def create_composite_signature(df, columns_to_sign):
        """

        """
        def composite_sig(*values):
            # Include timestamp in signature
            current_time = datetime.now().isoformat()
            data_str = "|".join([str(v) if v is not None else "" for v in values])
            data_with_meta = f"{data_str}|{current_time}"
            
            signature = hashlib.sha256(data_with_meta.encode()).hexdigest()
            return f"{signature}:{current_time}"
        
        composite_udf = udf(composite_sig, StringType())
        
        return df.withColumn(

            composite_udf(*[col(c) for c in columns_to_sign])
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def verify_signature_chain(df, id_column, signature_column):

        window_spec = Window.orderBy(id_column)
        
        # Get previous signature

        chain_verify_udf = udf(verify_chain, BooleanType())
        
        return df_with_chain.withColumn(

                col(id_column),
                col(signature_column),
                col("previous_signature")
            )
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_batch_signature(df, columns):
        """
        Generate signature for entire batch
        """
        # Collect all signatures
        signatures = df.select(
            concat_ws("|", *[col(c).cast("string") for c in columns]).alias("row_data")

        # Create batch signature
        batch_signature = hashlib.sha256(signatures.encode()).hexdigest()
        
        return batch_signature

"""
Purpose: Ensure data consistency across multiple dimensions
Use Case: Data quality validation, cross-field validation, business rule enforcement
"""

class ConsistencyCheckPattern:
    """
    Implements comprehensive data consistency checking
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_sample_data():
        """Create sample order data with potential inconsistencies"""
        data = [
            (1, "ORD001", 5, 10.00, 50.00, "2024-01-01", "2024-01-05", "SHIPPED"),
            (2, "ORD002", 3, 25.50, 76.50, "2024-01-02", "2024-01-06", "DELIVERED"),
            (3, "ORD003", 10, 15.00, 140.00, "2024-01-03", "2024-01-07", "SHIPPED"),  # Inconsistent total
            (4, "ORD004", 2, 30.00, 60.00, "2024-01-10", "2024-01-08", "DELIVERED"),  # Delivery before order
            (5, "ORD005", 0, 20.00, 0.00, "2024-01-05", "2024-01-09", "CANCELLED"),  # Zero quantity
            (6, "ORD006", 7, 12.50, 87.50, "2024-01-06", "2024-01-10", "PROCESSING"),
            (7, "ORD007", -2, 15.00, -30.00, "2024-01-07", None, "PENDING"),  # Negative quantity
        ]
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(
            data,
            ["id", "order_id", "quantity", "unit_price", "total_amount", 
             "order_date", "delivery_date", "status"]
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_calculation_consistency(df):
        """
        Check if calculated fields are consistent
        """
        return df.withColumn(
            "expected_total",
            col("quantity") * col("unit_price")
        ).withColumn(
            "total_consistent",
            (col("total_amount") - col("expected_total")).between(-0.01, 0.01)
        ).withColumn(
            "calculation_status",
            when(col("total_consistent"), lit("CONSISTENT"))
            .otherwise(lit("INCONSISTENT"))
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_temporal_consistency(df, start_date_col, end_date_col):
        """
        Check temporal/date consistency
        """
        return df.withColumn(
            "date_consistent",
            when(col(end_date_col).isNull(), lit(True))
            .when(col(start_date_col) <= col(end_date_col), lit(True))
            .otherwise(lit(False))
        ).withColumn(
            "temporal_status",
            when(col("date_consistent"), lit("VALID"))
            .otherwise(lit("INVALID_DATE_ORDER"))
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_value_range_consistency(df, column_rules):
        """
        Check if values are within expected ranges
        column_rules: dict with column names and (min, max) tuples
        """
        result_df = df
        
        for column, (min_val, max_val) in column_rules.items():
            result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                f"{column}_in_range",
                col(column).between(min_val, max_val)
            )
        
        # Create overall range consistency flag
        range_columns = [f"{col}_in_range" for col in column_rules.keys()]
        
        result_df = result_df.withColumn(
            "range_consistent",
            when(
                sum([when(col(c), 0).otherwise(1) for c in range_columns]) == 0,
                lit(True)
            ).otherwise(lit(False))
        )
        
        return result_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_state_transition_consistency(df, status_column, valid_transitions):
        """
        Check if status transitions are valid
        valid_transitions: dict of valid state transitions
        """
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("order_id").orderBy("id")
        
        df_with_prev = df.withColumn(
            "previous_status",
            col(status_column).over(window_spec.rowsBetween(-1, -1))
        )
        
        def is_valid_transition(current, previous):
            if previous is None:
                return True
            return current in valid_transitions.get(previous, [])
        
        transition_udf = udf(is_valid_transition, BooleanType())
        
        return df_with_prev.withColumn(
            "transition_valid",
            transition_udf(col(status_column), col("previous_status"))
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_cross_field_consistency(df, consistency_rules):
        """
        Check consistency based on business rules involving multiple fields
        consistency_rules: list of tuples (rule_name, condition)
        """
        result_df = df
        
        for rule_name, condition in consistency_rules:
            result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                f"rule_{rule_name}",
                when(condition, lit(True)).otherwise(lit(False))
            )
        
        # Overall consistency
        rule_columns = [f"rule_{rule[0]}" for rule in consistency_rules]
        result_df = result_df.withColumn(
            "all_rules_passed",
            when(
                sum([when(col(c), 0).otherwise(1) for c in rule_columns]) == 0,
                lit(True)
            ).otherwise(lit(False))
        )
        
        return result_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_consistency_report(df, check_columns):
        """
        Generate comprehensive consistency report
        """
        report = df.agg(
            count("*").alias("total_records"),
            *[_sum(when(col(c), 1).otherwise(0)).alias(f"{c}_pass_count") 
              for c in check_columns]
        )
        
        # Calculate pass rates
        total = report.first()["total_records"]
        
        report_data = [(col_name.replace("_pass_count", ""), 
                       report.first()[col_name],
                       round(report.first()[col_name] / total * 100, 2))
                      for col_name in report.columns if col_name != "total_records"]
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(
            report_data,
            ["check_name", "pass_count", "pass_rate_percent"]
        )

"""
Purpose: Ensure referential integrity between related datasets
Use Case: Foreign key validation, relationship verification, data lineage
"""

class ReferentialIntegrityPattern:
    """
    Implements referential integrity checking across datasets
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_sample_data():
        """Create sample related datasets"""
        #
```python
 # Customers table
        customers = [
            (1, "CUST001", "John Doe", "john@email.com"),
            (2, "CUST002", "Jane Smith", "jane@email.com"),

            (4, "CUST004", "Alice Wilson", "alice@email.com"),
        ]
        
        # Orders table (with some orphaned records)
        orders = [
            (1, "ORD001", 1, "2024-01-01", 100.00),
            (2, "ORD002", 2, "2024-01-02", 250.50),
            (3, "ORD003", 1, "2024-01-03", 175.25),
            (4, "ORD004", 5, "2024-01-04", 300.00),  # Orphaned - customer doesn't exist
            (5, "ORD005", 3, "2024-01-05", 450.80),
            (6, "ORD006", 6, "2024-01-06", 200.00),  # Orphaned - customer doesn't exist
        ]
        
        # Order items table
        order_items = [
            (1, 1, "PROD001", 2, 25.00),
            (2, 1, "PROD002", 1, 50.00),
            (3, 2, "PROD001", 5, 25.00),
            (4, 2, "PROD003", 3, 41.83),
            (5, 3, "PROD002", 3, 50.00),
            (6, 7, "PROD001", 1, 25.00),  # Orphaned - order doesn't exist
        ]
        
        # Products table
        products = [
            (1, "PROD001", "Product A", 25.00),
            (2, "PROD002", "Product B", 50.00),
            (3, "PROD003", "Product C", 41.83),
            (4, "PROD004", "Product D", 75.00),
        ]
        
        customers_df = spark.createDataFrame(
            customers, 
            ["customer_id", "customer_code", "name", "email"]
        )
        
        orders_df = spark.createDataFrame(

        )

        )
        
        products_df = spark.createDataFrame(
            products,
            ["product_id", "product_code", "product_name", "price"]
        )
        
        return customers_df, orders_df, order_items_df, products_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_foreign_key_integrity(child_df, parent_df, child_key, parent_key):
        """
        Check foreign key integrity between child and parent tables
        """
        # Left join to find orphaned records
        integrity_check = child_df.alias("child").join(
            parent_df.alias("parent"),
            col(f"child.{child_key}") == col(f"parent.{parent_key}"),
            "left"
        ).select(
            col("child.*"),
            col(f"parent.{parent_key}").alias("parent_key_exists")
        ).withColumn(
            "referential_integrity",
            when(col("parent_key_exists").isNotNull(), lit("VALID"))
            .otherwise(lit("ORPHANED"))
        )
        
        return integrity_check
    
    @staticmethod
    def identify_orphaned_records(child_df, parent_df, child_key, parent_key):
        """
        Identify orphaned records (child records without parent)
        """
        orphaned = child_df.alias("child").join(
            parent_df.alias("parent"),
            col(f"child.{child_key}") == col(f"parent.{parent_key}"),
            "left_anti"
        )
        
        return orphaned
    
    @staticmethod
    def identify_dangling_references(parent_df, child_df, parent_key, child_key):
        """
        Identify parent records with no child records
        """
        dangling = parent_df.alias("parent").join(
            child_df.alias("child"),
            col(f"parent.{parent_key}") == col(f"child.{child_key}"),
            "left_anti"
        )
        
        return dangling
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_multi_level_integrity(tables_chain):
        """
        Check referential integrity across multiple related tables
        tables_chain: list of tuples (df, key_column, parent_key_column)
        """
        results = {}
        
        for i in range(len(tables_chain) - 1):
            child_df, child_key, _ = tables_chain[i]
            parent_df, parent_key, _ = tables_chain[i + 1]
            
            integrity_check = ReferentialIntegrityPattern.check_foreign_key_integrity(
                child_df, parent_df, child_key, parent_key
            )
            
            results[f"level_{i}_to_{i+1}"] = integrity_check
        
        return results
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_cascading_deletes(parent_df, child_df, parent_key, child_key, 
                                   records_to_delete):
        """
        Validate impact of cascading deletes
        """
        # Find parent records to delete
        parents_to_delete = parent_df.join(
            records_to_delete,
            parent_df[parent_key] == records_to_delete[parent_key]
        )
        
        # Find affected child records
        affected_children = child_df.join(
            parents_to_delete.select(parent_key),
            child_df[child_key] == parents_to_delete[parent_key]
        )
        
        # Generate impact report
        impact_report = spark.createDataFrame([
            ("Parents to delete", parents_to_delete.count()),
            ("Children affected", affected_children.count())
        ], ["category", "count"])
        
        return {
            "impact_report": impact_report,
            "affected_children": affected_children
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_integrity_report(child_df, parent_df, child_key, parent_key, 
                                  relationship_name):
        """
        Generate comprehensive referential integrity report
        """
        total_child_records = child_df.count()
        
        integrity_check = ReferentialIntegrityPattern.check_foreign_key_integrity(
            child_df, parent_df, child_key, parent_key
        )
        
        valid_count = integrity_check.filter(col("referential_integrity") == "VALID").count()
        orphaned_count = integrity_check.filter(col("referential_integrity") == "ORPHANED").count()
        
        report = spark.createDataFrame([
            (relationship_name, total_child_records, valid_count, orphaned_count,
             round(valid_count / total_child_records * 100, 2) if total_child_records > 0 else 0)
        ], ["relationship", "total_records", "valid_references", "orphaned_records", "integrity_percent"])
        
        return report
    
    @staticmethod
    def enforce_referential_integrity(child_df, parent_df, child_key, parent_key, 
                                     action="filter"):
        """
        Enforce referential integrity by filtering or flagging invalid records
        action: 'filter' to remove orphaned records, 'flag' to mark them
        """
        if action == "filter":
            # Remove orphaned records
            clean_df = child_df.join(
                parent_df.select(parent_key),
                child_df[child_key] == parent_df[parent_key],
                "inner"
            ).select(child_df["*"])
            return clean_df
        
        elif action == "flag":
            # Flag orphaned records
            return ReferentialIntegrityPattern.check_foreign_key_integrity(
                child_df, parent_df, child_key, parent_key
            )
        
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid action: {action}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_circular_references(df, id_column, parent_id_column, max_depth=10):
        """
        Detect circular references in hierarchical data
        """
        # Create initial path
        result_df = df.withColumn("path", col(id_column).cast("string"))
        result_df = result_df.withColumn("depth", lit(0))
        result_df = result_df.withColumn("has_cycle", lit(False))
        
        # Iteratively check for cycles
        for depth in range(max_depth):
            result_df = result_df.alias("current").join(
                df.alias("parent"),
                col(f"current.{parent_id_column}") == col(f"parent.{id_column}"),
                "left"
            ).select(
                col("current.*"),
                col(f"parent.{parent_id_column}").alias("next_parent")
            ).withColumn(
                "has_cycle",
                when(
                    col("path").contains(col("next_parent").cast("string")),
                    lit(True)
                ).otherwise(col("has_cycle"))
            ).withColumn(
                "path",
                when(
                    col("next_parent").isNotNull(),
                    concat_ws("->", col("path"), col("next_parent").cast("string"))
                ).otherwise(col("path"))
            ).drop("next_parent")
        
        return result_df.select(id_column, parent_id_column, "path", "has_cycle")

class ComprehensiveDataIntegrityFramework:
    """
    Combines all data integrity patterns into a unified framework
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_comprehensive_dataset():
        
```python
"""Create a comprehensive dataset for testing all patterns"""
        transactions = [
            (1, "TXN001", 1, "PROD001", 5, 10.00, 50.00, "2024-01-01", "2024-01-05", "COMPLETED"),
            (2, "TXN002", 2, "PROD002", 3, 25.00, 75.00, "2024-01-02", "2024-01-06", "COMPLETED"),
            (3, "TXN003", 1, "PROD001", 2, 10.00, 25.00, "2024-01-03", "2024-01-07", "COMPLETED"),  # Wrong total
            (4, "TXN004", 5, "PROD003", 4, 15.00, 60.00, "2024-01-10", "2024-01-08", "COMPLETED"),  # Invalid customer, wrong dates
            (5, "TXN005", 2, "PROD002", -1, 25.00, -25.00, "2024-01-05", "2024-01-09", "CANCELLED"),  # Negative quantity
        ]
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(
            transactions,
            ["id", "transaction_id", "customer_id", "product_code", "quantity", 
             "unit_price", "total_amount", "order_date", "delivery_date", "status"]
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def run_all_integrity_checks(df, customers_df, products_df):
        """
        Run all integrity checks on the dataset
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("RUNNING COMPREHENSIVE INTEGRITY CHECKS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        results = {}
        
        # 1. CHECKSUM VERIFICATION
        print("\n[1/5] Running Checksum Verification...")
        df_with_checksum = ChecksumVerificationPattern.calculate_row_checksum(df)
        batch_checksum = ChecksumVerificationPattern.calculate_batch_checksum(df)
        results['checksum'] = {
            'data': df_with_checksum,
            'batch_checksum': batch_checksum
        }
        print("✓ Checksum verification completed")
        
        # 2. HASH VERIFICATION
        print("\n[2/5] Running Hash Verification...")
        df_with_hash = HashVerificationPattern.calculate_hash(df, "sha256")
        duplicate_check = HashVerificationPattern.detect_duplicates_by_hash(
            df, ["customer_id", "product_code", "quantity"]
        )
        results['hash'] = {
            'data': df_with_hash,
            'duplicate_check': duplicate_check
        }
        print("✓ Hash verification completed")
        
        # 3. SIGNATURE VERIFICATION
        print("\n[3/5] Running Signature Verification...")
        df_with_signature = SignatureVerificationPattern.generate_signature(
            df,
            key_column="transaction_id",
            data_columns=["customer_id", "product_code", "quantity", "total_amount"],
            secret_key="integrity_secret_key"
        )
        signature_verification = SignatureVerificationPattern.verify_signature(
            df_with_signature,
            key_column="transaction_id",
            data_columns=["customer_id", "product_code", "quantity", "total_amount"],
            signature_column="signature",
            secret_key="integrity_secret_key"
        )
        results['signature'] = {
            'data': df_with_signature,
            'verification': signature_verification
        }
        print("✓ Signature verification completed")
        
        # 4. CONSISTENCY CHECKS
        print("\n[4/5] Running Consistency Checks...")
        
        # Calculation consistency
        calc_check = ConsistencyCheckPattern.check_calculation_consistency(df)
        
        # Temporal consistency
        temporal_check = ConsistencyCheckPattern.check_temporal_consistency(
            df, "order_date", "delivery_date"
        )
        
        # Range consistency
        range_rules = {
            "quantity": (0, 1000),
            "unit_price": (0.01, 10000.00),
            "total_amount": (0, 100000.00)
        }
        range_check = ConsistencyCheckPattern.check_value_range_consistency(df, range_rules)
        
        # Cross-field consistency
        consistency_rules = [
            ("positive_quantity_for_completed", 
             (col("status") != "COMPLETED") | (col("quantity") > 0)),
            ("cancelled_has_negative_or_zero", 
             (col("status") != "CANCELLED") | (col("quantity") <= 0)),
            ("completed_has_delivery_date", 
             (col("status") != "COMPLETED") | col("delivery_date").isNotNull())
        ]
        cross_field_check = ConsistencyCheckPattern.check_cross_field_consistency(
            df, consistency_rules
        )
        
        results['consistency'] = {
            'calculation': calc_check,
            'temporal': temporal_check,
            'range': range_check,
            'cross_field': cross_field_check
        }
        print("✓ Consistency checks completed")
        
        # 5. REFERENTIAL INTEGRITY
        print("\n[5/5] Running Referential Integrity Checks...")
        
        # Customer referential integrity
        customer_integrity = ReferentialIntegrityPattern.check_foreign_key_integrity(
            df, customers_df, "customer_id", "customer_id"
        )
        
        # Product referential integrity
        product_integrity = ReferentialIntegrityPattern.check_foreign_key_integrity(
            df, products_df, "product_code", "product_code"
        )
        
        # Generate integrity reports
        customer_report = ReferentialIntegrityPattern.generate_integrity_report(
            df, customers_df, "customer_id", "customer_id", "Transactions->Customers"
        )
        
        product_report = ReferentialIntegrityPattern.generate_integrity_report(
            df, products_df, "product_code", "product_code", "Transactions->Products"
        )
        
        results['referential'] = {
            'customer_integrity': customer_integrity,
            'product_integrity': product_integrity,
            'customer_report': customer_report,
            'product_report': product_report
        }
        print("✓ Referential integrity checks completed")
        
        return results
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_master_integrity_report(results, df):
        """
        Generate a master integrity report combining all checks
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("MASTER INTEGRITY REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        total_records = df.count()
        
        # Checksum stats
        print("\n--- CHECKSUM VERIFICATION ---")
        print(f"Total Records: {total_records}")
        results['checksum']['batch_checksum'].show()
        
        # Hash verification stats
        print("\n--- HASH VERIFICATION ---")
        duplicate_count = results['hash']['duplicate_check'].filter(
            col("is_duplicate") == True
        ).count()
        print(f"Duplicate Records Found: {duplicate_count}")
        
        # Signature verification stats
        print("\n--- SIGNATURE VERIFICATION ---")
        valid_signatures = results['signature']['verification'].filter(
            col("signature_valid") == True
        ).count()
        invalid_signatures = total_records - valid_signatures
        print(f"Valid Signatures: {valid_signatures}/{total_records}")
        print(f"Invalid Signatures: {invalid_signatures}/{total_records}")
        
        # Consistency check stats
        print("\n--- CONSISTENCY CHECKS ---")
        
        calc_consistent = results['consistency']['calculation'].filter(
            col("total_consistent") == True
        ).count()
        print(f"Calculation Consistent: {calc_consistent}/{total_records}")
        
        temporal_consistent = results['consistency']['temporal'].filter(
            col("date_consistent") == True
        ).count()
        print(f"Temporal Consistent: {temporal_consistent}/{total_records}")
        
        range_consistent = results['consistency']['range'].filter(
            col("range_consistent") == True
        ).count()
        print(f"Range Consistent: {range_consistent}/{total_records}")
        
        all_rules_passed = results['consistency']['cross_field'].filter(
            col("all_rules_passed") == True
        ).count()
        print(f"All Business Rules Passed: {all_rules_passed}/{total_records}")
        
        # Referential integrity stats
        print("\n--- REFERENTIAL INTEGRITY ---")
        print("\nCustomer Integrity Report:")
        results['referential']['customer_report'].show()
        print("\nProduct Integrity Report:")
        results['referential']['product_report'].show()
        
        # Overall integrity score
        print("\n--- OVERALL INTEGRITY SCORE ---")
        
        # Calculate weighted score
        checksum_score = 100  # Assuming batch checksum is valid
        hash_score = ((total_records - duplicate_count) / total_records * 100) if total_records > 0 else 0
        signature_score = (valid_signatures / total_records * 100) if total_records > 0 else 0
        consistency_score = (all_rules_passed / total_records * 100) if total_records > 0 else 0
        
        customer_integrity_pct = results['referential']['customer_report'].first()['integrity_percent']
        product_integrity_pct = results['referential']['product_report'].first()['integrity_percent']
        referential_score = (customer_integrity_pct + product_integrity_pct) / 2
        
        overall_score = (
            checksum_score * 0.15 +
            hash_score * 0.15 +
            signature_score * 0.20 +
            consistency_score * 0.25 +
            referential_score * 0.25
        )
        
        score_df = spark.createDataFrame([
            ("Checksum Verification", round(checksum_score, 2)),
            ("Hash Verification", round(hash_score, 2)),
            ("Signature Verification", round(signature_score, 2)),
            ("Consistency Checks", round(consistency_score, 2)),
            ("Referential Integrity", round(referential_score, 2)),
            ("OVERALL INTEGRITY SCORE", round(overall_score, 2))
        ], ["Check Type", "Score (%)"])
        
        score_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Quality classification
        if overall_score >= 95:
            quality = "EXCELLENT"
        elif overall_score >= 85:
            quality = "GOOD"
        elif overall_score >= 70:
            quality = "FAIR"
        else:
            quality = "POOR"
        
        print(f"\nData Quality Classification: {quality}")
        
        return overall_score
    
    @staticmethod
    def identify_problematic_records(results, df):
        """
        Identify all records that failed any integrity check
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("PROBLEMATIC RECORDS ANALYSIS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Start with base dataframe
        problematic = df.alias("base")
        
        # Add consistency check results
        calc_check = results['consistency']['calculation'].select(
            "id", 
            col("total_consistent").alias("calc_ok")
        )
        
        temporal_check = results['consistency']['temporal'].select(
            "id",
            col("date_consistent").alias("temporal_ok")
        )
        
        range_check = results['consistency']['range'].select(
            "id",
            col("range_consistent").alias("range_ok")
        )
        
        cross_field = results['consistency']['cross_field'].select(
            "id",
            col("all_rules_passed").alias("rules_ok")
        )
        
        # Add referential integrity results
        customer_ref = results['referential']['customer_integrity'].select(
            "id",
            (col("referential_integrity") == "VALID").alias("customer_ref_ok")
        )
        
        product_ref = results['referential']['product_integrity'].select(
            "id",
            (col("referential_integrity") == "VALID").alias("product_ref_ok")
        )
        
        # Join all checks
        problematic = problematic.join(calc_check, "id", "left") \
            .join(temporal_check, "id", "left") \
            .join(range_check, "id", "left") \
            .join(cross_field, "id", "left") \
            .join(customer_ref, "id", "left") \
            .join(product_ref, "id", "left")
        
        # Identify issues
        problematic = problematic.withColumn(
            "issues",
            concat_ws(", ",
                when(~col("calc_ok"), lit("Calculation")).otherwise(lit("")),
                when(~col("temporal_ok"), lit("Temporal")).otherwise(lit("")),
                when(~col("range_ok"), lit("Range")).otherwise(lit("")),
                when(~col("rules_ok"), lit("Business Rules")).otherwise(lit("")),
                when(~col("customer_ref_ok"), lit("Customer Ref")).otherwise(lit("")),
                when(~col("product_ref_ok"), lit("Product Ref")).otherwise(lit(""))
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "has_issues",
            ~(col("calc_ok") & col("temporal_ok") & col("range_ok") & 
              col("rules_ok") & col("customer_ref_ok") & col("product_ref_ok"))
        )
        
        # Filter and clean up issues column
        problematic_records = problematic.filter(col("has_issues")).withColumn(
            "issues",
            when(col("issues").startsWith(", "), col("issues").substr(lit(3), lit(1000)))
            .otherwise(col("issues"))
        )
        
        print(f"\nTotal Problematic Records: {problematic_records.count()}/{df.count()}")
        print("\nProblematic Records Details:")
        problematic_records.select(
            "transaction_id", "customer_id", "product_code", 
            "calc_ok", "temporal_ok", "range_ok", "rules_ok",
            "customer_ref_ok", "product_ref_ok", "issues"
        ).show(truncate=False)
        
        return problematic_records

class AdvancedIntegrityFeatures:
    """
    Advanced features for data integrity management
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_integrity_audit_log(df, integrity_results):
        """
        Create an audit log of all integrity checks performed
        """
        from datetime import datetime
        
        audit_entries = []
        timestamp = datetime.now().isoformat()
        
        # Log checksum verification
        audit_entries.append((
            timestamp,
            "CHECKSUM_VERIFICATION",
            "BATCH_LEVEL",
            df.count(),
            df.count(),
            "PASSED",
            "Batch checksum calculated successfully"
        ))
        
        # Log signature verification
        sig_results = integrity_results['signature']['verification']
        valid_sigs = sig_results.filter(col("signature_valid") == True).count()
        total = sig_results.count()
        
        audit_entries.append((
            timestamp,
            "SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION",
            "ROW_LEVEL",
            total,
            valid_sigs,
            "PASSED" if valid_sigs == total else "FAILED",
            f"{valid_sigs}/{total} signatures valid"
        ))
        
        # Log consistency checks
        consistency = integrity_results['consistency']['cross_field']
        passed = consistency.filter(col("all_rules_passed") == True).count()
        total = consistency.count()
        
        audit_entries.append((
            timestamp,
            "CONSISTENCY_CHECK",
            "ROW_LEVEL",
            total,
            passed,
            "PASSED" if passed == total else "FAILED",
            f"{passed}/{total} records passed all rules"
        ))
        
        # Log referential integrity
        cust_report = integrity_results['referential']['customer_report'].first()
        audit_entries.append((
            timestamp,
            "REFERENTIAL_INTEGRITY",
            "CUSTOMER_FK",
            cust_report['total_records'],
            cust_report['valid_references'],
            "PASSED" if cust_report['orphaned_records'] == 0 else "FAILED",
            f"{cust_report['integrity_percent']}% integrity"
        ))
        
        audit_log = spark.createDataFrame(
            audit_entries,
            ["timestamp", "check_type", "check_level", "total_records", 
             "passed_records", "status", "details"]
        )
        
        return audit_log
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_data_lineage_with_integrity(df, source_info):
        """
        Create data lineage tracking with integrity metadata
        """
        lineage_df = df.withColumn("source_system", lit(source_info['system'])) \
            .withColumn("source_timestamp", lit(source_info['timestamp'])) \
            .withColumn("ingestion_timestamp", lit(datetime.now().isoformat())) \
            .withColumn("data_hash", sha2(
                concat_ws("|", *[col(c).cast("string") for c in df.columns]), 
                256
            ))
        
        return lineage_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def implement_data_quality_gates(df, integrity_results, thresholds):
        """
        Implement quality gates based on integrity check results
        thresholds: dict with minimum acceptable scores
        """
        gates = {}
        
        # Signature verification gate
        sig_results = integrity_results['signature']['verification']
        valid_sigs = sig_results.filter(col("signature_valid") == True).count()
        total = sig_results.count()
        sig_pass_rate = (valid_sigs / total * 100) if total > 0 else 0
        
        gates['signature_gate'] = {
            'passed': sig_pass_rate >= thresholds.get('signature', 95),
            'score': sig_pass_rate,
            'threshold': thresholds.get('signature', 95)
        }
        
        # Consistency gate
        consistency = integrity_results['consistency']['cross_field']
        passed = consistency.filter(col("all_rules_passed") == True).count()
        total = consistency.count()
        consistency_rate = (passed / total * 100) if total > 0 else 0
        
        gates['consistency_gate'] = {
            'passed': consistency_rate >= thresholds.get('consistency', 90),
            'score': consistency_rate,
            'threshold': thresholds.get('consistency', 90)
        }
        
        # Referential integrity gate
        cust_report = integrity_results['referential']['customer_report'].first()
        ref_integrity = cust_report['integrity_percent']
        
        gates['referential_gate'] = {
            'passed': ref_integrity >= thresholds.get('referential', 95),
            'score': ref_integrity,
            'threshold': thresholds.get('referential', 95)
        }
        
        # Overall gate
        all_gates_passed = all(gate['passed'] for gate in gates.values())
        gates['overall'] = {
            'passed': all_gates_passed,
            'message': "All quality gates passed" if all_gates_passed else "Quality gates failed"
        }
        
        return gates
    
    @staticmethod
    def auto_remediate_integrity_issues(df, problematic_records):
        """
        Automatically remediate common integrity issues where possible
        """
        # Get IDs of problematic records
        problematic_ids = problematic_records.select("id").rdd.flatMap(lambda x: x).collect()
        
        remediation_log = []
        
        # Separate clean and problematic records
        clean_records = df.filter(~col("id").isin(problematic_ids))
        issues_to_fix = df.filter(col("id").isin(problematic_ids))
        
        # Fix calculation inconsistencies
        fixed_calculations = issues_to_fix.withColumn(
            "total_amount_original",
            col("total_amount")
        ).withColumn(
            "total_amount",
            col("quantity") * col("unit_price")
        ).withColumn(
            "remediation_applied",
            when(
                col("total_amount") != col("total_amount_original"),
                lit("RECALCULATED_TOTAL")
            ).otherwise(lit(""))
        )
        
        remediation_log.append({
            'issue': 'CALCULATION_INCONSISTENCY',
            'action': 'RECALCULATE_TOTAL',
            'records_affected': fixed_calculations.filter(
                col("total_amount") != col("total_amount_original")
            ).count()
        })
        
        # Note: Other issues like orphaned records would require business logic decisions
        # For demo purposes, we'll flag them for manual review
        
        return {
            'clean_records': clean_records,
            'remediated_records': fixed_calculations,
            'remediation_log': remediation_log
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_integrity_dashboard_metrics(df, integrity_results):
        """
        Generate metrics suitable for a data integrity dashboard
        """
        total_records = df.count()
        
        # Calculate metrics
        metrics = []
        
        # 1. Data Completeness
        null_counts = df.select([
            _sum(when(col(c).isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)).alias(c) 
            for c in df.columns
        ]).first().asDict()
        
        total_cells = total_records * len(df.columns)
        null_cells = sum(null_counts.values())
        completeness = ((total_cells - null_cells) / total_cells * 100) if total_cells > 0 else 0
        
        metrics.append(("Data Completeness", round(completeness, 2), "%"))
        
        # 2. Signature Validity
        sig_results = integrity_results['signature']['verification']
        valid_sigs = sig_results.filter(col("signature_valid") == True).count()
        sig_validity = (valid_sigs / total_records * 100) if total_records > 0 else 0
        
        metrics.append(("Signature Validity", round(sig_validity, 2), "%"))
        
        # 3. Consistency Score
        consistency = integrity_results['consistency']['cross_field']
        passed = consistency.filter(col("all_rules_passed") == True).count()
        consistency_score = (passed / total_records * 100) if total_records > 0 else 0
        
        metrics.append(("Consistency Score", round(consistency_score, 2), "%"))
        
        # 4. Referential Integrity
        cust_report = integrity_results['referential']['customer_report'].first()
        ref_integrity = cust_report['integrity_percent']
        
        metrics.append(("Referential Integrity", round(ref_integrity, 2), "%"))
        
        # 5. Duplicate Records
        duplicate_check = integrity_results['hash']['duplicate_check']
        duplicates = duplicate_check.filter(col("is_duplicate") == True).count()
        duplicate_rate = (duplicates / total_records * 100) if total_records > 0 else 0
        
        metrics.append(("Duplicate Rate", round(duplicate_rate, 2), "%"))
        
        # 6. Overall Health Score
        health_score = (completeness + sig_validity + consistency_score + ref_integrity) / 4
        metrics.append(("Overall Health Score", round(health_score, 2), "%"))
        
        dashboard_df = spark.createDataFrame(metrics, ["Metric", "Value", "Unit"])
        
        return dashboard_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def export_integrity_report(integrity_results, output_path="/tmp/integrity_report"):
        """
        Export comprehensive integrity report to files
        """
        print(f"\nExporting integrity reports to: {output_path}")
        
        # Export signature verification results
        integrity_results['signature']['verification'].select(
            "transaction_id", "signature_valid", "verification_status"
        ).write.mode("overwrite").parquet(f"{output_path}/signature_verification")
        
        # Export consistency check results
        integrity_results['consistency']['cross_field'].write.mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(f"{output_path}/consistency_checks")
        
        # Export referential integrity results
        integrity_results['referential']['customer_integrity'].write.mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(f"{output_path}/customer_referential_integrity")
        
        integrity_results['referential']['product_integrity'].write.mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet(f"{output_path}/product_referential_integrity")
        
        print("✓ Integrity reports exported successfully")

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
import time
from datetime import datetime

# Initialize Spark Session with optimization configurations
def create_optimized_spark_session(pattern_name):
    """
    Create a Spark session with specific optimization configurations
    """
    return SparkSession.builder \
        .appName(f"Optimization_Pattern_{pattern_name}") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.cbo.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.statistics.histogram.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10485760") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200") \
        .getOrCreate()

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 1: Rule-Based Optimization Pattern (Refined)
# ============================================================================
class RuleBasedOptimizationPattern:
    """
    Demonstrates rule-based optimization techniques in PySpark.
    These optimizations are applied automatically by Catalyst optimizer.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def predicate_pushdown_example(self):
        """
        Predicate Pushdown: Filters are pushed down to data source level
        to reduce data read from disk/network
        """
        print("\n=== Rule-Based: Predicate Pushdown ===")
        
        # Create sample data
        data = [(i, f"name_{i}", i * 100, f"dept_{i % 5}") 
                for i in range(1, 100001)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            data, 
            ["id", "name", "salary", "department"]
        )
        df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/employees")
        
        # Read with filter - filter will be pushed to parquet reader
        employees_df = self.spark.read.parquet("/tmp/employees")
        
        # BAD: Filter after reading all data
        print("\nWithout optimization awareness:")
        start = time.time()
        result_bad = employees_df.select("*").filter(col("salary") > 50000)
        count_bad = result_bad.count()
        print(f"Time taken: {time.time() - start:.3f}s, Count: {count_bad}")
        
        # GOOD: Filter early (Catalyst will push this down)
        print("\nWith predicate pushdown:")
        start = time.time()
        result_good = employees_df.filter(col("salary") > 50000).select("*")
        count_good = result_good.count()
        print(f"Time taken: {time.time() - start:.3f}s, Count: {count_good}")
        
        # Show query plan
        print("\nOptimized Physical Plan:")
        result_good.explain(mode="formatted")
        
        return result_good
    
    def column_pruning_example(self):
        """
        Column Pruning: Only required columns are read from source
        """
        print("\n=== Rule-Based: Column Pruning ===")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet("/tmp/employees")
        
        # BAD: Select all then filter columns
        print("\nWithout column pruning awareness:")
        start = time.time()
        result_bad = df.select("*").select("id", "name")
        count_bad = result_bad.count()
        print(f"Time taken: {time.time() - start:.3f}s")
        
        # GOOD: Select only needed columns early
        print("\nWith column pruning:")
        start = time.time()
        result_good = df.select("id", "name")
        count_good = result_good.count()
        print(f"Time taken: {time.time() - start:.3f}s")
        
        result_good.explain(mode="formatted")
        return result_good
    
    def constant_folding_example(self):
        """
        Constant Folding: Compile-time evaluation of constant expressions
        """
        print("\n=== Rule-Based: Constant Folding ===")
        
        df = self.spark.read.parquet("/tmp/employees")
        
        # Expressions with constants are evaluated at compile time
        result = df.select(
            col("id"),
            col("name"),
            (col("salary") * (1 + 0.1)).alias("salary_with_bonus"),  # 1+0.1 folded to 1.1
            (lit(100) * lit(2)).alias("constant_expr"),  # Folded to 200
            when(col("salary") > 50000, lit("High"))
                .otherwise(lit("Low")).alias("salary_grade")
        )
        
        print("\nQuery plan showing constant folding:")
        result.explain(mode="formatted")
        result.show(5)
        
        return result
    
    def join_reordering_example(self):
        """
        Join Reordering: Optimizer reorders joins for better performance
        """
        print("\n=== Rule-Based: Join Reordering ===")
        
        # Create sample datasets
        large_df = self.spark.range(0, 100000).select(
            col("id").alias("order_id"),
            (col("id") % 1000).alias("customer_id"),
            (col("id") % 100).alias("product_id")
        )
        
        medium_df = self.spark.range(0, 1000).select(
            col("id").alias("customer_id"),
            concat(lit("Customer_"), col("id")).alias("customer_name")
        )
        
        small_df = self.spark.range(0, 100).select(
            col("id").alias("product_id"),
            concat(lit("Product_"), col("id")).alias("product_name")
        )
        
        # Multi-way join - optimizer will reorder for efficiency
        result = large_df \
            .join(medium_df, "customer_id") \
            .join(small_df, "product_id") \
            .select("order_id", "customer_name", "product_name")
        
        print("\nOptimized join order:")
        result.explain(mode="formatted")
        result.show(5)
        
        return result

# PATTERN 2: Cost-Based Optimization Pattern (Refined)
# ============================================================================
class CostBasedOptimizationPattern:
    """
    Demonstrates cost-based optimization using statistics and histograms
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def collect_and_use_statistics(self):
        """
        Collect table and column statistics for CBO
        """
        print("\n=== Cost-Based: Statistics Collection ===")
        
        # Create and save sample data
        orders_data = [
            (i, i % 1000, i % 100, i * 50.0, f"2024-{(i % 12) + 1:02d}-01")
            for i in range(1, 50001)
        ]
        orders_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            orders_data,
            ["order_id", "customer_id", "product_id", "amount", "order_date"]
        )
        orders_df.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable("orders")
        
        # Collect statistics
        print("\nCollecting table statistics...")
        self.spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE orders COMPUTE STATISTICS")
        
        print("\nCollecting column statistics...")
        self.spark.sql("""
            ANALYZE TABLE orders COMPUTE STATISTICS FOR COLUMNS 
            order_id, customer_id, product_id, amount
        """)
        
        # Show statistics
        stats = self.spark.sql("DESCRIBE EXTENDED orders").collect()
        print("\nTable Statistics:")
        for row in stats:
            if 'Statistics' in str(row):
                print(row)
        
        return orders_df
    
    def join_strategy_selection(self):
        """
        CBO selects optimal join strategy based on statistics
        """
        print("\n=== Cost-Based: Join Strategy Selection ===")
        
        # Create tables with different sizes
        large_table = self.spark.range(0, 100000).select(
            col("id").alias("user_id"),
            concat(lit("User_"), col("id")).alias("username")
        )
        large_table.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable("users")
        
        small_table = self.spark.range(0, 100).select(
            col("id").alias("role_id"),
            concat(lit("Role_"), col("id")).alias("role_name")
        )
        small_table.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable("roles")
        
        user_roles = self.spark.range(0, 100000).select(
            col("id").alias("user_id"),
            (col("id") % 100).alias("role_id")
        )
        user_roles.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable("user_roles")
        
        # Collect statistics
        self.spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE users COMPUTE STATISTICS")
        self.spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE roles COMPUTE STATISTICS")
        self.spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE user_roles COMPUTE STATISTICS")
        
        # Query with multiple joins - CBO will choose strategies
        result = self.spark.sql("""
            SELECT u.username, r.role_name, COUNT(*) as cnt
            FROM users u
            JOIN user_roles ur ON u.user_id = ur.user_id
            JOIN roles r ON ur.role_id = r.role_id
            GROUP BY u.username, r.role_name
            LIMIT 10
        """)
        
        print("\nCBO-optimized join plan:")
        result.explain(mode="cost")
        result.show()
        
        return result
    
    def broadcast_join_optimization(self):
        """
        Automatic broadcast join selection based on table size
        """
        print("\n=== Cost-Based: Broadcast Join Optimization ===")
        
        large_df = self.spark.table("users")
        small_df = self.spark.table("roles").limit(50)
        
        # CBO will automatically choose broadcast join for small table
        result = large_df.alias("u") \
            .join(
                small_df.alias("r"),
                col("u.user_id") % 100 == col("r.role_id"),
                "inner"
            ) \
            .select("u.username", "r.role_name")
        
        print("\nAutomatic broadcast join:")
        result.explain(mode="formatted")
        result.show(5)
        
        # Force broadcast hint for comparison
        from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
        result_hint = large_df.alias("u") \
            .join(
                broadcast(small_df.alias("r")),
                col("u.user_id") % 100 == col("r.role_id"),
                "inner"
            ) \
            .select("u.username", "r.role_name")
        
        print("\nExplicit broadcast hint:")
        result_hint.explain(mode="formatted")
        
        return result
