    def optimize_shuffle_with_aqe(self):
        """
        AQE optimizes shuffle operations dynamically
        """
        print("\n=== AQE: Shuffle Optimization ===")
        
        # Create data requiring shuffle
        df = self.spark.range(0, 1000000).select(
            (col("id") % 1000).alias("partition_key"),
            col("id").alias("value"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("amount")
        )

        result = df.groupBy("partition_key") \

# PATTERN 4: Runtime Optimization Pattern
# ============================================================================
class RuntimeOptimizationPattern:
    """
    Demonstrates runtime optimization techniques and monitoring
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def dynamic_resource_allocation(self):
        """
        Monitor and optimize resource usage at runtime
        """
        print("\n=== Runtime: Dynamic Resource Allocation ===")
        
        # Enable dynamic allocation
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled", "true")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.dynamicAllocation.minExecutors", "1")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors", "10")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.dynamicAllocation.initialExecutors", "2")
        
        # Create varying workload
        print("\nPhase 1: Light workload")
        df1 = self.spark.range(0, 10000)
        result1 = df1.groupBy((col("id") % 10).alias("key")).count()
        result1.show()
        
        print("\nPhase 2: Heavy workload")
        df2 = self.spark.range(0, 10000000)
        result2 = df2.groupBy((col("id") % 100).alias("key")) \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                sum("id").alias("sum"),
                avg("id").alias("avg"),
                stddev("id").alias("stddev")
            )
        result2.show()
        
        print("\nPhase 3: Back to light workload")
        result3 = df1.select("id").distinct().count()
        print(f"Distinct count: {result3}")
        
        return result2
    
    def cache_optimization_runtime(self):
        """
        Smart caching decisions based on runtime analysis
        """
        print("\n=== Runtime: Cache Optimization ===")
        
        # Create base dataframe
        base_df = self.spark.range(0, 1000000).select(
            col("id"),
            (col("id") % 1000).alias("category"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("value")
        )
        
        # Scenario: DataFrame used multiple times
        print("\nWithout caching - multiple computations:")
        start = time.time()
        
        result1 = base_df.filter(col("value") > 500).count()
        result2 = base_df.filter(col("value") <= 500).count()
        result3 = base_df.groupBy("category").agg(avg("value")).count()
        
        time_without_cache = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time without cache: {time_without_cache:.3f}s")
        print(f"Results: {result1}, {result2}, {result3}")
        
        # With intelligent caching
        print("\nWith caching - reuse computation:")
        base_df_cached = base_df.cache()
        
        start = time.time()
        
        result1 = base_df_cached.filter(col("value") > 500).count()
        result2 = base_df_cached.filter(col("value") <= 500).count()
        result3 = base_df_cached.groupBy("category").agg(avg("value")).count()
        
        time_with_cache = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time with cache: {time_with_cache:.3f}s")
        print(f"Results: {result1}, {result2}, {result3}")
        print(f"Speedup: {time_without_cache/time_with_cache:.2f}x")
        
        # Check cache status
        print(f"\nCache status - Is cached: {base_df_cached.is_cached}")
        
        # Unpersist when done
        base_df_cached.unpersist()
        
        return base_df_cached
    
    def partition_optimization_runtime(self):
        """
        Runtime partition optimization based on data characteristics
        """
        print("\n=== Runtime: Partition Optimization ===")
        
        # Create data with uneven distribution
        data = []
        # Skewed partitions
        for i in range(100000):
            data.append((i % 10, f"value_{i}", i * 1.5))
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, ["key", "name", "amount"])
        
        print(f"Initial partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
        
        # Analyze partition sizes
        partition_sizes = df.rdd.glom().map(len).collect()
        print(f"Partition size distribution: min={min(partition_sizes)}, "
              f"max={max(partition_sizes)}, avg={sum(partition_sizes)/len(partition_sizes):.0f}")
        
        # Repartition based on key for better distribution
        print("\nRepartitioning by key for balanced distribution:")
        df_repartitioned = df.repartition(20, "key")
        
        partition_sizes_new = df_repartitioned.rdd.glom().map(len).collect()
        print(f"New partition size distribution: min={min(partition_sizes_new)}, "
              f"max={max(partition_sizes_new)}, avg={sum(partition_sizes_new)/len(partition_sizes_new):.0f}")
        
        # Coalesce for final output (reduce partitions)
        print("\nCoalescing for output:")
        df_final = df_repartitioned.coalesce(5)
        print(f"Final partitions: {df_final.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
        
        return df_final
    
    def execution_monitoring_pattern(self):
        """
        Monitor query execution and optimize based on metrics
        """
        print("\n=== Runtime: Execution Monitoring ===")
        
        # Create sample workload
        df = self.spark.range(0, 5000000).select(
            col("id"),
            (col("id") % 1000).alias("group_key"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("value1"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("value2")
        )
        
        # Complex query to monitor
        query = df.filter(col("value1") > 50) \
            .groupBy("group_key") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                sum("value2").alias("sum_value2"),
                avg("value2").alias("avg_value2"),
                min("value1").alias("min_value1"),
                max("value1").alias("max_value1")
            ) \
            .filter(col("count") > 1000) \
            .orderBy(desc("sum_value2"))
        
        # Execute with timing
        print("\nExecuting query with monitoring...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        result = query.collect()
        
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        print(f"Execution time: {execution_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"Result rows: {len(result)}")
        
        # Show query execution plan
        print("\nQuery execution plan:")
        query.explain(mode="formatted")
        
        # Performance metrics
        print("\nPerformance Summary:")
        print(f"- Total execution time: {execution_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"- Rows processed: 5,000,000")
        print(f"- Rows returned: {len(result)}")
        print(f"- Throughput: {5000000/execution_time:.0f} rows/sec")
        
        return query

# PATTERN 5: Feedback-Based Optimization Pattern
# ============================================================================
class FeedbackBasedOptimizationPattern:
    """
    Demonstrates feedback-based optimization using historical query performance
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        self.query_history = []
        
    def collect_query_metrics(self, query_name, df, execution_func):
        """
        Collect metrics from query execution for feedback
        """
        print(f"\n=== Collecting metrics for: {query_name} ===")
        
        start_time = time.time()
        start_memory = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        # Execute query
        result = execution_func(df)
        result_count = result.count() if hasattr(result, 'count') else len(result)
        
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        # Collect metrics
        metrics = {
            'query_name': query_name,
            'execution_time': execution_time,
            'result_count': result_count,
            'num_partitions': df.rdd.getNumPartitions(),
            'timestamp': datetime.now()
        }
        
        self.query_history.append(metrics)
        
        print(f"Execution time: {execution_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"Result count: {result_count}")
        
        return result, metrics
    
    def adaptive_configuration_tuning(self):
        """
        Adjust configuration based on query performance feedback
        """
        print("\n=== Feedback-Based: Adaptive Configuration Tuning ===")
        
        # Create test dataset
        df = self.spark.range(0, 2000000).select(
            col("id"),
            (col("id") % 100).alias("key"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("value")
        )
        
        # Test 1: Default configuration
        print("\n--- Test 1: Default shuffle partitions (200) ---")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")
        
        def query1(data):
            return data.groupBy("key").agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                avg("value").alias("avg_value")
            )
        
        result1, metrics1 = self.collect_query_metrics("default_config", df, query1)
        
        # Test 2: Reduced partitions based on data size
        print("\n--- Test 2: Optimized shuffle partitions (50) ---")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "50")
        
        result2, metrics2 = self.collect_query_metrics("optimized_config", df, query1)
        
        # Test 3: Further optimization
        print("\n--- Test 3: Further optimized (20) ---")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "20")
        
        result3, metrics3 = self.collect_query_metrics("further_optimized", df, query1)
        
        # Analyze feedback
        print("\n=== Performance Comparison ===")
        for metrics in [metrics1, metrics2, metrics3]:
            print(f"{metrics['query_name']}: {metrics['execution_time']:.3f}s")
        
        # Choose best configuration
        best_config = min([metrics1, metrics2, metrics3], 
                         key=lambda x: x['execution_time'])
        print(f"\nBest configuration: {best_config['query_name']} "
              f"({best_config['execution_time']:.3f}s)")
        
        return result3
    
    def query_rewriting_based_on_feedback(self):
        """
        Rewrite queries based on performance feedback
        """
        print("\n=== Feedback-Based: Query Rewriting ===")
        
        # Create sample data
        orders = self.spark.range(0, 100000).select(
            col("id").alias("order_id"),
            (col("id") % 1000).alias("customer_id"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("amount")
        )
        
        customers = self.spark.range(0, 1000).select(
            col("id").alias("customer_id"),
            concat(lit("Customer_"), col("id")).alias("customer_name")
        )
        
        # Approach 1: Join then filter
        print("\n--- Approach 1: Join then filter ---")
        def query_v1(orders_df, customers_df):
            return orders_df.join(customers_df, "customer_id") \
                .filter(col("amount") > 500) \
                .select("order_id", "customer_name", "amount")
        
        result1, metrics1 = self.collect_query_metrics(
            "join_then_filter", 
            orders, 
            lambda df: query_v1(df, customers)
        )
        
        # Approach 2: Filter then join (optimized based on feedback)
        print("\n--- Approach 2: Filter then join (optimized) ---")
        def query_v2(orders_df, customers_df):
            filtered_orders = orders_df.filter(col("amount") > 500)
            return filtered_orders.join(customers_df, "customer_id") \
                .select("order_id", "customer_name", "amount")
        
        result2, metrics2 = self.collect_query_metrics(
            "filter_then_join",
            orders,
            lambda df: query_v2(df, customers)
        )
        
        # Approach 3: Broadcast join (further optimized)
        print("\n--- Approach 3: Filter + Broadcast join ---")
        def query_v3(orders_df, customers_df):
            from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
            filtered_orders = orders_df.filter(col("amount") > 500)
            return filtered_orders.join(
                broadcast(customers_df), 
                "customer_id"
            ).select("order_id", "customer_name", "amount")
        
        result3, metrics3 = self.collect_query_metrics(
            "filter_broadcast_join",
            orders,
            lambda df: query_v3(df, customers)
        )
        
        # Performance comparison
        print("\n=== Query Rewrite Performance ===")
        improvements = []
        baseline = metrics1['execution_time']
        
        for metrics in [metrics1, metrics2, metrics3]:
            improvement = ((baseline - metrics['execution_time']) / baseline) * 100
            improvements.append(improvement)
            print(f"{metrics['query_name']}: {metrics['execution_time']:.3f}s "
                  f"({improvement:+.1f}%
```python
                  f"({improvement:+.1f}% vs baseline)")
        
        return result3
    
    def historical_statistics_optimization(self):
        """
        Use historical query statistics to optimize future queries
        """
        print("\n=== Feedback-Based: Historical Statistics Optimization ===")
        
        # Simulate multiple query executions and learn patterns
        df = self.spark.range(0, 1000000).select(
            col("id"),
            (col("id") % 100).alias("category"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("score"),

            min("value").alias("min_value"),
            max("value").alias("max_value")

        print("\nData Statistics:")
        print(f"Total records: {stats['total_count']}")
        print(f"Distinct categories: {stats['distinct_categories']}")
        print(f"Avg score: {stats['avg_score']:.2f}")
        print(f"Stddev score: {stats['stddev_score']:.2f}")
        print(f"Value range: [{stats['min_value']:.2f}, {stats['max_value']:.2f}]")
        
        # Use statistics to optimize query
        # Example: Choose partition count based on distinct categories
        optimal_partitions = min(200, max(10, stats['distinct_categories']))
        print(f"\nOptimal partitions based on categories: {optimal_partitions}")

        # Execute optimized query

            ) \

        result_count = result.count()
        exec_time = time.time() - start
        
        print(f"Execution time: {exec_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"Result count: {result_count}")
        
        result.show(10)
        
        return result
    
    def iterative_optimization_loop(self):
        """
        Iterative optimization based on continuous feedback
        """
        print("\n=== Feedback-Based: Iterative Optimization Loop ===")
        
        # Create workload
        df = self.spark.range(0, 500000).select(
            col("id"),
            (col("id") % 50).alias("partition_key"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("metric")
        )
        
        # Define query template
        def execute_query(data, config):
            self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", str(config['partitions']))
            
            result = data.groupBy("partition_key") \
                .agg(
                    count("*").alias("count"),
                    avg("metric").alias("avg_metric"),
                    percentile_approx("metric", 0.5).alias("median_metric")
                )
            
            start = time.time()
            count = result.count()
            exec_time = time.time() - start
            
            return exec_time, count
        
        # Iterative optimization
        configs = [
            {'name': 'baseline', 'partitions': 200},
            {'name': 'reduced', 'partitions': 100},
            {'name': 'optimized', 'partitions': 50},
            {'name': 'minimal', 'partitions': 25},
        ]
        
        results = []
        print("\nIterative optimization results:")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        for config in configs:
            exec_time, count = execute_query(df, config)
            results.append({
                'config': config['name'],
                'partitions': config['partitions'],
                'time': exec_time,
                'count': count
            })
            print(f"{config['name']:12} | Partitions: {config['partitions']:3} | "
                  f"Time: {exec_time:.3f}s")
        
        # Find optimal configuration
        optimal = min(results, key=lambda x: x['time'])
        print("-" * 60)
        print(f"\nOptimal configuration: {optimal['config']} "
              f"with {optimal['partitions']} partitions ({optimal['time']:.3f}s)")
        
        # Apply learning for future queries
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", str(optimal['partitions']))
        print(f"\nApplied optimal configuration for future queries")
        
        return results
    
    def generate_optimization_report(self):
        """
        Generate comprehensive optimization report from feedback
        """
        print("\n=== Feedback-Based: Optimization Report ===")
        
        if not self.query_history:
            print("No query history available")
            return
        
        print("\nQuery Performance History:")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        for idx, metrics in enumerate(self.query_history, 1):
            print(f"\n{idx}. {metrics['query_name']}")
            print(f"   Execution Time: {metrics['execution_time']:.3f}s")
            print(f"   Result Count: {metrics['result_count']}")
            print(f"   Partitions: {metrics['num_partitions']}")
            print(f"   Timestamp: {metrics['timestamp']}")
        
        # Calculate statistics
        avg_time = sum(m['execution_time'] for m in self.query_history) / len(self.query_history)
        min_time = min(m['execution_time'] for m in self.query_history)
        max_time = max(m['execution_time'] for m in self.query_history)
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("Summary Statistics:")
        print(f"  Total queries executed: {len(self.query_history)}")
        print(f"  Average execution time: {avg_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"  Fastest query: {min_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"  Slowest query: {max_time:.3f}s")
        
        # Recommendations
        print("\nOptimization Recommendations:")
        if max_time > 2 * avg_time:
            print("  ⚠ Significant performance variance detected")
            print("  → Consider analyzing slow queries for optimization opportunities")
        
        if avg_time > 5.0:
            print("  ⚠ High average execution time")
            print("  → Consider increasing parallelism or caching frequently used data")
        
        print("=" * 80)

def compare_optimization_strategies(spark):
    """
    Utility function to compare different optimization strategies
    """
    print("\n=== Comparing Optimization Strategies ===")
    
    # Create test dataset
    df = spark.range(0, 1000000).select(
        col("id"),
        (col("id") % 100).alias("key"),
        (rand() * 1000).alias("value")
    )
    
    strategies = {
        'No Optimization': {
            'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'false',
            'spark.sql.cbo.enabled': 'false',
            'spark.sql.shuffle.partitions': '200'
        },
        'Rule-Based Only': {
            'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'false',
            'spark.sql.cbo.enabled': 'false',
            'spark.sql.shuffle.partitions': '50'
        },
        'Cost-Based': {
            'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'false',
            'spark.sql.cbo.enabled': 'true',
            'spark.sql.shuffle.partitions': '50'
        },
        'Full Optimization': {
            'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'true',
            'spark.sql.cbo.enabled': 'true',
            'spark.sql.shuffle.partitions': '50'
        }
    }
    
    results = {}
    
    for strategy_name, config in strategies.items():
        print(f"\nTesting: {strategy_name}")
        
        # Apply configuration
        for key, value in config.items():
            spark.conf.set(key, value)
        
        # Run test query
        start = time.time()
        result = df.groupBy("key").agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value"),
            sum("value").alias("sum_value")
        ).collect()
        
        exec_time = time.time() - start
        results[strategy_name] = exec_time
        
        print(f"Execution time: {exec_time:.3f}s")
    
    # Print comparison
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("Strategy Comparison:")
    print("=" * 60)
    baseline = results['No Optimization']
    
    for strategy, time_taken in results.items():
        improvement = ((baseline - time_taken) / baseline) * 100
        print(f"{strategy:20} : {time_taken:.3f}s ({improvement:+.1f}%)")
    
    print("=" * 60)


# ============================================================================
# ENTRY POINT
# ============================================================================
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

This comprehensive PySpark program demonstrates all five query plan optimization patterns with detailed examples:

## **Key Features:**

### **1. Rule-Based Optimization (RBO)**
- Predicate pushdown to data sources
- Column pruning for efficient I/O
- Constant folding at compile time
- Automatic join reordering

### **2. Cost-Based Optimization (CBO)**
- Statistics collection and usage
- Intelligent join strategy selection
- Automatic broadcast join detection
- Cardinality-based optimization

### **3. Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)**
- Dynamic partition coalescing
- Skew join handling
- Runtime join strategy switching
- Shuffle optimization

### **4. Runtime Optimization**
- Dynamic resource allocation
- Smart caching strategies
- Partition balancing
- Performance monitoring

### **5. Feedback-Based Optimization**
- Configuration tuning based on history
- Query rewriting for better performance
- Historical statistics utilization
- Iterative improvement loops

Each
Each pattern includes:
- **Detailed code examples** with real-world scenarios
- **Performance comparisons** showing before/after optimization
- **Execution plan analysis** using `.explain()` methods
- **Metrics collection** and reporting
- **Best practices** and anti-patterns

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.skewedPartitionFactor", "5")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.skewedPartitionThresholdInBytes", "256MB")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.cbo.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.statistics.histogram.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10485760")  # 10MB
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")  # Adjust based on data size
```

```python
# ============================================================================
# BONUS: Advanced Optimization Techniques
# ============================================================================

class AdvancedOptimizationPatterns:
    """
    Additional advanced optimization techniques
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def bucketing_optimization(self):
        """
        Use bucketing to optimize joins and aggregations
        """
        print("\n=== Advanced: Bucketing Optimization ===")
        
        # Create sample data
        orders = self.spark.range(0, 100000).select(
            col("id").alias("order_id"),
            (col("id") % 1000).alias("customer_id"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("amount")
        )
        
        customers = self.spark.range(0, 1000).select(
            col("id").alias("customer_id"),
            concat(lit("Customer_"), col("id")).alias("name")
        )
        
        # Write data with bucketing
        print("\nWriting bucketed tables...")
        orders.write \
            .bucketBy(10, "customer_id") \
            .sortBy("customer_id") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .saveAsTable("orders_bucketed")
        
        customers.write \
            .bucketBy(10, "customer_id") \
            .sortBy("customer_id") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .saveAsTable("customers_bucketed")
        
        # Join bucketed tables - no shuffle needed!
        print("\nJoining bucketed tables (no shuffle):")
        result = self.spark.sql("""
            SELECT o.order_id, c.name, o.amount
            FROM orders_bucketed o
            JOIN customers_bucketed c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
            WHERE o.amount > 500
        """)
        
        result.explain(mode="formatted")
        print(f"Result count: {result.count()}")
        
        return result
    
    def z_ordering_optimization(self):
        """
        Z-Ordering for better data clustering (Delta Lake feature)
        """
        print("\n=== Advanced: Z-Ordering Optimization ===")
        
        # Create multi-dimensional data
        data = self.spark.range(0, 100000).select(
            col("id"),
            (col("id") % 100).alias("region"),
            (col("id") % 50).alias("product_category"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("sales"),
            date_add(lit("2024-01-01"), (col("id") % 365).cast("int")).alias("date")
        )
        
        # Save as parquet with partitioning
        print("\nWriting data with partitioning...")
        data.write \
            .partitionBy("region") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet("/tmp/sales_data")
        
        # Note: Z-ordering requires Delta Lake
        # This is a conceptual example
        print("""
        For Delta Lake tables, you would use:
        
        OPTIMIZE sales_table
        ZORDER BY (product_category, date)
        
        This clusters data for better query performance on these columns.
        """)
        
        # Query with multiple filters
        sales_df = self.spark.read.parquet("/tmp/sales_data")
        result = sales_df.filter(
            (col("product_category") == 25) & 
            (col("date") >= "2024-06-01")
        )
        
        print(f"\nFiltered result count: {result.count()}")
        result.show(5)
        
        return result
    
    def bloom_filter_optimization(self):
        """
        Use Bloom filters for efficient filtering
        """
        print("\n=== Advanced: Bloom Filter Optimization ===")
        
        # Create large and small datasets
        large_dataset = self.spark.range(0, 1000000).select(
            col("id").alias("transaction_id"),
            (col("id") % 10000).alias("account_id"),
            (rand() * 10000).alias("amount")
        )
        
        # Subset of accounts to filter
        filter_accounts = self.spark.range(0, 100).select(
            (col("id") * 100).alias("account_id")
        )
        
        # Traditional approach: Join
        print("\nTraditional join approach:")
        start = time.time()
        result_join = large_dataset.join(
            filter_accounts, 
            "account_id"
        ).select("transaction_id", "amount")
        count_join = result_join.count()
        time_join = time.time() - start
        print(f"Join time: {time_join:.3f}s, Count: {count_join}")
        
        # Bloom filter approach (semi-join)
        print("\nBloom filter (semi-join) approach:")
        start = time.time()
        result_semi = large_dataset.join(
            filter_accounts,
            "account_id",
            "leftsemi"  # More efficient for filtering
        ).select("transaction_id", "amount")
        count_semi = result_semi.count()
        time_semi = time.time() - start
        print(f"Semi-join time: {time_semi:.3f}s, Count: {count_semi}")
        
        # Using IN clause (Spark may use bloom filter internally)
        print("\nIN clause approach:")
        account_list = [row.account_id for row in filter_accounts.collect()]
        start = time.time()
        result_in = large_dataset.filter(
            col("account_id").isin(account_list)
        ).select("transaction_id", "amount")
        count_in = result_in.count()
        time_in = time.time() - start
        print(f"IN clause time: {time_in:.3f}s, Count: {count_in}")
        
        print(f"\nPerformance comparison:")
        print(f"  Join: {time_join:.3f}s (baseline)")
        print(f"  Semi-join: {time_semi:.3f}s ({(1-time_semi/time_join)*100:.1f}% faster)")
        print(f"  IN clause: {time_in:.3f}s ({(1-time_in/time_join)*100:.1f}% faster)")
        
        return result_semi
    
    def vectorized_udf_optimization(self):
        """
        Use Pandas UDF (vectorized) instead of regular UDF
        """
        print("\n=== Advanced: Vectorized UDF Optimization ===")
        
        from pyspark.sql.functions import udf, pandas_udf
        from pyspark.sql.types import DoubleType
        import pandas as pd
        
        # Create test data
        df = self.spark.range(0, 100000).select(
            col("id").cast("double").alias("value")
        )
        
        # Regular Python UDF (slow - row-by-row processing)
        @udf(returnType=DoubleType())
        def complex_calculation_udf(x):
            import math
            return math.sqrt(x) * math.log(x + 1) + math.sin(x)
        
        # Pandas UDF (fast - vectorized processing)
        @pandas_udf(returnType=DoubleType())
        def complex_calculation_pandas_udf(x: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
            import numpy as np
            return np.sqrt(x) * np.log(x + 1) + np.sin(x)
        
        # Test regular UDF
        print("\nTesting regular Python UDF:")
        start = time.time()
        result_udf = df.withColumn(
            "result", 
            complex_calculation_udf(col("value"))
        )
        count_udf = result_udf.count()
        time_udf = time.time() - start
        print(f"Regular UDF time: {time_udf:.3f}s")
        
        # Test Pandas UDF
        print("\nTesting Pandas UDF (vectorized):")
        start = time.time()
        result_pandas = df.withColumn(
            "result",
            complex_calculation_pandas_udf(col("value"))
        )
        count_pandas = result_pandas.count()
        time_pandas = time.time() - start
        print(f"Pandas UDF time: {time_pandas:.3f}s")
        
        speedup = time_udf / time_pandas
        print(f"\nSpeedup: {speedup:.2f}x faster with Pandas UDF")
        
        result_pandas.show(5)
        
        return result_pandas
    
    def data_skipping_optimization(self):
        """
        Use data skipping with min/max statistics
        """
        print("\n=== Advanced: Data Skipping Optimization ===")
        
        # Create partitioned data with clear ranges
        data = []
        for partition in range(10):
            for i in range(10000):
                data.append((
                    partition * 10000 + i,
                    partition,
                    partition * 100 + (i % 100),
                    f"2024-{partition + 1:02d}-01"
                ))
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            data,
            ["id", "partition_id", "value", "date"]
        )
        
        # Write with partitioning
        df.write \
            .partitionBy("partition_id") \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .parquet("/tmp/partitioned_data")
        
        # Query with partition filter - data skipping in action
        print("\nQuerying with partition filter (data skipping):")
        start = time.time()
        
        result = self.spark.read.parquet("/tmp/partitioned_data") \
            .filter(
                (col("partition_id") == 5) &
                (col("value") > 550)
            )
        
        count = result.count()
        exec_time = time.time() - start
        
        print(f"Execution time: {exec_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"Result count: {count}")
        print("\nOnly partition 5 was scanned (9 partitions skipped)")
        
        result.explain(mode="formatted")
        result.show(5)
        
        return result
    
    def whole_stage_codegen_optimization(self):
        """
        Demonstrate whole-stage code generation benefits
        """
        print("\n=== Advanced: Whole-Stage Code Generation ===")
        
        # Create data
        df = self.spark.range(0, 1000000).select(
            col("id"),
            (col("id") % 100).alias("key"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("value1"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("value2")
        )
        
        # Complex query that benefits from code generation
        result = df.filter(col("value1") > 500) \
            .filter(col("value2") < 800) \
            .select(
                col("key"),
                (col("value1") + col("value2")).alias("sum"),
                (col("value1") * col("value2")).alias("product"),
                when(col("value1") > col("value2"), lit("A"))
                    .otherwise(lit("B")).alias("category")
            ) \
            .groupBy("key", "category") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                avg("sum").alias("avg_sum"),
                max("product").alias("max_product")
            )
        
        print("\nQuery with whole-stage code generation:")
        result.explain(mode="formatted")
        
        # Look for "WholeStageCodegen" in the plan
        print("\nNote: Look for '*WholeStageCodegen*' in the plan above")
        print("This indicates multiple operators fused into single Java code")
        
        start = time.time()
        count = result.count()
        exec_time = time.time() - start
        
        print(f"\nExecution time: {exec_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"Result count: {count}")
        
        result.show(10)
        
        return result

class OptimizationBenchmark:
    """
    Comprehensive benchmarking suite for optimization patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        self.results = []
    
    def benchmark_query(self, name, query_func, iterations=3):
        """
        Benchmark a query with multiple iterations
        """
        print(f"\nBenchmarking: {name}")
        times = []
        
        for i in range(iterations):
            start = time.time()
            result = query_func()
            if hasattr(result, 'count'):
                count = result.count()
            else:
                count = len(result)
            exec_time = time.time() - start
            times.append(exec_time)
            print(f"  Iteration {i+1}: {exec_time:.3f}s")
        
        avg_time = sum(times) / len(times)
        min_time = min(times)
        max_time = max(times)
        
        self.results.append({
            'name': name,
            'avg_time': avg_time,
            'min_time': min_time,
            'max_time': max_time,
            'iterations': iterations
        })
        
        print(f"  Average: {avg_time:.3f}s (min: {min_time:.3f}s, max: {max_time:.3f}s)")
        
        return avg_time
    
    def generate_report(self):
        """
        Generate comprehensive benchmark report
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("OPTIMIZATION BENCHMARK REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        if not self.results:
            print("No benchmark results available")
            return
        
        # Sort by average time
        sorted_results = sorted(self.results, key=lambda x
```python

        print("-" * 80)
        
        for idx, result in enumerate(sorted_results, 1):

class OptimizationBestPractices:
    """
    Collection of best practices and anti-patterns
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_best_practices(spark):
        """
        Show best practices vs anti-patterns
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("OPTIMIZATION BEST PRACTICES")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Create sample data
        df = spark.range(0, 100000).select(
            col("id"),
            (col("id") % 100).alias("category"),
            (rand() * 1000).alias("value")
        )
        
        print("\n1. FILTER EARLY (Predicate Pushdown)")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # ANTI-PATTERN
        print("\n❌ ANTI-PATTERN: Filter after expensive operations")
        print("""
        df.groupBy("category") \\
          .agg(sum("value")) \\
          .filter(col("category") < 10)  # Filter AFTER aggregation
        """)
        
        # BEST PRACTICE
        print("\n✅ BEST PRACTICE: Filter before expensive operations")
        print("""
        df.filter(col("category") < 10) \\  # Filter BEFORE aggregation
          .groupBy("category") \\
          .agg(sum("value"))
        """)
        
        print("\n2. SELECT ONLY NEEDED COLUMNS")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # ANTI-PATTERN
        print("\n❌ ANTI-PATTERN: Select all columns unnecessarily")
        print("""
        df.select("*") \\
          .join(other_df, "id") \\
          .select("id", "value")  # Selected all, used few
        """)
        
        # BEST PRACTICE
        print("\n✅ BEST PRACTICE: Select only required columns early")
        print("""
        df.select("id", "value") \\  # Select early
          .join(other_df.select("id", "name"), "id")
        """)
        
        print("\n3. AVOID EXPENSIVE UDFs")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # ANTI-PATTERN
        print("\n❌ ANTI-PATTERN: Use Python UDF for simple operations")
        print("""
        @udf(returnType=IntegerType())
        def add_one(x):
            return x + 1
        
        df.withColumn("new_value", add_one(col("value")))
        """)
        
        # BEST PRACTICE
        print("\n✅ BEST PRACTICE: Use built-in functions")
        print("""
        df.withColumn("new_value", col("value") + 1)
        """)
        
        print("\n4. CACHE WISELY")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # ANTI-PATTERN
        print("\n❌ ANTI-PATTERN: Cache everything or nothing")
        print("""
        df.cache()  # Cache data used only once
        result = df.filter(col("value") > 500).count()
        """)
        
        # BEST PRACTICE
        print("\n✅ BEST PRACTICE: Cache data reused multiple times")
        print("""
        df_cached = df.filter(col("value") > 500).cache()
        result1 = df_cached.groupBy("category").count()
        result2 = df_cached.agg(avg("value"))
        result3 = df_cached.orderBy("value").limit(10)
        df_cached.unpersist()  # Clean up when done
        """)
        
        print("\n5. PARTITION APPROPRIATELY")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # ANTI-PATTERN
        print("\n❌ ANTI-PATTERN: Too many or too few partitions")
        print("""
        df.repartition(1000)  # Too many for small data
        large_df.coalesce(1)  # Too few for large data
        """)
        
        # BEST PRACTICE
        print("\n✅ BEST PRACTICE: Balance partition count with data size")
        print("""
        # Rule of thumb: 128MB - 1GB per partition
        optimal_partitions = max(data_size_gb * 2, num_cores * 2)
        df.repartition(optimal_partitions)
        """)
        
        print("\n6. USE APPROPRIATE JOIN STRATEGIES")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # ANTI-PATTERN
        print("\n❌ ANTI-PATTERN: Large table joins without hints")
        print("""
        large_df1.join(large_df2, "id")  # May cause shuffle
        """)
        
        # BEST PRACTICE
        print("\n✅ BEST PRACTICE: Use broadcast for small tables")
        print("""
        from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
        large_df.join(broadcast(small_df), "id")
        """)
        
        print("\n7. AVOID COLLECT ON LARGE DATA")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # ANTI-PATTERN
        print("\n❌ ANTI-PATTERN: Collect large datasets to driver")
        print("""
        all_data = large_df.collect()  # OOM risk!
        for row in all_data:
            process(row)
        """)
        
        # BEST PRACTICE
        print("\n✅ BEST PRACTICE: Process data in distributed manner")
        print("""
        large_df.foreach(lambda row: process(row))
        # Or use mapPartitions for batch processing
        """)
        
        print("\n8. LEVERAGE PARTITIONING FOR FILTERS")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # ANTI-PATTERN
        print("\n❌ ANTI-PATTERN: Don't use partition columns in filters")
        print("""
        df.write.partitionBy("date").parquet("path")
        # Later...
        spark.read.parquet("path").filter(col("value") > 100)
        """)
        
        # BEST PRACTICE
        print("\n✅ BEST PRACTICE: Filter on partition columns")
        print("""
        spark.read.parquet("path") \\
          .filter(col("date") == "2024-01-01")  # Partition pruning!
        """)
        
        print("\n9. USE DATAFRAME API OVER RDD")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # ANTI-PATTERN
        print("\n❌ ANTI-PATTERN: Use RDD for structured data")
        print("""
        rdd = df.rdd.map(lambda row: (row.id, row.value * 2))
        """)
        
        # BEST PRACTICE
        print("\n✅ BEST PRACTICE: Use DataFrame API with Catalyst optimizer")
        print("""
        df.select(col("id"), (col("value") * 2).alias("doubled"))
        """)
        
        print("\n10. ANALYZE AND USE STATISTICS")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # ANTI-PATTERN
        print("\n❌ ANTI-PATTERN: Skip statistics collection")
        print("""
        df.write.saveAsTable("table")
        # No statistics collected
        """)
        
        # BEST PRACTICE
        print("\n✅ BEST PRACTICE: Collect statistics for CBO")
        print("""
        df.write.saveAsTable("table")
        spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE table COMPUTE STATISTICS")
        spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE table COMPUTE STATISTICS FOR COLUMNS col1, col2")
        """)
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)

# TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE

class OptimizationTroubleshooting:
    """
    Common performance issues and solutions
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_troubleshooting_guide():
        """
        Print troubleshooting guide for common issues
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("PERFORMANCE TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        issues = {
            "1. Out of Memory (OOM) Errors": {
                "symptoms": [
                    "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError",
                    "Container killed by YARN",
                    "Executor lost"
                ],
                "causes": [
                    "Insufficient executor memory",
                    "Data skew causing single partition to be too large",
                    "Too many partitions in memory (cache/broadcast)",
                    "Large collect() operations"
                ],
                "solutions": [
                    "Increase executor memory: spark.executor.memory",
                    "Increase memory fraction: spark.memory.fraction",
                    "Enable spill to disk: spark.memory.offHeap.enabled",
                    "Repartition data to handle skew",
                    "Avoid collect() on large datasets",
                    "Use coalesce() to reduce partitions before cache"
                ],
                "code_example": """
# Increase memory
spark.conf.set("spark.executor.memory", "16g")
spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", "0.8")

# Handle skew
df_repartitioned = df.repartition(400, "skewed_column")

# Avoid collect
# BAD: data = df.collect()
# GOOD: df.write.parquet("output")
                """
            },
            
            "2. Slow Shuffle Operations": {
                "symptoms": [
                    "Long shuffle read/write times in Spark UI",
                    "Many small shuffle files",
                    "High network traffic"
                ],
                "causes": [
                    "Too many shuffle partitions",
                    "Unoptimized join strategy",
                    "No partition pruning",
                    "Data skew"
                ],
                "solutions": [
                    "Adjust shuffle partitions",
                    "Enable AQE for dynamic optimization",
                    "Use broadcast joins for small tables",
                    "Partition data appropriately",
                    "Enable shuffle compression"
                ],
                "code_example": """
# Optimize shuffle partitions
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")

# Use broadcast join
from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
result = large_df.join(broadcast(small_df), "key")

# Enable compression
spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.compress", "true")
                """
            },
            
            "3. Data Skew Issues": {
                "symptoms": [
                    "Few tasks taking much longer than others",
                    "Uneven partition sizes",
                    "Some executors idle while others busy"
                ],
                "causes": [
                    "Uneven data distribution",
                    "Hot keys in joins/aggregations",
                    "Poor partitioning strategy"
                ],
                "solutions": [
                    "Enable AQE skew join handling",
                    "Use salting technique for hot keys",
                    "Repartition with multiple columns",
                    "Filter out null keys if appropriate"
                ],
                "code_example": """
# Enable skew join handling
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.skewedPartitionThresholdInBytes", "256MB")

# Salting technique for skewed keys
from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, concat, lit

df_salted = df.withColumn("salt", (rand() * 10).cast("int"))
df_salted = df_salted.withColumn("salted_key", concat(col("key"), lit("_"), col("salt")))

# Repartition with multiple columns
df_balanced = df.repartition(200, "col1", "col2")
                """
            },
            
            "4. Slow File Reads": {
                "symptoms": [
                    "Long time in scan operations",
                    "Reading unnecessary data",
                    "Many small files"
                ],
                "causes": [
                    "No partition pruning",
                    "Small file problem",
                    "Inefficient file format",
                    "No predicate pushdown"
                ],
                "solutions": [
                    "Use columnar formats (Parquet, ORC)",
                    "Partition data appropriately",
                    "Compact small files",
                    "Use partition filters",
                    "Collect statistics"
                ],
                "code_example": """
# Write with partitioning
df.write.partitionBy("date", "region").parquet("output")

# Read with partition filter (predicate pushdown)
df = spark.read.parquet("output").filter(col("date") == "2024-01-01")

# Compact small files
df.coalesce(10).write.parquet("compacted_output")

# Use columnar format
df.write.format("parquet").save("output")  # Better than CSV
                """
            },
            
            "5. Inefficient Joins": {
                "symptoms": [
                    "Long join execution time",
                    "Excessive shuffling",
                    "Cross joins appearing in plan"
                ],
                "causes": [
                    "Missing join conditions",
                    "Wrong join strategy",
                    "No statistics for CBO",
                    "Cartesian products"
                ],
                "solutions": [
                    "Always specify join conditions",
                    "Use broadcast for small tables",
                    "Collect statistics",
                    "Use appropriate join type",
                    "Pre-filter data before join"
                ],
                "code_example": """
# Collect statistics
spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE table1 COMPUTE STATISTICS")
spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE table2 COMPUTE STATISTICS")

# Use broadcast hint
result = large_df.join(broadcast(small_df), "key")

# Filter before join
filtered_df1 = df1.filter(col("date") >= "2024-01-01")
filtered_df2 = df2.filter(col("active") == True)
result = filtered_df1.join(filtered_df2, "key")

# Avoid cartesian product
# BAD: df1.join(df2)  # No condition!
# GOOD: df1.join(df2, "key")
                """
            },
            
            "6. Excessive GC (Garbage Collection)": {
                "symptoms": [
                    "High GC time in executor metrics",
                    "Frequent GC pauses",
                    "Slow task execution"
                ],
                "causes": [
                    "Insufficient memory",
                    "Too many objects created",
                    "Memory leaks",
                    "Inefficient serialization"
                ],
                "solutions": [
                    "Increase executor memory",
                    "Use Kryo serialization",
                    "Reduce object creation in UDFs",
                    "Tune GC settings",
                    "Use primitive types where possible"
                ],
                "code_example": """
# Enable Kryo serialization
spark.conf.set("spark.serializer", "org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer")

# Increase memory
spark.conf.set("spark.executor.memory", "16g")
spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", "0.8")

# Tune GC
spark.conf.set("spark.executor.extraJavaOptions", 
               "-XX:+UseG1GC -XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=35")

# Use primitive types
# BAD: df.select(col("value").cast("string"))
# GOOD: df.select(col("value"))  # Keep as numeric
                """
            },
            
            "7. Spill to Disk Issues": {
                "symptoms": [
                    "High spill metrics in Spark UI",
                    "Slow shuffle operations",
                    "Disk I/O bottleneck"
                ],
                "causes": [
                    "Insufficient memory for operations",
                    "Large aggregations",
                    "Memory-intensive UDFs"
                ],
                "solutions": [
                    "Increase executor memory",
                    "Increase memory fraction",
                    "Reduce partition count",
                    "Use incremental aggregations",
                    "Enable compression for spills"
                ],
                "code_example": """
# Increase memory for execution
spark.conf.set("spark.executor.memory", "20g")
spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", "0.8")

# Enable spill compression
spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.spill.compress", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.compress", "true")

# Reduce memory pressure
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "100")  # Fewer, larger partitions
                """
            }
        }
        
        for issue, details in issues.items():
            print(f"\n{issue}")
            print("=" * 80)
            
            print("\nSymptoms:")
            for symptom in details["symptoms"]:
                print(f"  • {symptom}")
            
            print("\nCauses:")
            for cause in details["causes"]:
                print(f"  • {cause}")
            
            print("\nSolutions:")
            for solution in details["solutions"]:
                print(f"  • {solution}")
            
            print("\nCode Example:")
            print(details["code_example"])
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)

╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    OPTIMIZATION PATTERNS SUMMARY                           ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

1. RULE-BASED OPTIMIZATION (RBO)
   ✓ Predicate Pushdown: Move filters close to data source
   ✓ Column Pruning: Read only required columns
   ✓ Constant Folding: Evaluate constants at compile time
   ✓ Join Reordering: Optimize join sequence automatically
   
   Impact: 30-50% performance improvement on I/O-bound queries

2. COST-BASED OPTIMIZATION (CBO)
   ✓ Statistics Collection: Gather table and column statistics
   ✓ Cardinality Estimation: Better query planning
   ✓ Join Strategy Selection: Choose optimal join algorithm
   ✓ Broadcast Optimization: Automatic small table broadcasting
   
   Impact: 40-70% improvement on join-heavy workloads
   
   Action Required: ANALYZE TABLE commands for statistics

3. ADAPTIVE QUERY EXECUTION (AQE)
   ✓ Dynamic Partition Coalescing: Reduce shuffle partitions at runtime
   ✓ Skew Join Handling: Automatically detect and handle data skew
   ✓ Join Strategy Switching: Change join strategy based on runtime stats
   ✓ Local Shuffle Reader: Optimize shuffle for better locality
   
   Impact: 20-60% improvement, especially with skewed data
   
   Configuration: spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=true (default in Spark 3.2+)

4. RUNTIME OPTIMIZATION
   ✓ Dynamic Resource Allocation: Scale executors based on workload
   ✓ Intelligent Caching: Cache frequently accessed data
   ✓ Partition Optimization: Balance data distribution
   ✓ Execution Monitoring: Track and optimize based on metrics
   
   Impact: 25-50% improvement through resource efficiency

5. FEEDBACK-BASED OPTIMIZATION
   ✓ Configuration Tuning: Learn from execution history
   ✓ Query Rewriting: Optimize based on performance patterns
   ✓ Historical Statistics: Use past performance data
   ✓ Iterative Improvement: Continuous optimization loop
   
   Impact: 15-40% improvement over time through learning

6. ADVANCED TECHNIQUES
   ✓ Bucketing: Pre-shuffle data for join optimization
   ✓ Z-Ordering: Optimize data layout for multi-dimensional queries
   ✓ Bloom Filters: Efficient filtering with minimal overhead
   ✓ Vectorized UDFs: 10-100x faster than regular Python UDFs
   ✓ Data Skipping: Partition pruning and min/max statistics
   ✓ Whole-Stage Codegen: Fuse operators into optimized Java code
   
   Impact: 50-200% improvement for specific use cases

╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                         QUICK WINS CHECKLIST                               ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

□ Enable Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)
  spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")

□ Enable Cost-Based Optimization (CBO) with statistics
  spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE your_table COMPUTE STATISTICS")

□ Use appropriate file formats (Parquet/ORC over CSV/JSON)
  df.write.format("parquet").save("path")

□ Partition data logically
  df.write.partitionBy("date", "region").parquet("path")

□ Cache reused DataFrames
  df.cache() when using multiple times

□ Use broadcast joins for small tables
  from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
  large_df.join(broadcast(small_df), "key")

□ Adjust shuffle partitions based on data size
  spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")

□ Filter early in your query pipeline
  df.filter(...).groupBy(...) not df.groupBy(...).filter(...)

□ Use built-in functions instead of UDFs
  col("value") + 1 instead of udf(lambda x: x + 1)

□ Monitor and tune based on Spark UI metrics
  Check shuffle read/write, GC time, task duration

╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                      PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION WORKFLOW                     ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

1. MEASURE BASELINE
   - Run query and capture metrics
   - Check Spark UI for bottlenecks
   - Identify slow stages

2. ANALYZE BOTTLENECKS
   - High shuffle? → Reduce partitions or use broadcast
   - Data skew? → Enable AQE skew handling or use salting
   - Slow I/O? → Use columnar format, partition pruning
   - High GC? → Increase memory, use Kryo serialization

3. APPLY OPTIMIZATIONS
   - Start with quick wins (AQE, CBO, caching)
   - Apply targeted optimizations for specific issues
   - Use appropriate data structures and formats

4. MEASURE IMPROVEMENT
   - Re-run with optimizations
   - Compare metrics
   - Validate results are correct

5. ITERATE
   - Continue optimizing based on new bottlenecks
   - Document learnings for future queries
   - Establish best practices for your workload

╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                         CONFIGURATION CHEAT SHEET                          ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

SMALL DATA (<1GB):
  spark.sql.shuffle.partitions = 50
  spark.executor.memory = 4g

MEDIUM DATA (1-100GB):
  spark.sql.shuffle.partitions = 200
  spark.executor.memory = 8g
  spark.sql.adaptive.enabled = true

LARGE DATA (>100GB):
  spark.sql.shuffle.partitions = 400+
  spark.executor.memory = 16g
  spark.sql.adaptive.enabled = true
  spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled = true
  spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled = true

JOIN-HEAVY:
  spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold = 50MB
  spark.sql.cbo.enabled = true
  spark.sql.adaptive.enabled = true

AGGREGATION-HEAVY:
  spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled = true
  spark.memory.fraction = 0.75
  spark.shuffle.compress = true

╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                           MONITORING METRICS                               ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

Key Metrics to Watch:
  • Task Duration: Should be balanced (no stragglers)
  • Shuffle Read/Write: Minimize unnecessary shuffles
  • GC Time: Should be <10% of task time
  • Spill (Memory/Disk): Minimize or eliminate
  • Data Skew: Partition sizes should be balanced
  • Cache Hit Rate: High for cached data

Red Flags:
  ⚠ Tasks with 10x+ longer duration than median
  ⚠ GC time >20% of execution time
  ⚠ Large amount of spill to disk
  ⚠ Many small shuffle files (<1MB each)
  ⚠ OOM errors or executor failures
  ⚠ Cross joins in execution plan

def quick_performance_test(spark=None):
    """
    Quick performance test to validate optimizations
    """
    if spark is None:
        spark = create_optimized_spark_session("quick_test")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("QUICK PERFORMANCE TEST")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create test data
    print("\nCreating test dataset (1M rows)...")
    df = spark.range(0, 1000000).select(
        col("id"),
        (col("id") % 100).alias("category"),
        (rand() * 1000).alias("value1"),
        (rand() * 1000).alias("value2")
    )
    
    # Test 1: Basic aggregation
    print("\nTest 1: Basic Aggregation")
    start = time.time()
    result1 = df.groupBy("category").agg(
        count("*").alias("count"),
        avg("value1").alias("avg_value")
    ).collect()
    time1 = time.time() - start
    print(f"Time: {time1:.3f}s")
    
    # Test 2: With caching
    print("\nTest 2: Aggregation with Caching")
    df_cached = df.cache()
    df_cached.count()  # Materialize cache
    
    start = time.time()
    result2 = df_cached.groupBy("category").agg(
        count("*").alias("count"),
        avg("value1").alias("avg_value")
    ).collect()
    time2 = time.time() - start
    print(f"Time: {time2:.3f}s")
    print(f"Improvement: {((time1-time2)/time1*100):.1f}%")
    
    # Test 3: Complex query
    print("\nTest 3: Complex Query")
    start = time.time()
    result3 = df_cached.filter(col("value1") > 500) \
        .groupBy("category") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            sum("value2").alias("sum_value"),
            avg("value2").alias("avg_value")
        ) \
        .filter(col("count") > 1000) \
        .orderBy(desc("sum_value")) \
        .limit(10) \
        .collect()
    time3 = time.time() - start
    print(f"Time: {time3:.3f}s")
    
    df_cached.unpersist()
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("Quick test completed!")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    if spark is None:
        spark.stop()

def analyze_query_plan(df, query_name="Query"):
    """
    Analyze and print detailed query plan information
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"Query Plan Analysis: {query_name}")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    print("\n1. Logical Plan (Unresolved):")
    print("-" * 80)
    df.explain(extended=False)
    
    print("\n2. Optimized Logical Plan:")
    print("-" * 80)
    df.explain(mode="simple")
    
    print("\n3. Physical Plan:")
    print("-" * 80)
    df.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    print("\n4. Cost-Based Plan (if available):")
    print("-" * 80)
    try:
        df.explain(mode="cost")
    except:
        print("Cost-based plan not available")
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}\n")


def compare_query_plans(df1, df2, name1="Query 1", name2="Query 2"):
    """
    Compare two query plans side by side
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"Query Plan Comparison: {name1} vs {name2}")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    print(f"\n{name1} Plan:")
    print("-" * 80)
    df1.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    print(f"\n{name2} Plan:")
    print("-" * 80)
    df2.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}\n")


def get_optimization_recommendations(spark, df):
    """
    Analyze DataFrame and provide optimization recommendations
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("OPTIMIZATION RECOMMENDATIONS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    recommendations = []
    
    # Check partition count
    num_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    print(f"\nCurrent partitions: {num_partitions}")
    
    if num_partitions > 1000:
        recommendations.append({
            'priority': 'HIGH',
            'issue': 'Too many partitions',
            'recommendation': f'Consider reducing partitions to 200-400',
            'code': f'df = df.coalesce({min(400, num_partitions // 2)})'
        })
    elif num_partitions < 10:
        recommendations.append({
            'priority': 'MEDIUM',
            'issue': 'Too few partitions',
            'recommendation': 'Consider increasing partitions for better parallelism',
            'code': f'df = df.repartition({max(50, num_partitions * 4)})'
        })
    
    # Check if AQE is enabled
    aqe_enabled = spark.conf.get("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "false")
    if aqe_enabled.lower() == "false":
        recommendations.append({
            'priority': 'HIGH',
            'issue': 'Adaptive Query Execution disabled',
            'recommendation': 'Enable AQE for automatic runtime optimizations',
            'code': 'spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")'
        })
    
    # Check if CBO is enabled
    cbo_enabled = spark.conf.get("spark.sql.cbo.enabled", "false")
    if cbo_enabled.lower() == "false":
        recommendations.append({
            'priority': 'MEDIUM',
            'issue': 'Cost-Based Optimization disabled',
            'recommendation': 'Enable CBO and collect statistics for better query planning',
            'code': 'spark.conf.set("spark.sql.cbo.enabled", "true")'
        })
    
    # Check shuffle partitions
    shuffle_partitions = int(spark.conf.get("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200"))
    if shuffle_partitions == 200:
        recommendations.append({
            'priority': 'LOW',
            'issue': 'Using default shuffle partitions',
            'recommendation': 'Tune shuffle partitions based on your data size',
            'code': 'spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "400")  # Adjust as needed'
        })
    
    # Print recommendations
    if recommendations:
        print("\nRecommendations found:")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        for idx, rec in enumerate(recommendations, 1):
            print(f"\n{idx}. [{rec['priority']}] {rec['issue']}")
            print(f"   Recommendation: {rec['recommendation']}")
            print(f"   Code: {rec['code']}")
    else:
        print("\n✓ No major optimization issues found!")
        print("  Your configuration looks good.")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    
    return recommendations


def export_optimization_report(spark, output_path="optimization_report.txt"):
    """
    Export comprehensive optimization report to file
    """
    import datetime
    
    with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
        f.write("=" * 80 + "\n")
        f.write("SPARK OPTIMIZATION REPORT\n")
        f.write(f"Generated: {datetime.datetime.now()}\n")
        f.write("=" * 80 + "\n\n")
        
        # Spark Configuration
        f.write("CURRENT SPARK CONFIGURATION\n")
        f.write("-" * 80 + "\n")
        
        important_configs = [
            "spark.sql.adaptive.enabled",
            "spark.sql.cbo.enabled",
            "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions",
            "spark.executor.memory",
            "spark.executor.cores",
            "spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold",
            "spark.memory.fraction",
            "spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled"
        ]
        
        for config in important_configs:
            try:
                value = spark.conf.get(config, "NOT SET")
                f.write(f"{config}: {value}\n")
            except:
                f.write(f"{config}: ERROR READING\n")
        
        f.write("\n" + "=" * 80 + "\n")
        f.write("END OF REPORT\n")
        f.write("=" * 80 + "\n")
    
    print(f"\n✓ Optimization report exported to: {output_path}")

"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple, Optional
import logging
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s'

# 1. OFFLINE MIGRATION PATTERN
# ============================================================================
class OfflineMigrationPattern:
    """
    Offline Migration Pattern
    -------------------------
    Migrates data during a maintenance window when the source system is offline.
    Best for: Systems that can tolerate downtime, complete data consistency required.
    
    Characteristics:
    - Source system is taken offline
    - Full data migration in one operation
    - No concurrent access issues
    - Simpler implementation
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(self.__class__.__name__)
    
    def migrate_full_dataset(
        self,
        source_path: str,
        target_path: str,
        source_format: str = "parquet",
        target_format: str = "delta",
        partition_columns: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        validation_enabled: bool = True
    ) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """
        Performs complete offline migration of dataset.
        
        Args:
            source_path: Path to source data
            target_path: Path to target location
            source_format: Source data format
            target_format: Target data format
            partition_columns: Columns to partition by
            validation_enabled: Enable post-migration validation
            
        Returns:
            Migration statistics and status
        """
        self.logger.info("Starting offline migration...")
        start_time = datetime.now()
        
        try:
            # Step 1: Read source data
            self.logger.info(f"Reading source data from {source_path}")
            source_df = self.spark.read.format(source_format).load(source_path)
            source_count = source_df.count()
            
            # Step 2: Add migration metadata
            migrated_df = source_df.withColumn(
                "migration_timestamp", 
                lit(current_timestamp())
            ).withColumn(
                "migration_batch_id",
                lit(start_time.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"))
            )
            
            # Step 3: Write to target
            self.logger.info(f"Writing data to target {target_path}")
            writer = migrated_df.write.format(target_format).mode("overwrite")
            
            if partition_columns:
                writer = writer.partitionBy(*partition_columns)
            
            writer.save(target_path)
            
            # Step 4: Validation
            validation_result = {}
            if validation_enabled:
                validation_result = self._validate_migration(
                    source_df, 
                    target_path, 
                    target_format
                )
            
            end_time = datetime.now()
            duration = (end_time - start_time).total_seconds()
            
            return {
                "status": "SUCCESS",
                "source_count": source_count,
                "duration_seconds": duration,
                "migration_timestamp": start_time,
                "validation": validation_result
            }
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.error(f"Migration failed: {str(e)}")
            return {
                "status": "FAILED",
                "error": str(e),
                "migration_timestamp": start_time
            }
    
    def _validate_migration(
        self, 
        source_df: DataFrame, 
        target_path: str, 
        target_format: str
    ) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """Validates migrated data against source."""
        self.logger.info("Validating migration...")
        
        target_df = self.spark.read.format(target_format).load(target_path)
        
        source_count = source_df.count()
        target_count = target_df.count()
        
        # Remove migration metadata columns for comparison
        target_df_clean = target_df.drop("migration_timestamp", "migration_batch_id")
        
        return {
            "source_count": source_count,
            "target_count": target_count,
            "count_match": source_count == target_count,
            "schema_match": source_df.schema == target_df_clean.schema
        }

# 2. ONLINE MIGRATION PATTERN
# ============================================================================
class OnlineMigrationPattern:
    """
    Online Migration Pattern
    ------------------------
    Migrates data while the source system remains operational.
    Best for: Zero-downtime requirements, gradual migration.
    
    Characteristics:
    - Source system remains online
    - Incremental data migration
    - Change Data Capture (CDC) integration
    - Eventual consistency
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(self.__class__.__name__)
    
    def migrate_incremental(
        self,
        source_path: str,
        target_path: str,
        checkpoint_path: str,
        watermark_column: str,
        last_watermark: Optional[str] = None,
        batch_size: int = 100000
    ) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """
        Performs incremental online migration.
        
        Args:
            source_path: Path to source data
            target_path: Path to target location
            checkpoint_path: Path to store migration checkpoints
            watermark_column: Column to track progress (e.g., timestamp)
            last_watermark: Last processed watermark value
            batch_size: Number of records per batch
            
        Returns:
            Migration statistics
        """
        self.logger.info("Starting online incremental migration...")
        
        try:
            # Read source data
            source_df = self.spark.read.parquet(source_path)
            
            # Filter for new/changed records
            if last_watermark:
                incremental_df = source_df.filter(
                    col(watermark_column) > last_watermark
                )
            else:
                incremental_df = source_df
            
            # Add migration tracking
            migrated_df = incremental_df.withColumn(
                "migration_timestamp",
                current_timestamp()
            ).withColumn(
                "migration_type",
                lit("ONLINE_INCREMENTAL")
            )
            
            # Process in batches to avoid overwhelming target
            total_records = migrated_df.count()
            self.logger.info(f"Processing {total_records} records")
            
            # Write incrementally with append mode
            migrated_df.write \
                .format("delta") \
                .mode("append") \
                .save(target_path)
            
            # Update checkpoint
            new_watermark = migrated_df.agg(
                max(watermark_column).alias("max_watermark")
            ).collect()[0]["max_watermark"]
            
            self._update_checkpoint(checkpoint_path, new_watermark)
            
            return {
                "status": "SUCCESS",
                "records_migrated": total_records,
                "new_watermark": str(new_watermark),
                "migration_type": "ONLINE_INCREMENTAL"
            }
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.logger.error(f"Online migration failed: {str(e)}")
            return {
                "status": "FAILED",
                "error": str(e)
            }
    
    def _update_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_path: str, watermark: any):
        """Updates migration checkpoint."""
        checkpoint_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            [(str(watermark), datetime.now())],
            ["watermark", "timestamp"]
        )
        checkpoint_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(checkpoint_path)
